analysis.name: Ainash Childebayeva
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This was definitely one of the harder anthropology classes, especially bc I had no genetics background. She lectures very quickly, & I got points off for unimportant stuff, but she's knowledgeable. You can tell she cares more about her research than teaching. Admirable professor but not an easy class - check prior syllabi before registering.

had her for INB-337. All she does is read off the slides, no emotion, no care, nothing interesting in teaching style. She's showed up late to her own class so many times. As of right now she's been late more than on time. Class is boring and she's intentionally vague on assignments.

I had her for a different class than the one I had listed here. But the points still remains that she is not really capable of teaching and has a huge ego and I guess the department is making her teach some other classes for the fall.

Lots of reading (~2 scientific papers by the start of each class). Lectures were often too fast to make time for class discussion and student lectures which were unproductive in my opinion. Very disorganized, most assignments had no rubric or clear guidelines and instructions would be changed at the last minute. Was hard to discern what she wanted.

The courseload was very heavy, office hours were often cancelled. Had to read 2 scientific research papers and a textbook chapter by every class, had a 5,000-word research paper due at end of the semester and 2 exams worth 30% of the grade. Found it hard to keep up with slides in lecture due to the speed of her lectures and lack of explaining.

analysis.name: Aurora Wallace
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's a new professor at UT but friendly. Lectures are straightforward. Homeworks are short. She offers plenty of support if you're confused. Participation work is required on Mondays, but she gives makeups for it. Exams closely follow the practice materials and HW, though they can get tricky—especially the final. Highly recommend!

Really great experience taking her for Probability 1. Explains everything very clearly and tests are pretty easy as long as you are familiar with the material. Gives a lot of really good prep material for the tests too.

Best math teacher I've ever had. I took her for calc one and for lectures you would read the textbook before class and then complete a really short online assignment. The weekly homework load was very manageable. subject was explained very well and always answered questions.

The course content itself is incredibly easy. If you get stuck, she is very helpful over email/office hours. I did very well on the HWs and midterms, but I just barely got an A bc of the final, which is weighted 30%. In-class activities once a week for a participation grade. Handwriting is a bit difficult to read at times.
Really great and caring professor. Good lecturer as well, although attendance wasn't mandatory — take if you can.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Adams
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class is a simple but engaging VAPA that Dr. Adams structured to be easy. The class is beyond manageable and has little to no workload as long as you pay attention to the lectures, do the readings, and study a bit for the weekly quizzes. There were no exams in the class, and instead of a final, there is a fun final project. Highly Recommended!

I'd die for Lizzy. If you didnt like her you probably thought you could get away with doing nothing, which is just plain lazy and you only have yourself to blame. Loved her lectures, she's so funny. Have to buy tophat for attendance. No tests, just weekly quizzes with 2 drops and a final project. Loved this class so much, it was really interesting.

Dr. Adams is a great lecturer, but it's the lengthy daily readings that made me dread going to this class, as well as the weekly quizzes.  You truly will learn a lot, but unless you like learning out of an online textbook and then going and being talked at about it, I don't recommend.  If you're looking for an easy a though, take her Rome class.

I fell ill and had to drop.  The nature of the course is fast paced but I love the way she has the course structured and once I understood the flow it got so much easier.  It takes time to learn another language but the way she teaches does make it really fun. I plan to take her class again.

One of my favorite classes I've taken at UT I'm a classics minor but I feel like even if you don't know anything about classics it's very accessible. Dr. Adams pairs the readings and movies so well and it is just such an interesting class. I'm also not a big horror movie person but still loved it, definitely recommend. Also not too much work!

analysis.name: Michael Aubrey
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I don't think Dr. Aubrey should be teaching Gen Chem 2. His quizzes are hard and you can't study for them because he puts a harder version of the example that you have never seen, he makes mistakes that have to be corrected by students. He doesn't explain things during lecture and expects us to know a lot (we are 2nd semester first-year students).

He does seem very sweet, and I can tell he's trying, but for the portion I was there for (electrochemistry) I genuinely never had any clue what was going on during class. I felt like he was just saying things, but I could never follow the lecture. I did manage to do well on the first exam somehow, but honestly try for another professor if possible.

Really sweet guy, but like other reviews said he kind of struggles with lecturing in a clear, easy-to-understand way if you don't already know the subject material. It's clear he knows a lot about what he's teaching, but you'll definitely need to study outside of class. Overall a pretty average class experience.

This class is recommended for the chemistry major/honors track and so most of us thought we had to take it, but you do not have to! Dr. Aubrey is one of those guys that are just way too smart to be teaching intro to gen chem. Because he is so smart he does not explain nor teach very well. He is not a good teacher, but he is nice, I don't recommend.

Lectures are hard to follow and are frequently focused on interesting but ultimately irrelevant applications or details of course content, making tests and quizzes very difficult. The textbooks are the best way to learn the test/quiz relevant material. He's kind and clearly very knowledgeable about the content, but doesn't convey it well.

analysis.name: Kristen Adams
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I went back here to say that I am so glad Im taking other BME professors rn that are genuinely qualified to teach at this level and material. After going through several of her classes, I almost lost faith in pursuing BME. She dropped my grade by a letter grade for not taking an instapoll during an exam I literally took and directly handed to her.

She cares way more about Instapolls (which she takes even during exam days), than showing your mastery of the material. Wish she just had a sign-in sheet. Lecturing style is monotone with slow pacing; shows no enthusiasm in the material. You'll learn way more from watching CPPMechEngTutorials, who saved me during the heat transfer unit.

Instructor is condescending in Office Hours. TA never shows up to Office hours. LA was very helpful tho so go to them for help. Heat transfer is pretty difficult and instructor struggles with teaching it because of staffing issues so be prepared. 1 exam is dropped so try to do well for them and don't take final exam unless you have to.

Even when I was physically in class and completed Instapoll, I was marked “absent” because I had not taken the optional bonus quiz. No clear communication, policies that were not detailed in the syllabus were suddenly enforced later. One additional absence results in a 10% drop from your overall grade. Grade dropped from A to B.

Professor has a very disorganized style of teaching. Very difficult to follow. Never solved problems fully in class, claiming that she would mess up on the math (which ig she did anyways). Never paid attention to her in class because its frankly a waste of time. I recommend watching Dr. John Biddle's lectures on youtube.

analysis.name: Maria Arredondo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Arredondo is the most kind and caring professor I have had throughout my time at UT. You can tell she truly cares about her students and has compassion for them as human beings! Her classes are easy and you actually learn useful things! Her lectures are engaging, lots of videos and activities! So fun! Take her classes!

Dr. Arredondo is incredibly kind and her lectures and tests are extremely easy and somewhat common sense. Her powerpoints are super easy to understand and help a lot with the tests. The grading distribution is very fair and you will without a doubt get an A, highly recommend her class!!

I had her this semester and I was scared because she had little reviews. However, she was so so sweet and literally will help you with anything. Super approachable as well. I didn't pay attention in class also 6 free absences and I studied the day or two before the exams and I did well on the exams. Memorization based exams mostly. Just take her!

I loved this class, the lectures were very interesting and interactive. The content wasn't hard to follow, very straightforward. Studied on the day of the exams and made an A on all of them. Just do your work and pay attention and you'll be fine.

I love Dr. Arredondo! The class is easy - just common sense with some extra detail.   All of the assignments had clear-cut grading criteria; if you ever have trouble, she and her TA were very helpful. Exams were simple as well, Quizlet was great for studying. Readings were assigned but I rarely did them.

analysis.name: Ashley Green
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's passionate and very well-versed in conservation, but in turn means she's a harsh grader. Will take off points for grammar, formatting, punctuation, etc. Also a very slow grader; did not start receiving grades til the start of March (mid-sem). Expect to do a homework assignment due before every class. Exams are FRQ heavy.

this course felt like so much work. Always hard to find big project assignment instructions on canvas. disorganized. Very harsh grader. Curriculum is very interesting! Good lecturer, not much class interaction.

I genuinely struggled trying to get myself to show up to this class. I was excited to take ecology but it was nothing like I expected. She didn't give us anything to prepare for exams. This class was so much harder than it needed to be & very unorganized. It was disheartening because I've heard other 373 classes are so much easier. Not an easy A

She knows her stuff and loves her field, but she does not know how to teach. The entire class is her lecturing at students, making it difficult to stay engaged. Students often slept while she lectured lol. Three exams and no drops, so if you bomb the first exam (our class average was a 69!), there's no way of getting an A. Very discouraging.

Class was interesting honestly. It felt like she was learning content for the first time with us, and honestly lots of what was on the slides was very surface-level. Exams were odd, and she refuses to give practice problems otherwise she's "giving us the answers". Not the worst professor ever, but I expected better.

analysis.name: Alex Macedo
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: LITERALLY THE GOAT! Didn't show up to class for a whole month or two but still end up with an A. The exam is basically what is covered during exam review session, and final is not cumulative. 3 quizzes drops, 2-4 HW drops. THIS IS FOR M 427L.

This man is NOT accessible outside of class, doesn't answer emails, and isn't clear in his lectures. He rambles about easy concepts and speeds through the difficult stuff. His exams are only 3 q's. If you take this class DON'T FORGET THE QUEST HW he won't mention it in class or put it on Canvas. The material itself seems easy, he makes it hard.

DO NOT TAKE if no experience in calc. 2 exams, 3 questions each all purely based on bad lectures. notes and lectures not posted, does not respond to emails, must rely on your own notes to study. discussion and HW not what is related to exams. there are better calc teachers. avoid or get ready to get a C for getting 1 question on the exam wrong.

Horrible teaching style, boring lectures, and unclear grading. Grades everything last minute so you don't know your actual standing until the end of the semester. Class time with the TA every other day gets you nowhere-- it's all busy work with a group you're randomly assigned to and nobody pulls any weight.

Macedo requires you to solve the questions in his own way which can be really annoying for tests. I struggled with Calculus and did not find the lectures that helpful. Most people generally get good grades but the instruction was not great.

analysis.name: Avi Blitz
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Blitz is one of the best professors I've ever had, hands down. He will go out of his way to help you, and he cares tremendously for his students. Loved the atmosphere of his class. I am shocked to see that others claim to have not liked his class: I have a feeling they weren't expecting Hebrew to be so difficult. Take him, you'll learn so much!

Avi is an absolute GEM of a professor. His classroom feels like home. He's so kind and welcoming, and he TAILORS THE CLASS MATERIAL TO THE CLASS based on our interests in subject material. He's also accessible out of class at Schulchan Ivrit or by email. He will improve your Hebrew drastically, and you'll have fun learning!

TAKE AVI!!! I absolutely loved his class. He crafted slideshows just for us and according to the topics that WE wanted to learn about. He's so kind and funny and cares so much for his students' success.

he grades really tough on homeworks (i got a lot of 60s) and there's hw everyday + weekly quizzes. good at teaching, supportive but sometimes unsympathetic (or has too high expectations of how easily we can retain words). accessible through groupme or text, not email. class discussions sometimes became anti-Palestine which was uncomfortable

I would definitely not recommend. This professor demonstrates a lack of care for his students and total apathy about the subject im interested in. A very poor experience I give 0 as a score if I coyld

analysis.name: Amber Taylor
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I can't say enough great things. Very caring and gives wonderful feedback. By far the most supportive and invested professor I have had. Her students are lucky to have her. Expect a well-structured class that you will really learn from.

Took for Rhetoric of City Streets. You get to choose a topic related to Austin that interests you to research for the whole semester. Most smaller assignments are completion pass/fail, with two large essays, and one final multimedia project. Definitely recommend!

I loved taking Rhetoric of City Streets with Professor Taylor so much that now every time a new course schedule comes out, I check for her name specifically to see if she's teaching a new class that I could take. There is writing, obviously, but she gives you plenty of class time to work on the projects and offers great, constructive feedback.

a true hidden gem for a writing flag. tookrhetoric of city streets with her and do not regret it. super flexible and caring and the class is actually very interesting. papers do tend to be on the heavier side, but taylor is always willing to help and grades leniantly. you also have a lot of opportunities for extra credit!

analysis.name: Janine Barchas
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 65 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ridiculous standards for what she wants from her essays (not difficult, she just has her own ideas for what SHE thinks your writing should look like, and will crucify you if you don't give her what she wants to see). I found her obsession with Jane Austen and constant patting herself on the back obnoxious enough that I wouldn't take her again.

If you're a Jane Austen fanatic, and are ready to join a cult dedicated to her excellency, I still wouldn't recommend this class. Grades are based upon essays to do with "research" where the expectations are very unclear + 2 exams. Professor and TA's can be arrogant and VERY particular to their own point of view, and VERY condescending otherwise.

Dr. Barchas is somewhat unapproachable and has very strict views when it comes to grading. Students never get access to the rubric and expectations for all assignments are not made clear whatsoever. Lectures are somewhat useful as they serve as material for the quizzes, research papers, and midterm. Attendance is mandatory for discussion sections.

Barchas has a psycho-sexual relationship with Jane Austen. She obsesses over her to the point of sucking out all the fun of her novels. When first signing up, I read the warnings of this class, and ignored them. I thought I would be the exception - I love to read, write, and I'm well versed in Austen. Listen to me now: you are NEVER the exception.

This is the worst professor I have ever met in my life. She knows nothing about teaching. She just grades your paper whatever she wants and she ruins many students' GPA. If you want to take her class, please prepare for a C or D for this class.l

analysis.name: David Buss
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's not too open to criticisms of his research work, but I have to give it to him, he's a great professor. Assigned textbooks are very helpful. Attendance not mandatory, but you should just go and experience his lectures. Very interesting course, but don't get caught up in the narrow social framework of Evo Psych. Always stay skeptical.

He is one of the best professors here at UT hands down. You'll definitely need to read the textbook to pass the exams but the readings are manageable. He loves to interact with his students and he is a very funny guy. One of my favorite courses I have taken.

Dr. Buss is back to teaching evolutionary psych! I'd highly recommend the class. The only grades are 4 exams, which are fair and the info is largely covered in the lectures. (But reading will help a lot). Very interesting topic and lectures -- no attendance taken but you'll want to go. Dr. Buss and the TA are truly experts in this topic.

The lectures had a lot of interesting and valuable material! This course was only graded on 4 exams, but they were all very easy to pass as long as you did the readings. The lecture slides also give an overview of material you needed to focus on knowing for each exam.
This class was a complete joke.

analysis.name: Brent Iverson
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 152 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Iverson is the best professor I've had at UT! He records his lectures, but I highly recommend going to class because the vibes he gives off are great and he's an amazing lecturer. He has old exams posted which help a lot when it comes to studying for exams. His tests are a challenge, but definitely doable. He is the best ochem professor.

MUST TAKE HIS CLASS! You'll not only acquire more than enough knowledge to tackle subsequent UT courses (& MCAT) but he also imbues his class w/ wholesome lessons in life. In brief, Dr. Iverson is a prof who enjoys pointing out how smoothly he segues from one topic to the next, providing his class with "time capsules," & advocating to run run run!

Iverson is AMAZING. People always look forward to his lectures- he knows how to explain the same topic in a million different ways so every kind of student will understand. He works tirelessly to make sure every student has the opportunity to do extremely well in his class, and the head TA (Chris) is great too. You will love this class!!!!
Dr. Iverson, if you read this. You made me love a class I once used to hate. I was having anxiety over Ochem, but you changed that. Thank you for being there for your students, thank you for caring.

You are LUCKY if you have the chance to take him. I was so scared to take Ochem bc I'm an average student and I loved his class and he is hands down my fav prof. He is super accessible outside class despite corona. He goes above and beyond to help you learn and keep you interested in lecture. He also provides a ton helpful materials and practices.

analysis.name: Eric Bickel
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor seems intent on using his class as some sort of "filter". While his first priority should be ensuring students understand the material, he is more interested in using his position for his own interests. Exams seem to be deliberately convoluted. You'd think some people would have better things to do in life but maybe he doesn't.

Exams consist of topics not practiced on the homework and rarely mentioned in class. Doesn't prioritize making sure students actually understand the material and are able to practice it. Alongside this, there is a heavy workload with tests, case studies and homework, along with weekly quizzes.

he is honestly not a bad professor but sometimes lectures are boring. the exams are very fair and are similar to the practice ones that he uploads but they definitely felt very rushed. the case studies and hw take forever to complete though. overall not as bad as what these reviews are making him seem like.

Studied the material he gave us + textbook for weeks in preparation for the final. Did not matter he decided to test us over software formulas and stuff that was not on the textbook or any class work. There was no way to study for that final. A lot of people failed even with his “holiday bonus”. Condescending when you ask questions. Bad teacher.

Avoid this guy if you can. His exams are hard, w/ concepts that are barely touched on in class. Grading feels almost vindictive. The class doesn't feel like an educational experience—it feels like a punishment for not deciphering his convoluted teaching style. Case studies are lengthly, discussions mandatory, 8am, no exam drops, steer clear of him.

analysis.name: Douglas Bruster
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took this as a hybrid course, so there was an in-person discussion session once a week while lectures were online. Discussions are fast-paced, so think quick. Otherwise, lecture videos are 2-3 hrs of content with one easy 10 Q quiz due at the end of the week, each week. Could do it all in one day and have the rest of the week off.

“Professor Bruster is an excellent 10/10 instructor, but I had concerns with the grading. My TA's feedback felt unusually strict and sometimes hard to connect to the rubric, making it difficult to know how to improve. I also struggled with the quizzes; the 2-minute limit for 10 questions felt too fast. Adding 1–2 minutes would have helped.”

i think that the tests are pretty hard if you don't pay attention to lectures. so simple fix (which i realized mid semester) -- you actually have to go to the lectures. exams are best tackled by rewatching movies. (some tests grade one scenes you won't remember otherwise.) really great prof tho and you can tell he teaches for the love of the game.

Bruster is such a cool and fun guy, and I would definitely love to take him again. All lectures are recorded so it's easy to catch up if you miss class. I took this as a VAPA for my RTF degree, would recommend for other RTF majors because it shares a lot of the same basic terminology as foundational RTF courses. Overall, very easy course.

I really enjoyed the Films of Alfred Hitchcock class. I do think this warrants more time than a VAPA should take, but if you have the time (3-ish hours outside of class/week), then I recommend it. The professor is great, but just know that achieving a true A is actually pretty difficult.

analysis.name: David Bogard
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Well structured class! Weekly homework + quiz (based on hw problem), readings (not required) before each class to better understand material, uploads lecture notes, and exams are very fair. Very kind professor and I would recommend!

This class definitely helped me grow a lot as an engineer and a problem solver. Bogie orients the content so it's contextualized in problem solving and real applications, and teaches just the right amount of theory. You are expected to read the textbook before every lecture, so it gets difficult to stay on pace, but this class is very rewarding.

I enjoyed this class even though it was pretty difficult. Exams problems are very similar to the homework problems. I'm a pretty average student, and I didn't feel the need to study extensively for the tests as there are no surprises. Lecture can be very confusing and he goes through the slides fast. He does posts the annotated notes from class.

Dr. Bogard is very knowledgeable and funny. Lectures can be a little hard to pay attention to, but rewatching them on Canvas definitely helps. Assignments can be long and difficult but quizzes are very similar to it. Midterms are reasonable difficulty, but final exam was nothing like the midterms and was harder. Overall, great & helpful professor.

Lectures are fast-paced and hard to understand if you didn't do the reading. Tests are a lot like the homework problems and practice tests, and include a conceptual portion. Material is difficult, but he teaches the concepts in an intuitive way and is overall a good and fun professor. Do practice problems before tests and you should be fine.

analysis.name: Carlos Torres-Verdin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor really cares about teaching. He has a binder full of practical examples that he uses to teach. He writes summaries for each lecture. Exams are aligned with homework. Great TAs. Excellent solution sets. Field trip included.

Great instructor and very well organized. He teaches practical knowledge and designs the homework and exams to be complementary. Nice person. Very helpful. Optional field trip and visit to core facilities. Cares about students.

Hes a great professor that really wants the entire class to engage and learn. Exams are hard, but if you understand the material you will be fine! Go to office hours, he is even better explaining one-on-one. He is accesible after class, super funny in lectures and tries his best to be as resourceful as possible to optimize students learning!
Wow, one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. You learn so much from this professor, but he is an all around great person. This class kicked my ass, but is extremely relevant to our major.

Overall great instructor and very well organized course with lots and lots of practical examples. Very good solution sets. Subject matter is hard but it is what we expect in a professional setting. The instructor organizes a field trip. Highly recommended

analysis.name: Caryn Conley
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Worst class I've ever taken. It was immensely difficult, and each weekly homework assignment increases in scope and complexity. By the end of the semester, it was taking me 10+ hours per homework (she seems to think it's funny, too). Tests aren't any easier, and the examples in class are elementary compared to what you are asked to learn yourself.

Worst professor I've ever had. She doesn't know Python. Every week you have homework and because it's so difficult you have to start the day it gets assigned otherwise you wont finish. Her lectures don't help because they're very simplistic when compared to her assignments. It's like having a project every week. Reading the book helps a bit.

UT fired Dantu because he was bad at teaching, and they brought in someone worse. Conley is a poor hire who needs to be fired ASAP. She is horrible at teaching, awkward at interacting, and incredibly unhelpful at answering questions. Tests were insanely hard, while examples were elementary in class, and appeals were not  accepted.

Dr. Conley seems nice, but she is not a very interesting or inspiring professor at all. The average class day in MIS 304 consists of Dr. Conley reading a 10-20 slide PowerPoint as lecture, and giving one or two in-class practice problems at the end of class. Expect to devote 10-12h/week on homework assignments. Wish I chosen a different professor..

This class is a lot of work. Hopefully u get an easy client and your team actually does work. Definitely most workload of any mis class but it is the capstone. Conley can be unclear at times so always clarify on slack. Also, lectures are so boring and the pre class hw never aligns but what can you do.

analysis.name: Cynthia Cabrera
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cabrera is obviously very passionate about teaching. But she consistently gets practice problems wrong and explains concepts in overly complex ways. If you can do well with this teacher that means you already took calculus or you completely learned the course on your own time. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

Just horrible at teaching, nice person and passionate at math, but she makes so many little mistakes while teaching it makes someone who already took calculus worse at calculus. Would not recommend. If you get this teacher I would recommend self teaching and tutors. Good luck.

She is a lovely person who cares about her work, however, she is not a good professor. She overcomplicates simple concepts and underexplains the more difficult ones. Exams are weighted heavily making the other assignments seem unimportant even when they take a lot of time. I would recommend avoiding her and taking calculus with another professor.

Getting in contact with her is very hard. She overcomplicates subjects, and her lectures are very hard to understand. Many of the assignments you do seem unrelated to what you are learning. In addition, on the tests, there is a lot of material that you will feel like you never learned. Take calculus with someone else.

She's incredibly sweet and you can tell she loves her job. However, she's not a good teacher. About 1/5 or of her students actually go to lectures because they're unhelpful, she's a confusing lecturer. Time is spent super inefficiently. If you reach out to her personally, she'll try her best but you'll have better luck self-teaching in this class.

analysis.name: Can Kilic
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Despite the uncertainty principle, I am 100% certain of Dr. Kilic's position as the GOAT and of his momentous pedagogical skills. I've taken 315 and now 373 with him, and he goes through ALL steps of the derivations and makes concepts amazingly clear and intuitive. I have given several lectures myself now and he is my greatest inspiration for them.

I had Dr. Kilic for waves (my review is somewhere below) and now for quantum- unlike an electron's position, I can say with absolute certainty that he is probably my favorite phys prof I've had so far. He made something complex understandable, especially after setting a solid foundation in PHY 315. I'm gonna miss having him as a teacher next sem :(

Dr. Kilic, my goat! I was terrified for this class, but he made waves very accessible and I finally felt like a true physics major after taking the class. For the exams: just keep calm. Most questions aren't terribly difficult, just tricky. I only wish I'd studied more for the weekly quizzes. 10/10, might consider taking this class again. Lol.

Dr. Kilic made this 315 very manageable for me with difficult homework's and good lectures that balanced each other out. You have a week to complete homework's with one quiz a week. Office hours were very useful for me as they helped a lot with mastering/practicing the content. Exams could be regraded on request as well. I would recommend taking.

Amazing lecturer who explains concepts and derivations clearly, I felt like I had a thorough understanding of the content. Lectures move a little fast but lecture notes are always uploaded pretty promptly afterward.

analysis.name: Kirsten Bradbury
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 162 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: She is so awesome, I loved having her an have taken several classes with her - I wish I could take every class with her. She's so accommodating and lenient and cares about her students more than anything else.

This class is one of the easiest but most enjoyable courses I've taken this year. You have to genuinely try not to get an A, because the entire course is online and open-note. Dr. Bradbury is really funny, and her lectures can be super interesting. I recommend taking this class if you need something easy and fun to fill up your schedule.

Clinical psych with Bradbury is one of the best classes in the psych major. TAKE IT. Her lectures are super interesting and easy to understand and readings aren't too heavy. Quizzes could sometimes be hyper-specific but as an online asynch course I get that. She was very nice and helpful over email too!

EASY A. Take this class if you need a UGS class! Amazing professor who is super understanding and laid back. Very few not hard assignment. Laid back about due dates and can miss about 10 classes without it effecting your grade. Genuinely a good person to talk to and have as a recommendation.

I really hated how this class was formatted. We had quizzes almost every other day, and the material itself wasn't hard but rather the amount of readings and lectures she provided was too much to do in a short amount of time. Each quiz was spaced out 2-3 days. Dr. Bradbury herself is fine, lectures tend to be repetitive and unnecessarily long.

analysis.name: Lulu Cambronne
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor is frequently confused in her own lectures and does not answer questions well. There are pacing issues as the most difficult content is often skimmed over. The exams/assignments are moderately challenging, and you need to self-teach most of the content. Start studying for exams a week in advance- content is dense. There is EC though.

lectures are usually hard to get and prof cambronne stumbles often, mostly when a student doesn't understand first try or asks any question. i would probably feel better if i went to office hours. TAs were great, very helpful at discussion sections. content is application, not memorizing, on the midterms, but study past exams and you'll be fine

Cambronne is a nice and intelligent woman. However, she is not able to translate her knowledge in a digestible manner. She often confuses herself in lecture and is not proficient in the calculations she's teaching. Concepts are not clearly explained or stated. She's kind, but I had to teach everything myself. Disappointing.

Dr. Cambronne was contagiously passionate about the subject, and tried to make the lectures applicable to life. The class was difficult for me and the exams were all open ended, but she has extra credit and I heard she rounds end of sem. I think this is the only class she teaches so she learns everyone's names and makes a point to reach out to you.

Exams are heavily application based. There is little to no opportunity to get that type of application practice, so exams are very difficult to prepare for, and she does not offer a curve. To do well in the course, you need to be the type of student that thinks above and beyond the things taught in class. TAs are amazing though, ask them for help

analysis.name: Caitlin Gorback
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Most difficult, sour professor I've ever had. Professors w/ 40+ years of teaching hold more grace and kindness than her, she just started. She'll dock more points if she regrades, 80% of grade=2 HWs + 2 exams, always has a pessimistic attitude, HW/quizzes/exams are intensely difficult, all free responses. I admire her commitment to misery!

Some of the most dry lectures I have ever been through. And grading depends primarily on open ended tests that cover over 400 slides worth of material. She teaches like a robot and attendance is mandatory. Wouldn't recommend to anyone at all.

avoid at all costs, take anyone else as a matter of fact. Passive aggressive teaching style, don't know how she was even hired. Expects us to be tested on creating numerous pro formas for a final exam without any notes, after maybe doing 1 assignment in class that took us days to do. Honestly a terrible experience.

One of the most boring classes I've ever sat through. She is snarky, very passive aggressive, acts like she knows everything and nothing at the same time, and is a tough grader with wacky grading policies. The guest lectures were the best part and she would consistently interrupt them to ask her own questions. Take any other professor if into RE.

This is the best example of someone that is a good researcher but has a hard time conveying information to students. Lectures were not engaging and she often made passive aggressive remarks. The material itself could have been easy if it had been clearly communicated, but there were often contradicting statements and mistakes on the slides.

analysis.name: Jessica Chancey
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: all the good reviews are from people that are cracked. she is the worst professor i've ever had. even if you word for word memorize what she says in lectures some points will be taken off of exams. her grading rubrics make no sense whatsoever. on top of this her lectures make no sense. even if you take good notes lectures are incoherent ramblings

Course is disorganized which disadvantages students who are paying to learn. The structure of the lectures make learning more difficult than need be. The professor contradicts herself and randomly mentions information that was never discussed before. "As I told you..." (she has not, in fact, told us). No thorough explanations of content in OH.

Pro: Lots of extra credit, recorded lectures, class groupme, seems nice
Con: Unclear grading criteria for exams, conflicting answers from TAs, contradicts her lectures/slides, bad lecturer
You might get a good grade in the class but she is overall not someone you wanna take Neuro One from. As a friend described "she's incompetent"

Major complaint is the grading criteria for this class. Questions on hw are sometimes unclear. Exams have several free response which is fine, but would sometimes lose points for not mentioning things that she wasn't clear on requiring.

I genuinely felt like if she had made her slides less picture based and more info it would've been fine, the other reviews are treating going to office hours, rewatching lectures, and meeting w/ her outside of class as normal, you should be able to go to lecture do the required homeworks and understand material well not have to do 10 extra steps

analysis.name: Shao-Ying Cheng
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 98 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I like that he post his lecture online. His test is VERY TRICKY, so remember to RE-READ everything and choose the best answer. Tbh, I found his class somewhat easy. I play his lecture 2x and learn overnight still got 90s on test (never go to class so attendance grade ~50%). Overall, just take detailed note and you're good
This dude is really funny and cute. He drew a frog during class. Genuinely the best lecturer I had at UT. His lectures are enough to succeed in the course.

Very funny and a great lecturer. Homework + discussion exercises are easy and are essential for doing the FR on the exams. Exams are very fair, but difficult to get past high B-low A bc of tricky wording and a few highly specific questions (none correct, more than one correct, select all). Memorize lectures + study guide, curve was A- to A for me.

Don't take for an easy A course, even though the UT+ distribution looks amazing. Class average was a B- this semester & said he won't curve the grade & not even bother emailing him asking him to. Tests are based more on whether or not you can pick up the deception he is trying to trick you on more than how much you studied. Don't bother w/ textbook

Discussion sessions are optional but material covered in them make up at least 30pts on the exam, so go to them! The best way to study for exams is to use the study guide and supplement lecture slides /notes with the book to fill in any gaps. The class is hard but Dr Cheng is engaging and readily accessible, along with the TAs, outside of class.

analysis.name: Rene Cabrera
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: People are really dramatic, Rene is a good guy. He wants his students to do well and took measures to improve his class after people tanked the first midterm - that's why there's a drop guys!! He takes time to work together on the homework DURING lecture time on Thursdays and ensures the exams are based on HW/practice - even held review sessions.

genuinely the worst diff eq professor you could take at UT. tests were unbeleivably difficult and conceptual. half of the class would leave the exam room with only 2.5/5 questions done. so much unnecessary work assigned as well. reading quizzes, application quizzes, and worksheet assigned every week, homework every other week. stay away from rene.

His lectures were very proof-based and didn't follow the logical flow of how you would like to learn content for the first time. This made it difficult to parse what was important or not. However, he is a caring professor and will help you should you ask. 2 midterms and a final, lowest is dropped, first test was a lot harder than the other two.

His lectures were not helpful for the most part, I ended up just teaching myself and did just fine. I do think he lacks communication and understanding. He came off as rude, making little remarks to me during our short conversations as I tried to fix a mistake on an exam. I just warn you to avoid running into any issues with him, he is no help.

M361K is hard regardless of the prof. However, Rene does a good job giving you all of the materials you need to succeed - exam Qs were similar to (or the same) as HW and practice exam Qs. The HWs are difficult and take time, but he helps a lot during office hours. This sem., he made the final optional. He is a caring guy who wants you to succeed.

analysis.name: Eric Dewaal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class took me through the 5 stages of grief and is the most difficult class I've taken. De Waal is a good lecturer but expects you to know A LOT and intentionally words his questions to be tricky. He also grades the free response extremely harshly so you lose points on little things. I managed to get an A by studying ~25 hours for the final...

This class was very difficult from the beginning. Exams are very specific and he expects you to know all of it. He gives a lot of study materials though, but just a lot of material on the exam, and very very oddly worded questions that are difficult to understand.

I really liked Dr. De waal even tho I dropped. He cares a lot about his students, but the exams killed me. I studied multiple days before each exam and didn't pass a single one. Content is interesting but very complex and memorization heavy. Taking with a diff prof next semester.

The exams were insanely hard. Sure, there was a lot of material, but he will nitpick on the specific criteria he determines for points for FRQs even though other open-ended answers are correct. He will take away any information that is 'incorrect'. The high school was not even a 100 for any of the exams except the easiest one (exam 4).

This class was really difficult for me, and the exams killed me a little. FRQs were graded harshly in my opinion, but the MCQ portion was okay. It's a lot of memorization and content but he himself was a good lecturer. He broke things down relatively well and does give resources. I recommend doing the worksheets to prepare but its def a heavy class

analysis.name: David DiCarlo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is not a very good professor. He does not have any industry experience and his background is just physics and water. I don't get why UT Austin keeps hiring inexperienced professors being so close to Houston. His lecture notes and writing are a mess. He makes us show memes every class, because of how boring it gets!

Is it fun? No, its thermo. DiCarlo makes it as enjoyable as thermo could possibly be though, and makes an effort to know all the students. Topics are not digestible just through lectures, and required lots of reviewing notes, textbooks, and office hours (always very approachable). Test heavy, but if you understand concepts, they aren't that bad.
Best class I've ever taken. People say it's hard, but it's so light if you just lock in. 10/10 would take again, all thanks to Professor DiCarlo

He is very disorganized and sloppy. He makes many mistakes. He is very hard to understand. No one understood what he was saying. The only thing good about him is that he had a good sense of humor, other than that, he is a terrible prof. I wouldn't recommend anyone taking a class with him.

Professor DiCarlo makes coming to class fun he stops the lectures halfway through class so students can stand up and tell dad jokes, a much needed break from a 1.5 hour lecture of heavy material. He cares about each student and makes an effort to learn everyones name and interests. Thermo is a hard subject but he keeps you invested and tests easy.

analysis.name: Hugh Daigle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Sweet guy and never gave us a lot of homework. He allows 1 page for cheat sheets and midterms weren't hard to get an A. Just review his slides and put everything on your cheat sheet. He also gave a super easy 10 point bonus question on a midterm once, so the average was like a 103. I am definitely going to take his sustainability course too.

Dr Daigle is awesome! Exams are very similar to homework and lectures and you get a cheat sheet. He curves HEAVILY. Lab reports are long and tedious (like 30 pages...), but you only have to do 3 ish and he is a light grader. He also pushes due dates if he feels there is too much on his students' plates. Very passionate about rocks!
Amazing lectures, I wished he taught more classes on formation evaluation.

Dr. Daigle is very wholesome. He is clear he is very passionate about teaching. Even though the topic is mostly boring, it is nice listening to his lecture. A single pop quiz in the semester. Homeworks were easy/graded generously. TAs were nice. Open note exams. The exams were straightforward, some math, some T/F. 3 lab reports were written.

Dr. Daigle's course is a great introduction to the many challenges that come with using more renewables. Assignments and presentations were straightforward, and the content was interesting. I would recommend this class to anyone who meets the prerequisites. Virtually all of the open note final could be completed by referencing the slides.

analysis.name: Dirk Mateer
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: So fun and easily manageable while taking calc 1. There are lectures 2 a week, and they're really interesting. You read 1 chapter a week and do in-Quizitive every Tuesday by 8 pm. He does do in-class Kahoot's and Think-Pair-Shares for participation points, but we have 3 weeks left of classes, and almost everyone already has enough points.

I was dreading taking an economics class—I was a mostly straight A student in high school, but nearly failed macro. I took micro with Dr. Mateer, and honestly, it was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. He makes lectures fun and engaging with games and activities that demonstrate key economics concepts. I highly recommend! Take this class!

Dirk is the best professor I've had. Fantastic lecturer and a super forgiving grading system (everyone should get A's as long as they show up and try). Don't need to study too much for tests and very engaging in class as he gives out candy for participation & money for kahoot wins. Only downside to this glorious man is his nephew Mateer (OU's QB).

Dirk is friendly and passionate about teaching, but lectures are often inefficient/irrelevant. The textbook has the important content for exams, while in-class “activities” meant to be engaging are a waste of time (ex: donut eating contests). Exams are fair but get harder through the semester. Class attendance is needed for participation points.

Dirk is the GOAT. King made everything easy and he was just so real. Nothing about the course was hard and exams were similar to the Kahoots and the homework. He's funny and always gave out prizes for first in the Kahoots or for participating when he needed volunteers. He bought me a frosty from Wendy's one time and also brought donuts to class.

analysis.name: Kaori Duffey
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Duffey-sensei is truly a gift! lots of homework, tests, and a daily quiz, but as is to be expected when learning such a hard language. it is a lot of work, but it truly does pay off! lots of opportunities to raise your grade, just study hard! she is so sweet, and is always willing to help you when you are struggling. cannot recommend enough!

Duffy-sensei fosters a really comfortable and fun learning environment. As long as you show up every class and give your best effort, you will do well. She has been my favorite instructor so far at UT, please take her class!

Duffey sensei is always caring and considerate of her students and very available outside class through office hours. There's definitely less work than the lower division courses, but there are short tests every two weeks. There is a major project that you shouldn't procrastinate on, but if you put some work into it everyday it's very manageable

I LOVE DUFFEY SENSEI! If I could take her for all of my Japanese classes, I would definitely! She is the sweetest and super nice. As long as you're on top of the content and stay prepared for the quizzes, you will be okay. Learning Japanese is hard, but definitely take the initiative to learn. If you fall behind, this class will be very hard!

A GEM. I absolutely adore her! She is so kind & understanding. She will hold you accountable to actually do the work, so don't slack off but she will understand if you accidentally forget to turn in something. Just don't take advantage of her kindness! She truly is a great person. If I could take her for ALL of my semesters of Japanese I would!!

analysis.name: Donna Kornhaber
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Y'all this woman is my goat. I had her for LAH 350: Best Pictures (which wasn't an option on RMP oops) and it was my favorite class I've ever taken. She knows everything about film formalism and I respect her so much. Just do the assignments and stay engaged in class and she'll love you. I can't hype her up enough I loveeeee her.

Dr. Kornhaber is amazing!! She is the most kind and flexible professor I've ever had. Every opinion, insight, or thought is welcome in her classroom and she never makes a student feel stupid. The content is amazing and has changed how I watch movies for the better. Highly recommend to take her, she is beyond great!

Dr. Kornhaber's class is interesting and teaches you a lot about film. The course load seems daunting with all of the books and films you are assigned, but you can get away with just writing about films. I would recommend watching the films (which are all classics anyway) and just spark-noting the readings. The discussions are boring but required.

The class can be very interesting or boring but shes very nice and really wants you to learn the material. You do not have to do too much work on the essays and she gives you plenty of options to write on so you aren't limited.  The class was fun and very interesting. Make sure to use the university writing center. It helps a ton in this class.

Very fun class! Watching movies as homework was great. Except when you watch movies in class you might fall asleep. She is very flexible with watching the movies and reading the books because she understands we have other classes. Grading depends mostly on TAs however, but still an easy A.

analysis.name: Donnie Sackey
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Sackey lectures, TA's grade. His lectures are very interesting, random, and engaging. Just engage with him during lecture to make him feel a little more love. He is a great source of advice when doing the actual assignments for the class, but make sure to give him time to respond. He also had a great dynamic with Dr. Laude in joint lectures.

Dr. Sackey is the best! I've taken him for a few classes and he is a very understanding professor who likes to push his students to perform WITHOUT hurting their grade. I wish all my professors were like him.

Topic: Rhetoric & Data Visualization | Excellent (and hilarious) professor! I'd recommend this to any STEM major. You'll not just learn to write but make great PowerPoints. Btw, don't be scared by "98 = A". Like 75% of the grade is participation *and* there's enough extra credit opportunities to bring that down to a de facto 94.
very funny and pretty nice! sometimes he can be blunt but i think its more of his sense of humor ... dont take him too seriously lol

Professor Sackey is one of the best professors I had at UT so far. He always gives extensive feedback, makes lectures super interesting, and has a lot of office hours outside of class. He's kind, caring, helpful, and hilarious. You can tell he's passionate about what he teaches! Would love to take a class with him again.

analysis.name: Thomas Edison
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Thomas Edison wants his students to succeed, and provides plenty of opportunities to for you to practice and ask questions. If you want to do well the most important thing to do imo is to go to his office hours every week. His class will be tough, but you'll understand the material much better than with other professors. Pressure makes diamonds

Lots of HW, weekly quizzes, 3 exams, 1 final. He did allow a makeup exam for the 1st exam because the class did poorly on it. 
He's tough, but cares. Go to office hours, whether it's his or the TA's. Ask questions. The worst thing you can do for this class is not participate or ask questions. Sets up a strong foundation for future courses.

The quizzes, exams, and course content of this class are extremely difficult. If you are not religious, find a religion and start praying. Would not recommend this class or professor to anyone. The proffesor is very hard to communicate with via email, does not release keys to anything, and will laugh in your face for asking questions.

Dr. Edison is one of the most difficult professors I've ever had but also has taught me the most in such a short amount of time. Honestly, the quizzes aren't that relevant to your course grade but will be very difficult. I'm very grateful to have a break from how all consuming his class is, you will need to set aside probably 10 hours every week

Very knowledgeable, but does not post keys to very tough home works/quizzes. Lectures are a lot of information thrown at you, but he knows his stuff. Nothing matters but exam grades, need 60 average. Can be condescending. Plays favorites. Incredibly difficult, don't expect an A. Jump from HW to exams is very unreasonable. Not great professor

analysis.name: Edward Theriot
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS CAN BE TRICKY! DR. THERIOT CARES ABOUT HIS STUDENTS! MAKE SURE TO GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS! IF YOU PUT THE EFFORT, AN A ISN'T IMPOSSIBLE! UNLIKE OTHER BIO 370 CLASSES, THERE IS MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS! TA TAHMIN IS THE BEST!

Ed is the fookin man. Never seen a professor care so much about his students until him. The material is fairly easy and has long office hours and review sessions that he does himself. Pretty funny dude. Take him if you can! Gives out practice tests too. Very easy going and doesn't overwhelm you with material. The best BIO370 prof hands down.

Even a semester later I randomly think how Dr. Theriot is doing. He was a wonderful professor. Other than being passionate about this class and his research, he is an incredibly caring man to students. He will extend his office hours for as long as you need, even to talk about things like his personal passion for duck-hunting! Take him if you can!

I always think back to how wonderful of a professor Ed is. Sometimes lectures can seem to go on forever and seem very confusing, so I recommend reading the chapters before class so you can follow along. Tests and discussion section matter. Very caring guy - to the extreme. Will sit down with you for two hours to make sure you understand a subject.

Class is hard ranked, which can push your grades down on tests. However, at the end, he fills up most of the F slots with the students that dropped the class. NEED TO READ. Class based on just 4 tests, no final. Great guy, passionate and involved in the material, very helpful in class. If you put in the effort, hell work to help your grade too.

analysis.name: Michael Endl
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 83 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Super easy and interesting course. Information on tests is easy to learn but very specific so attendance and good listening and note taking are important (we're in college this isn't hard). As long as you take notes this is a free A.

Dr. Endl is really funny, and his lectures can be really interesting. I didn't pay all that much attention in class, which is my own fault, but half of your grade comes from just showing up. The tests aren't that difficult, but if you don't come/don't pay attention, you may get stuck. Overall, this was a great course to take for science credit.

Good professor. Class has 4 Tests and 4HWs and that is it for your grade. Tests were usually chill; you can find flashcards online. There is extra credit if needed. I found the class pretty intresting. Definitely made me think of the universe in ways I had never before, and it's really cool if you are interested in space and possibilities of life.

You can tell the professor is not only an expert in the field, but also passionate to the point that he makes every single lecture fascinating to a room of people likely entirely disconnected from his field of study. Grade is comprised of 4 exams, attendance, and 4 homeworks. The exam questions are exactly adjacent to what is covered in lecture.

This class is about astrobiology, not speculating on aliens. However, it was easy. There's 4 homeworks that are similar to the 4 unit tests, no final. Attendance "mandatory" but it's taken through instapolls, and you only need 70% to get full credit. Professor Endl is genuinely passionate about astrobiology, but prefers subs over canceling class.

analysis.name: ETHEL BAYER SANTOS
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are hard to understand- but the exercises that she provides for the exams are extremely helpful- and I don't see how anyone wouldn't get an A in this class. Use your resources and you'll be fine. She likes open discussion, so will try to get you to talk during classes. She is sweet, and cares a lot about the subject.

Unfortunately I didn't have a great time in this class, mostly due to the lectures. The powerpoints were somehow both overly complex and vague at the same time, and I ended up using the textbook to understand many of the topics we had to cover. Exams were fine though, but I wouldn't be surprised if she changes things up in the future.

Unfortunately, my experience with Dr. Santos disappointing. The course lacked clear guidance and structure, making it difficult for students to understand expectations or succeed. Opportunities for meaningful feedback and support were minimal, and most times, the instructor's tone felt discouraging rather than constructive. Avoid if possible.

analysis.name: Eman  Alasadi
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I would say the only downside of this class is the grade distribution, but I really love her resources like her practice sets. I re-took CH301 after taking Laude last semester. She is SO incredible and straightforward and the way that she teaches makes perfect sense to me. We learn exactly what we need to do well on the exam, no fluff!

If you have to take any sort of Chemistry at UT, TAKE HER. This is probably the most caring and thoughtful professor I have ever had. Her lectures are actual fun and she goes out of her way to make sure students understand. Uploads all here lectures online and offers so many resources for studying. Occasional extra credit during class

Truly an outstanding professor. She goes above and beyond to support her students and provides an exceptional amount of resources to help you succeed. She is deeply invested in making sure students actually understand the material and is always willing to spend extra time explaining concepts. PChem could use slightly more rigor, but she's great

Professor Eman was the best chemistry professor ever!! She is super sweet and wants everyone to succeed. She offered 2 makeup exams at the end of the semester that will replace your lowest two exams. She is hilarious and lectures were always engaging. You do have to study and put in some time/work, but all the material is accessible and organized.

The best professor I've ever had. She gives out: extra credit, participation quizzes, practice questions, multiple practice exams for each unit, cheat sheets, FAQ's, annotated lectures, her YT channel and transcripts, a STUDY SCHEDULE, and keys to go with everything I just mentioned. Hilarious, laid back but caring. Exam grading is clear. TAKE HER.

analysis.name: Emily Caudill
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 200 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Don't take under any circumstances. She knows the material, but does not know how to teach. She jumps from slide to slide and has in class quizzes every week. These quizzes go over the same material learned from that same day. She uses other professors materials to "try" and "teach." SHE DOES NOT DROP EXAMS ANYMORE. Expect to do 6+ hours every week

Professor Caudill is the most unlikeable chemistry professor. Her voice tells you she doesn't want to be there. I found the lectures to be disengaging and hard to follow. The exam proctoring and academic integrity process was handled unfairly in my case, but the dean cleared me. She does NOT want the best for you. Do NOT take her.

slides were so unorganized, if you were to download it from canvas it will not match with what shes showing during lecture. its hard to pay attention to her, so many hw/quizzes due before class, doesnt drop exams or retest, had to drop the class because it was mentally draining trying to teach myself the material. take her or not, just be mindful

Some how my previous rating on here disappeared. Somewhat sketchy, but I will not allow my voice to be silenced, and I will exercise my first amendment right. She is monotone and boring. The only saving grace of this class is the review notes and organization of the class, but all other chem professors use it too, so it is somewhat irrelevant.

This teacher does not teach. In addition to not teaching, she somehow manages to blame the students for her lack of ability to teach. She gets distracted so easily in lecture and ends up wasting a good portion of lecture time asking students to be quiet even if they were whispering. She once yelled at her TA for helping a student.

analysis.name: Kelly Fulton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 130 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Avoid this professor and class! An insane amount of reading, which finds joy in. The format and structure of this class makes this class unbearable.

You might as well be doing readings on your own without registering because her lectures barely add anything insightful or interesting them. If you don't read and expect her to do her job and teach you the content, well prepared to be disappointed because her powerpoints are almost blank. Would not recommend. Readings are interesting though.

This professor is an absolute joke. Her lectures have nothing to do with the tests or assignments and she expect essentially memorization of the readings in order to pass tests. Now, getting a B is possible, but an A is ridiculous. This is intro to sociology, not a real class. DO NOT TAKE HER.

This class was a nightmare. Her lectures are long, tedious, and boring. She gives way too much reading for an intro class. Her in class assignments are annoying, and her exams are very confusing. She asks for little insignificant details that you won't know unless you recently read the material. I only got an A by reading all the material twice.

Don't take her. The first exam was easy but the second exam totally screwed me over. She tests over really tiny things and there are a bajillion readings so lots to memorize. In class she doesn't really lecture, just plays games on the computer and shows us graphs. I really regret taking this class.

analysis.name: Morgan Fong
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Aside from the reporting everyone thing here are some genuine critiques (I got reported). If you take this class be ready to learn pretty much entirely on your own. During class she lectures for 5 minutes and then lets you work on usually a needlessly hard in class coding assignment. Only good thing about her is the exams. Pretty straightforward.

Well-structured class, reasonable workload, and fair exams. However, Dr Fong is the most exasperating professor I have ever had. Her grading is picky to a fault and she is not understanding at all. Truly feels like she goes out of her way to make her class as annoying as possible. $100 mandatory textbook btw.

Cannot stand this prof. How do you have a PhD from a nationally ranked CS university and struggle to teach python daily? Does not want the students to succeed, is very harsh with overall grades due to "generous extra credit policy" but then accuses students of AI/cheating which makes them ineligible for said extra credit; AVOID at all costs.

Repeatedly crossed Guad without looking in hopes of being hit by a car otw to her class. She reports everyone for some unknown reason, regardless of the fact that half the coding assignments require a specific direction to follow (i got reported). Lectures are unhelpful and self-learned everything through the readings.

cheating reports aside, she's not a good professor. i self taught for EVERYTHING in this course - her lectures are around 20 minutes long and then you have to answer questions that are 10x harder than the practice for attendance. coding assignments have nothing to do with the class lectures. you're better off with ANYONE else, not worth the risk.

analysis.name: Nicholas Fey
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Grade is based on HW, 2 exams, 2 quizzes, and the final. Lectures are not mandatory (records lectures) but it is important to go/review because the quizzes and exams are of similar difficulty to the practice problems that he goes over in class. I had to learn most of the content on my own but doing the hw or asking TA's was very helpful

Dr.Fey is an amazing professor but you have to go to class. If you ask him questions he is super knowledgable. Homework is from the textbook, if you go to office hours the TA's help you with the answers. I would 100% take him again for any class.

Chill, approachable but his explanation to example/homework problems are not always so easy to understand. He said he won't be doing one random hw problem as weekly quiz in future semester. Midterms are two problems from some version of textbook. The practice exams provided do not always come with the solution, making their purpose questionable.

Dr. Fey is a good professor until the middle of the semester. Instead of walking through concepts, he relies on a handout to convey the information. For the last half of the semester, I had to self-teach some concepts and rely on the TAs. There was no answer key for past exams, but most of the midterm was textbook problems. He offered extra credit

He is a solid professor, but nothing to ride home about. Tests are 2 difficult questions and an hour long, meaning most of your grade was based on 8 total problems. I am a pretty average student, and it was not the worst. The teaching from handouts was bad, as others have said. Go to class, though, because he goes over example problems in depth.

analysis.name: Sarah Farrell
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Farrell was my favorite professor for my first semester of college. Before this class begun, I was worried about how difficult it would be to write essays all semester. There are 4 main projects that determine majority of care but if you put the effort and time in, you will be okay. She wants the best of everyone and cares for everyone.
Dr. Farrell is the best professor for RHE 306 and I found her class very interesting. Go to office hours and you should succeed.

She is super sweet and was my favorite professor! She made class interesting and collaborative! As someone who always struggled with writing and English she was always willing to help and genuinely cares about everyone! I would 100% take her class again!

Such a great professor! She was so kind and caring. She really knows what she is talking about and loves to help her students. She made this class way more interesting and enjoyable because of how flexible and helpful she was!

Lover her! She was easy with grading and there was only 4 projects, which she gave us lots of time to work on. Every day assignments were easy and she was the sweetest professor ever. Very understanding and there to help you out!

analysis.name: Frank Yan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE Frank aka Yuanke Yan his lectures are all over the place he cant speak English well enough to get past the first row. The course is graded relative to the class around you top 30% get an A is the only good thing about the class even though the test Avg is 40. Dont Take him if you want to leave the class with any knowledge in eco stats.

Exam grading is ranking based. It doesnt matter if the mean is super low in exams, the top 50% of the class gets an A- regardless of what grade you got, as long as its above 40%. Beyond that, he is good at lecturing, although his accent is not great. He also takes what other people want into heavy consideration.

This class sucks don't take it the midterm averages are in the 40s. Frank cant lecture or answer questions at all. If you took AP stats you will have a slight leg up at the start but still I would take another prof.

PLEASE AVOID IF YOU CAN. RUN.  Frank Yan is first off EXTREMELY hard to understand (not sure if he has linguistic issues). He always tells us in lecture that what we are learning is intuitive, when the MEAN for exam 2 was a 40. I am having mental health issues due to this class because it is honestly so stressful.

analysis.name: Filippo Mangolini
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This Italian man is a harsh grader and places a lot of stress on students. He is not a suitable professor for teaching this course since he can't explain the concepts well enough. In some cases, this man explains the concepts with bad examples. This course takes so much time that our PhD students have to sacrifice their research and leisure time.

Lectures are rigorous, and this course is overall time-consuming. You have to put a lot of time into it to get an A or A-. Every person in TMI and the material science track of ME needs to take it. Don't mess up with any exams, or your grade will drop a lot. This professor needs to explain those complex concepts in more detail.

There's no choice; for the Mat SCI track, we have to take this course. Overall, it's a challenging learning experience. Please avoid this lecturer at any cost. There are many more conceptual questions on his exams and final. You have to put those unfathomable concepts in your mind during a short period.

Two midterms and the final exam take up way too much of the course grades. Dude, there are no extra credits and the credits U can earn that easily. Take his homework seriously; the final is a hard version of the homework.  Overall, this course is challenging and can be a significant GPA drain.

Dr. Mangolini has perfected his craft. Canvas, HWs, lectures, and exams are all carefully curated and he is extremely organized. He's also super caring.
