Make sure to attend lectures and actually listen, because he's always dropping valuable information. Exams weren't too bad and relied heavily on info from daily canvas quizzes and handouts. 10/10.

analysis.name: Fred Valdez
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 109 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: One of the most straightforward courses I've taken at UT. Dr Valdez is pretty chill, and literally mentions what is going to appear on the tests. Takes notes during class, most of what appears on the tests is said during lectures. No trick questions on the tests, and overall an easy A if you put in a little effort.

i took this class as my last science credit needed, but missing a few didn't change my experience too much. again, lecture isn't mandatory, but labs are! the labs are very easy and TA dependent. exams are online and can be taken at home. allows for extra points if you talk to him in office hours. didn't "need" the book, so i just used lecture notes

Love Valdez. Graded mainly through lab assignments and exams. Exams are easy, take notes on the textbook, and you'll be fine. Lectures are optional, but very interesting! Lab attendance is required, but the TA will give you everything. Valdez is a very knowledgeable guy who's an expert in his field. Go to his office hours and get to know him.

my favorite class this sem! lectures are enjoyable -- go to them! labs are very doable as long as you actually put effort into them and the prelab stuff. exams are simple -- no trick questions + can pull up notes if needed. you can email him and explain your answer for pts back on exams. Incredibly nice and funny guy. I will miss his class!!

Loveeee him and his class. Professor Valdez is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he's doing. Great lectures and def worth attending. Exams are simple as long as you pay attention in class/read the textbook. Def take it if you can!

analysis.name: Frane Karabatic
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: (Spring 2025, Online course) He is great as a person, but the workload is heavy. Daily modules and it's recommended by him you study 4-6 hours per module...Theres 2 speaking tests and 9 “major” tests that are formatted like the modules/assignments. I'm not going to lie it's a big decision to take this class. Unless you're passionate, be prepared.

I cannot speak to the experience of Frane's Russian class (it didn't give me another option on here but I'm taking is BCMS classes). The first year was also a huge volume of work, but by the end of the year we basically spoke BCMS- he was incredibly flexible with deadlines and understanding of how much work he assigned was actually possible.

Reviewing for BCMS. First semester is a lot of work, but he is flexible with due dates so it's manageable. Heavy emphasis on conversation, and by end of first year you will be speaking Croatian. He's responsive and available outside class time for support if you are proactive in communicating.

I was doing 5 to 6 hours a week for his course. Most of the time, things were poorly explained and I felt poorly supported. I have hope that the rest of the Russian department at UT is better, but for now, I do not recommend online Russian 1 with this professor unless you want to be up late every night teaching yourself Russian.

Loved Frane as a person, but not a professor. Not only does he expect an insane amount of work out of you considering it is a 4 credit hour course, but ontop of that TA grades extremely harshly and acts as if we already speak the language when this is a first year introductory language course.

analysis.name: Signe Fourmy
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 121 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Fourmy is engaging, funny, and genuinely interested in what she's teaching. The hardest part about her class was the writing assignments. Still, I did pretty well so if you're a decent writer it shouldn't be too hard. It does depend on who your TA is though. Also, there was a LOT of extra credit (37 points) so just do that and you'll get an A.

Basically an English class. 70% of the grade comes from timed writes? due to fears about cheating with AI. DO NOT take if you are not a history major. Focuses on reading primary sources to learn about history but isn't successful due to the large time period and lack of class time. TA's are cryptic with help and grade harshly on differing scales.

Id say she was a teacher trying to be cool but failed, hence the discrepancy. Extra credit can raise your overall grade by 6 pts, more if you exempt the final. Essay grades depend on the TA, expect Bs. Most of the actual learning was done by hw reading, class was for analyzing the text (I only read what I expected was on the exam and did just fine)

This class will make you historically cry if you're not on top of everything. Depending on the TA you get your grade will either be semi-good or just bad. A (B) in this class is basically a D, so if you don't have the specific grade requirement to be exempt from the final exam, good luck. Readings can be time-consuming. Attendance mandatory.

If you are a STEM major and don't excel at writing essay's don't take this course. The essay's are graded very harshly and you must commit lots of time preparing for the in class handwritten essays. Only get 45 minutes and you only know the topic when you enter class. You won't know what readings it will be over as well. Just take it in the summer.

analysis.name: Patricia Garcia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I have nothing good to say. Her lectures are useless. She spends more time giving the facade of being jolly than she does coming up with quality assignments. All supposedly analytical writing assignments actually require us to support one of her biased views, and she rarely provides quality feedback. Professors like her give humanities a bad name.

A cutoff is 90, which is huge. Didn't read a single text all semester, and got an A. Going to lecture isn't required, but gets a decent amount of extra credit on exams. I was dreading humanities, but I feel like I got out of this awful requirement with Dr. Garcia's class. If you hate reading but need a Lit credit, I promise this is the best one.

Garcia's lectures are quite interesting and in depth and hit the main points that are on the frequent quizzes. Exams (4) consist of objective, short answer, and an essay question. There were 2 standalone extra credit opportunities and another on a close reading installment (4 CRITs total, 16%). We also went to the HRC for to see original books.

Im guessing (could be wrong) that she has tenure because she literally does not care about anything. So many arbitrary rules. She doesn't respond to emails on weekends (fine), needs two business days to respond (okay), then doesn't respond. But she said she "saw it though". She also changes her office hours all the time so you can really attend it.

Do not take unless you are politically liberal. I was super excited to cover Beowulf, until I realized it was feminist Beowulf (author has affinity for the word daddy and the F word). Listened to drag queen recitation in class. Prof read short story about 16 year old lesbians s*xual awakening in class. Super weird all around.

analysis.name: Laura Gonzalez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Hard to understand. Also, because she puts up her notes online, you don't feel like going to class. Her outlines are supposed to be for you write notes in but she often doesn't follow the outline. She goes way too fast and generally, you will be forced to look up the lecture online anyway because you will miss stuff.  Save yourself!
Super annoying and boring lectures that make you fall asleep.

She is very nice and sweet and tries to make lecture engaging, even if there is a lack of student participation. There are many small extra credit opportunities after each lecture, after each biweekly quiz (no final), and other misc EC assignments. Personally did not have a hard time understanding her accent, but others have said it can be tough.

She really heard the students out when we were struggling on her exams, and modified her curriculum for the better. She gives out extra credit for exams and honestly the class was definitely doable as long as you fill out the learning objectives. Her class was not hard as long as you stayed consistent with your studying and learning objectives.

Dr. Gonzalez was amazing. Focuses on research & group work more than most, which may be good or bad. Lectures could be dry, but slideshows had everything you needed. Tests had few questions but were never surprising, & there were ample opportunities for practice & EC. Gives great feedback and cares about your academic growth. Highly recommend!

analysis.name: James Gabrillo
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I'm a journalism senior taking his Multimedia Music Journ as elective and I've learned more from this class in 5 weeks than my actual required majors! He gives great 1-1 feedback that has already made me a better writer! The activities are really fun like this week we're doing reporting on live shows. Highly recommend Professor Gabrillo!

his class was one of the easiest i have taken. attendance and a weekly 200-400 word discussion post is what your grade is. show up and do the discussion post. also helps that he is very passionate about his job and brings cool guests to share their music journeys. take him if possible

I'm in Global Pop Music now and my reco is to take this class in fall!! Great prof and TAs are all super cool (they're his phd students). Mon&Wed lectures are super fun and you can see how much effort he puts into then. Thurs labs are small groups with TA. On friday night you submit a short essay based on fun prompts. My fave class in UT so far!!!

If you need to take a UGS, take global pop music with Dr. Gabrillo! His lectures are super interesting and fun, especially since he brings up popular and familiar music from different genres! He only assigns weekly short essays (200-400 words) where you write about topics discussed during lectures. I DEFINITELY recommmend!!

I love Professor Gabrillo in Multimedia Music! He seems like a really nice and caring human. Super interesting topics and case studies. We wrote essays based on a complex question of the week, then did couple of creative individual projects. He's super smart and assigns lots of readings (legit full books) but I just skimmed and survived!

analysis.name: Katie Gray
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She's a very nice professor but she does not spend enough time on the material and her examples in class do not help with the homework. The homework takes forever to complete even if you read the chapter and listen to the lecture. I would definitely recommend taking another professor for this class.

Katie is a really good teacher and makes the material easy for everyone to understand. I thought the class was really easy, so I never attended office hours. However, if you need to she makes herself very available for all students. She really cares about all of her students and is a really good resource.

Katie is the best mis 301 professor!! Her lectures prepare you for the exam content the best and all of her classes are recorded on zoom if you can't attend. The final group project was trickier than the rest of the class but she made herself available for any questions. Overall, I found better success in her class than my friends with other profs

Great professor! Great lectures, responsive to email, does a good job overall. Group project was kinda confusing but overall not too difficult. Got an A- but could've gotten an A if I put a little more effort into studying. Would definitely take again if I had the opportunity.

Anyone taking someone else for MIS 301 is missing out!

This professor is absolutely the best professor out of all MIS professors. If you go in person to class, she will teach you the content that will be on the test. She does offer Zoom classes, but I say go in person so you can do better. Overall, she genuinely cares about all her students, and I really liked her and her class.

analysis.name: Charulata Ghosh
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Highly recommend taking this prof! Straightforward class, tests made sense if you came to class. Canceled almost every friday which was awesome. She gave us a study guide with everything that would be on the tests, I studied for like 2 hours and got an A on both tests. Attendance optional but lectures were very helpful and short.

The class wasn't hard, but not the easiest. Lectures are interesting. The professor is nice. Tests aren't super hard, but make sure to study. There are attendance checks from time to time, but still go to class because you learn a lot from the lectures.

Instructions are kind of all over the place, but it doesn't really matter cause there aren't a lot of assignments. Homework is minimal, and the teacher is honestly such a chiller. Heavy on lectures, but the class is only 45 minutes so it's manageable.

I retained a lot through this class. The tests are very straightforward as long as you go to the lectures. Attendance is "required" but she does randomized attendance checks like once a month and cancels friday class often!

analysis.name: Andrea Gutierrez
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Class is a guided discussion as opposed to lectures. Know this going in. It is necessary to participate a little bit, but if you do the readings, you should have no problem doing so. No exams, they are replaced by an timed essay in class. Grading on it was not incredibly difficult however, and it proved to be a great and insightful class.

Professor is very knowledgeable about the subject, but the readings are not always very easy. You don't have to pay for a textbook for the course. Readings are on canvas. You'll also have to watch movies for class. Her feedback does help you build skills for writing and gaining confidence in the college setting. Grading seemed quite lenient.

Professor is fair and cares deeply about her subject. There are a lot of readings and films you'll have to watch for class, but grading is lenient. Sets the bar high for course content. Attendance is required for the grade. Students self-assess part of the participation grade. I'd take one of her courses again.

Professor is passionate about the subject, but there are a lot of reading and many are complex. That said, readings all together made up the best course packet of any course I've had at UT. You're also required to watch movies for class. Attendance and participation count. Professor is caring.

Lectures are mandatory which are quite honestly boring, but most of the content is learned there with the other part of the content learned by the constant journal entry assignments. Speaking of those, there is so much reading that goes with this class, which I would not expect of an elective class. The professor is chill and nice though honestly.

analysis.name: Gene McDonald
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I liked this lab! The format was recently changed, so many things were a bit of trial and error, but it's really clear how much he cares about us learning skills applicable outside of this course. Graded mostly on a few quizzes, mid semester report, and final report + lab performance. Very hands on, and I really enjoyed coming to lab!
This guy is literally the goat best prof in the whole department easily super chill and a good lecturer take this class. Best lab I've taken in undergrad!

Dr.McD is honestly so sweet. Although he can be a little sassy at times but he tries really hard to sure we have everything in order to do well in this course. His lectures are also very helpful. Dr.McDonald honestly is such a chill guy and he deserves the world.
Love Dr. McDonald. Knows his stuff!! Great lab. Not stressful, but I learned so much and was able to apply it to my other biochem/molecular classes.

Dr. Gene McDonald is an amazing professor who works extremely hard everyday to ensure his students are receiving the best possible biochemistry lab education that they can. The course is structured very well, and the experimental proposal is crucial in developing the necessary skills for graduate school and professional careers; I highly recommend.

analysis.name: Gengchen Mai
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Mai's lectures are clear and easy to follow. Assignments are manageable because each one comes with detailed, step-by-step instructions. The course final is a project presentation, undergraduates present in groups, graduate students present individually.

An expert in his field. He's very reasonable if you have to miss class, but he does take attendance very often. There is a ArcGIS lab exercise due every week, detailed steps given. Lab attendance required. Short quiz checks on lecture materials. 1 big group project. Super chill guy for how much work he has published and done in the industry.

Graduate-level seminar course, with 2–3 papers each week. The readings are challenging but comprehensive, covering a broad range of topics the GeoAI. Gengchen is very knowledgeable and always willing to help. He has great expertise in geospatial modeling and always provides valuable suggestions for my research projects

Dr. Mai is very well-known in the GeoAI fields, and he has strong records in publication and industry collaboration. I'd say you took his class is something you could put on a resume. However his lectures were hard and the labs were unforgiving. Take lots of notes during lecture, and beware of attendance checks at the start of class.

Dr. Mai is incredibly knowledgeable about GeoAI and, importantly, makes it accessible to those new to the field. His course is well-structured to gradually ramp up to complex reading material, and he is very patient and eager to break down every aspect of the topic for a clear, intuitive explanation.

analysis.name: Morgane Haesen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Madame Haesen is a fantastic professor. She cares a lot about all of her students, and makes the class very easy to understand. It is a hybrid class, so it is a commitment to show up in person having done the readings and assignments prior to class. Strongly reccomend, don't be scared if you need to take it for a language requirement.

Fantastic teacher, best one that I have had so far at UT. She is incredibly caring and understanding while still giving amazing feedback on assignments. I learned so much French from her, and she made everything so easy to understand without making the class TOO easy. 110% would recommend.

She is so kind and a great teacher. The class is overall easy, especially if you have done French in the past; it basically reviews what you've previously learned. She is super accessible, helpful, and willing to accommodate. There are hw and weekly quizzes, but they both only take max 30 min to do/study for. The tests are not too bad either.

Dr. Haesen is super caring. She provides feedback on how to improve on your pronunciation and grammar while providing positive feedback on your responses. I had her for FR406 & FR407, I wish she teaches FR412K. The only thing I disliked was the amount of work (about 8-10 assignments due per week) which are simple but SUPER time consuming. Take her!

F601C (Spring 25). One of the best professors at UT! This course was truly designed for beginners and she made everything approachable and engaging. Her teaching style made class enjoyable and exciting. Class went by fast. Could not recommend enough!

analysis.name: Zoya Heidari
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Unless you work in a lab, this is a wasted time class. She does not have any practical experience, and it shows. She does demand a lot from students making it impossible to have a nice academic experience. Please bring experienced professionals from Houston. UT is too expensive to make us learn from inexperienced people. She is nice, though.

Professor Heidari is the GOAT of PGE professors at UT Austin. She is great at lecturing and handling examples you will see on homework and tests. I am not a morning person yet I was able to remember what she taught more than the other professor who taught this class. She is easily a 10/10 professor and I can't praise her enough.
She was teaching Advanced Petrophysics for the first time. She is well equipped with the topic and always helpful inside and outside of the class. During the classes, she was very student-friendly.

analysis.name: Samuel Horewood
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tests are reasonable and easy if you go to lectures and pay attention. Readings are light, you're not tested hard on them. Prof is pretty engaging and funny during lectures, tries to make things interesting, relatable, and relevant. A bit hard to understand because of heavy Australian accent but not a detriment. His class is very test-heavy though.

Dr. Horewood is a wonderful professor. His passion for history shines in this class (HIS 315K: United States History, 1492–1865), creating intriguing lectures that help one navigate the nuanced stories of US History. Also, he makes his lectures incredibly concise and emphasizes all of the key information, further helping one succeed in his class.

really fun guy, makes history engaging and clearly loves the subject. going to lectures is definitely necessary, but as long as you do the tests aren't too bad. he's a good lecturer, would take his class again.
Such a fun guy. Really great class, can tell he is passionate about his job. Would totally take again.

analysis.name: Jennifer Fritz
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 467 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The lectures are a complete waste of time and do next to nothing to prepare you for the exams. She is not a good lecturer yet requires her students to attend them for credit. The tests are either made to be confusing intentionally or perhaps they are a reflection of the lack of care and effort that this professor puts into her class.

Dr. Fritz is a really nice professor, and you can tell that she is very knowledgable in the subject, however, this class was SO HARD. She gives good lectures and provides a lot of information, but the tests are so specific/detail oriented that no matter how much I studied I still only did okay. Be prepared to learn/study a lot of information.

Horrible professor. Worst class I've taken at this campus. Tests are ten times more in depth than what she teaches or tells you to learn about. With no prior biology knowledge, I will more than likely be dropping the class. I am a biology major and will be changing my major because of this horrible professor. Would not recommend.

The Unsalty Honest Truth::: Her class is tailored towards students who are already familiar with Biology. Her lectures and study guides are easy to understand, however, the tests are very detailed and tricky. Thankfully, I figured this out early on and decided to drop before my GPA did. Please do not take a chance and risk being given an L.

Lectures are easy to understand. however the tests are much harder than she portrays. It is important to take the time and study regularly. Keep up with the lectures and material because you will be learning new and testable material up until the class day before the exam. She also makes a lot of awkward sex and alcohol jokes.

analysis.name: Bryon Henry
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining

Assignments can be somewhat long, but they are manageable. Exams are generally similar to the homework, so they are fair and not overly difficult. He also allows the final exam to replace the lowest midterm, which is helpful. Lectures are recorded, but the notes can be disorganized at times, which made them harder to follow.

He's great! Any chance you can take him, do it! Finals are usually optional and will replace a previous test grade. No other professor in CE will do that for you. He is very understanding and an all around great man.

Dr. Liljestrand is a very kind and caring person. He always checked with us if we were understanding the material.

There is decent amount of homework, but I would do it and understand it.

Go to class and ask questions.

Dr. Monaco was one of the best teachers Ive ever had at UT. He truly cares about us and wants us to succeed. Even at 8am I would look forward to class as his lectures were great. It's overall ok. Doesn't really keep you engaged during lectures, but is a very lenient grader. If you get a good partner the homework and project can be done easily. Exams are hard to fail.

This professor was amazing! This was one of the easier computer science classes I took, and I learned many things from it. He makes data analytics interesting and fun to learn and use. Just be on top of assignments and know concepts well. The tests are pretty easy. This professor is the GOAT.

BEST math prof at UT. Had her both semesters for Calc 1 for science majors. Love the way she teaches, she just makes everything make sense. Tests are fair based on what we've learned in class.

I really like Professor Mina. She is really caring and cares about your improvement in Korean. However, I think her lectures are a bit boring and that Professor Eunjoo's class is more engaging. That being said, you will be in good hands if you take Professor Mina's class.

Amazing at explaining such hard concepts. Very passionate about teaching each subject matter, which helps. Exam grading emphasizes precision. Go to OH to do the homework. Get good with complex numbers, transform tables, and conceptual understanding of applications (sampling, filters).

One of the better EE professors in the department. Very clear and covers all the information without going too much into proofs. Dr. Hall is a very nice professor, but his lectures were disorganized. He also relied heavily on the TA, who did not seem to care much about this class. analysis.name: Laura de Castro Quaglia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: As long as you keep up with the work, it's an easy A. If you miss a few tho, it's hard ot get back up on your feet. There was like 2-3 assignments a week and then tests every 4 weeks. Overall great experience for a summer class.

Easiest government credit. You watch lecture videos from O'Brien. Exams are so straightforward. Never used the textbook.
The average of every assignment was failing or close and her feedback was terrible

analysis.name: Qixing Huang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very dry lecturer. Did not provide a syllabus and never gave out a clear grading scheme. Tons of generous extra credit (A total of 24 extra points towards our final grade). Thought a lot of complex topics were trivial and did not explain them correctly. Often brushed over topics necessary to complete assignments. Hard tests but graded generously.

Covers difficult concepts, some of which are not explained in depth. Exams are very challenging but graded leniently. Assignments are challenging, but you get 12 slip days, extra credit opportunities, and they're not graded too harshly either. Uses MATLAB which is not ideal, but u have the option for python for later assignments iirc.

Dr. Huang is a nice guy. You go through a lot of material and a bunch of math derivations in lecture. But, projects were not too hard w/ a bunch of extra credit. Exams were pretty hard but graded leniently. I think this was his first semester teaching generative visual computing, but it was pretty good.

Topics are very dense, both for good and bad. Concepts often feel somewhat overwhelming, but you will doubtlessly learn a great deal about a great deal. Exams are very rough, but graded leniently. Assignments are moderately rough, but have plenty of extra credit. Brush up on your math and be prepared for slow lectures.

Class was graded off of 6 projects and 2 exams (tons of EC tho). Exams were difficult (mostly theory that was covered in slides) but graded very leniently. Projects (choice of matlab or python) were time consuming but covered really cool topics. Lectures that didn't involve linear algebra were pretty good, but the ones that did were a struggle.

analysis.name: Steven Rossmann
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved this class! Fun and slightly more creative, but not difficult. Exactly what an elective should be. Professor Rossmann has a lot of cool experience, and it was fun hearing his stories. Easy and fun A. Highly recommend.

He is the nicest and most flexible teacher I've had at UT. He cares for his student so much and will use his many connections in the industry to help you succeed and broaden your network. If you show up to class, you're going to do very well in his class.

Really enjoyed this class. Prof. Rossman clearly cares a lot about his students and made an effort to get to know all of us. I found lectures somewhat boring, but the concept of building a brand throughout the semester was pretty cool.
I would definitely take him again 10/10 recommend if you're looking for credit/a chill upper division elective.

Professor Rossmann is an amazing professor. He truly cares about his students and tries to get to know every single one. He is a great talker and is so funny. If you can take his class you really should!

I took the online version of this class and lectures were pretty boring. There is always one project and a group discussion due every week. The work is pretty easy but kinda just feels like busy work. The grading isn't strict either. He also provided a lot of extra credit opportunities.

analysis.name: Rebecca A. Zarate (RAZ)
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Best teacher I think I had at UT Austin. Made me seriously consider statistics as a career path. Don't worry if you don't know anything before the class, Zarate is easy to talk to & she gives great advice. If you put some effort/interest in the course, you will get a good grade!

Super in depth lecturer. Classes technically didn't have attendance taken but all the work we did was in class based, practically no outside work necessary. As long as she sees that you are trying you will get a good grade if you put the work in. Highly recomend

Extremely easy, one open-note benchmark quiz per class determines the majority of your grade. The course is interesting and engaging, but sleep is more interesting and engaging, so that's what I did during the lectures.

She was my course coordinator, and is very energetic in lectures as well as very accessible outside of class. A lot of times, her email reminders were the reason I was submitting assignments on time. I'm sure any course she teaches would be a great time.

RAZ was the course coordinator for my psy 301 class in addition to managing her other class this semester, and she navigated it like a champ. Her beautiful graphs and witty comments made the class that much more enjoyable. I would highly recommend taking any course she teaches, as she is bound to make it engaging and relevant.

analysis.name: Veena Ravishankar
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 73 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class is not designed to be beginner friendly. It gets increasingly difficult fast and there are many assignments due each week as homework, some right after test days. The coding assignments are difficult with the autograder which is super finickly and often gives 0's for timed out sessions. Be prepared to suffer. A lot of AI is involved.

The programming assignments get increasingly hard through the semseter. There are many TA's but they have not been particulary active in helping students who have trouble with sessions being timed out in Gradescope. All assignments are graded with the auto-grader and no partial credit is given if you mess up the output of the code.

I find it so hard to actually learn the concepts and be engaged in this class. The practice problems in the lectures are nothing like the quizzes or exams. I really wish I had chosen a different professor as someone who has absolutely zero coding experience. It's been really tough. This is supposed to be a beginner's course!!!!

Dr. Ravishankar cares a LOT about her students. She's a very good person. Her lectures can be confusing, but watching the pre-lecture videos and going over the solutions to the problem sets are more than enough to learn the content. The exams aren't too hard. The weekly quizzes can be very unforgiving with grading, but you do get 2 quiz drops.

She isn't as bad as everyone else is saying. She is unclear at times (especially if u ask questions), but going to office hours/costudies/etc. helps u get a good grasp on the material. her tests are the same as the other profs, and not that hard. quizzes are also not that hard, esp when u can have a cheat sheet on each quiz and exam.

analysis.name: Adrian Rodriguez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took it last fall, and thermo is a pretty harsh class, but Prof Rodriguez teaches the concepts very well, and his TAs were pretty approachable. The grading wasn't too punishing, and I was able to reach a B despite thinking I was barely gonna pass. Oh, also, he likes to bring snacks to every lecture, so that was pretty cool of him to do.

Dr. Rodriguez is great, and you can tell he wants his students to do well. Thermo is naturally a difficult class, but he definitely made it easier through his effort and availability. Weekly quizzes are based on one hw problem from the additional set, and make sure to use the ASME test bank to study for tests, as problems are often recycled.

It's Thermo; it will be difficult. However, Rodriguez is caring and communicative enough to lighten the mental load. We used an online textbook (ZyBooks) with participation (watch a few animations) and challenge (homework problems) activities built in. Study for weekly quizzes, cram for tests, and rest assured Rodriguez is there to help out.

It was Rodriguez's first time teaching this course, and I really appreciated his willingness to work with students to make the class a smoother ride. Thermo is a difficult class, but he provided many opportunities for extra credit and always asked for feedback. His lectures were engaging, and I enjoyed his class.
Dr. Rodriguez had the most organized Canvas page I have ever seen, and he makes expectations very clear. Super kind and approachable- would highly recommend for 318M

analysis.name: Stephanie Rivaux
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently

Professor Rivaux was a good professor, I didn't enjoy taking statistics but she was always helpful and a good resource when you needed her. Always willing to take the extra time to support students.
I would take this class again. Challenging, but the prof made it worth it.

She was great!! She was responsive to emails, and it was so clear that she cared about our success. She is always rooting for you, but the class goes from 0-100 after test 1. She's great, but the actual course content is kinda hard. She does give unlimited chances on hw, and thankfully the grading format means exams don't weigh as much. Loved her!

Dr. Rivaux is a great professor, very caring, and understanding. You put in what you get out of it, so if you stay on top of assignments (DO NOT FALL BEHIND) & (COME TO CLASS), you will flourish in this course. Attend office hours if need be and do not be afraid to ask questions in class or just email her she is very kind. 

Brooke W

This class is easy to do well in if you pay attention in class and take notes.

Ryfe is a great guy and does genuinely want to help, but his teaching style is very unique and takes getting used to. Office hours will help!

This is NOT an easy class. Professor Ryfe and his TAs will grade hard but Ryfe is easy to talk to & is always open for office hours. very enjoyable class! lectures got boring sometimes, but the information given was useful! some of the test questions felt a bit random/unfair at times, but he offers a lot of extra credit opportunities. pretty simple assignments though. he does allow a cheat sheet on the exams, although it does not help that much LOL
This class definitely wasn't as hard as I thought. Professor Ryfe explains the concepts really well, but you have to be able to attend almost every lecture to understand the material.

analysis.name: Jahanett Ramirez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: She is my fav! Dr. Ramirez is incredibly knowledgeable and so kind. Her lectures are very informative and the group projects each class help us practice the info. This was an extremely impactful course everyone should take.

I took Dr. Ramirez for her UGS class, Hope Amidst Change. She is very knowledgeable about the study of grief, using the biopsychosocial model to help us understand grief throughout different stages of life. She cares a lot about her students and is willing to work with students when they need leniency.

I took Dr. Ramirez for my UGS class Hope Amidst Change. She is honestly so sweet and caring. Attendance is required, and she does assign a lot of readings. However, the class is fairly easy and informational. I would definitely recommend this UGS.

Professor Ramirez did a really good job of holding space for us as a class as we explored the really difficult topic of loss and grief. This course opened my eyes to a lot of things on a societal level in how we respond to loss and grief, and how, as a collective, we could benefit greatly from having more compassion for ourselves and each other.

Dr. Ramirez is an amazing professor and an expert in so many disciplines. The lectures in the course are very thorough and easy to follow. This translates to the assignments being easy to complete and making good grades feasible.

analysis.name: Mike Scott

Download the chrome extension Mike's Got Style to get an A in the class

analysis.name: Alan Sager
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

Thinking about Law School? Highly recommended

I've never taken a class like Sager's class before... The students who take up end up taking him over and over because he is such an amazing and knowledgeable professor. I am not a fan of Sager's teaching style. He is not very engaging to listen to and does little to explain cases. Don't expect to leave this course with a deeper understanding of any topics or cases. Often, it felt as though even he was confused and didn't have a clear line of reasoning. I got by with knowledge from past classes and the curve.

Despite all of the negative reviews on RMP, Dr. Sager is the best pre-law professor at UT. Do the readings, participate in class, and talk to him and you'll be fine. He has right wing views, but will listen to your opinion and truly consider it. If you're not pre law, don't take this class. It's way too difficult to not pay off.

analysis.name: Ann Thijs

Dr. Thijs is a nice person but shes not a good lecturer. SWEETEST MAN. guys he is SO SWEET. make sure to come to class bc there will be in class participation assignments and participation is part of ur grade. also don't forget to do instapolls, and don't half ass the project portoflio! TAs and prof are super nice overall, great class

There was weekly HW from the textbook, never took more than an hour. 3 tests and a final, found the tests generally hard, but was very generous with the grading. analysis.name: Alfred Tuley

Best professor at UT so far. He makes chemistry accessible to all. Highly recommend his office hours to get advice for quizzes and exams. He offers so many resources from himself and the chem dept. so many resources, extra credit is easy to get and max 30pts. gives everything needed to do well on exams. ngl acid and bases will cook you alive (im not kidding) but if you study you'll pass (all of our grades dropped by a letter). quizzes in class right after exam, must self study (his only downfall). GO TO OFFICE HOURS

analysis.name: Thanasis Kinias

Assigned a lot of readings, can do perfectly fine without doing them. Took feedback mid-semester and immediately applied it, reduced readings. Midterm exam was easy, have access to all slides and notes. Great class for the UGS credit and easy A.

analysis.name: Arban Uka

He always brings up interesting facts + engages students to give their opinion, even if the topic is not that hot (like differential equations). Would take again though I've graduated.

very smart and hardworking. very fair evaluation. always ready to help students. a bit messy and always busy (cause he finds time for everyone). kind and polite to extreme. sometimes hard to follow his genius track of thoughts :( . Still among best profs ive ever had
He details the math step by step, always.

analysis.name: Jason Urban

The class critique process is always so fun and helpful, and I have produce a lot of works Im proud with for my portfolio. Although the workload I can be a bit overwhelming sometimes, but all projects are fun.

I cannot stress enough how much I loved taking a litho class with Jason, he explained everything clearly and gave thorough demos. He does expect you to have good attendance and to actually work during class but it's worth it in order to understand everything that's taught. Definitely take a print class with him if you can!

He is one of the best professor I ever had! He is Inspirational, reasonable, friendly, caring, approachable, and very helpful. He always give clear guidelines when introducing projects. During discussions, he give you comments that can make you go further and want to go further.
nice funny smart cool guy. would recommend. Advice: don't be slovenly.

analysis.name: Etienne Vouga
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I really wanted to like this class due to my interest in competitive programming and preparing for coding interviews. The exam structure is extremely harsh with no partial credit (even though the syllabus says so) making it significantly easy to get a 0. The class is also mostly Turing students making it easy to get imposter syndrome.

I also had him for CS395T Physical Simulation. He is hands down the best CS professor I've had. His lectures are engaging and clear. His classes are also some of the hardest I've ever taken, with lots of tough but rewarding projects. But if you put in the effort, he is a pretty lenient grader. He does open-ended final projects in his classes.

The professor is a good teacher, but the exam grading is extremely unforgiving. It follows a strict 0, 50, or 100 scale. The partial credit mentioned in the syllabus is that you receive a 50% if you pass every single test case for one question, but you fail at least one test case for the other.
Find the bug, and do at least two leetcode problems a week. Did not quite like the amount of work for a 1 hour class.

All around amazing class. Lectures are clear, interesting and informative. Vouga is always available on Discord to answer questions. He's also just a really nice person and very easy to talk to. The content is hard but there's tons of support available. Projects are hard but fun and super rewarding. Lecture quizzes can be tricky but there's no exam

analysis.name: Viranga Perera
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 102 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Worst class I've ever taken. He overcomplicates topics which makes them seem harder than they actually are. Doesn't give partial credit back despite some past reviews saying he does. Use the homework to study, but expect to teach most of this class to yourself. I also never took physics before this which I think put me at a disadvantage

His summer course is fast paced, but his lectures are great and he makes sure that students understand the content before moving on. There's a decent amount of hw, but it helps to solidify understanding and to prepare for the exams. Course organization is solid and the teaching team is active on Ed. This is likely the easiest UT physics gets.

It's a lab and the lab is one of the worst designed pieces of education conceived. Its all stats and uncertainty. the whole point of physics is that its not engineering, its ideal, but this class is 5% doing physics concepts and 95% propagating uncertainty. Doesn't make a lick of sense. Perera is great though

Perera is an amazing lecturer, and his class is clearly structured and easy. The midterms are multiple choice and similar in difficulty to homework. If there are bad questions, Perera will drop them to ensure the exams result in grades that reflect the knowledge of the material.

The class is a basic introduction to engineering physics. The topics taught are the same as high school physics with a few changes. Dr. Perera wants his students to succeed and has designed his course so that most students will get A's. Homework will take a bit of time, but it isn't too hard; exams are just like the homework. Best UT Physics Prof!

analysis.name: Victor Eijkhout
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining

be careful with his dark magic. Overall, this is a horrible class that I wanted to drop out since day one, but I had no other options to choose.

Hard to understand, very old school, and not a good lecturer

analysis.name: Vaibhav Bahadur

Awesome, teacher would take this college class again.

Boring lectures to help prepare with the lab. Occasional quizzes and a short exam. Doesn't really help prep for lab. Overall, not super necessary or detrimental to doing well in the lab portion of the course.

His class was very disorganized. He would quiz over material learned in class that day, giving us no time to study or ask questions, and the midterm was not a good representation of the class material. He also canceled office hours every week. Lectures were boring and low effort. Heat Transfer lab is also a lot of work in general so fair warning.
He is very good i would take him 1000 times.

analysis.name: Volker  Bromm

Weekly quizzes were pretty easy. The lectures are really fast and I didn't actually learn much, but I could gather enough to do the projects and quizzes. The HWs were a bit confusing but his OH were helpful. Super easy grading on the group projects, you present to him in his office and submit a super short paper. Wish I learned more. Good blowoff.

Super knowledgeable, passionate, kind, and willing to help if you need it or just want to discuss astronomy in general. Works hard to make sure the class isn't stressful grade wise and gives intriguing lectures.
Very easy class, would take again. Accent is a little strong but he cares about the subject. 2 very easy exams, most of the grade is based off of 4 easy homeworks.

Very knowledgeable professor. His lectures are very interesting and you can tell he's passionate about what he's teaching. Weekly easy quizzes and 3-4 problem sets for the entire semester that are not hard at all. No midterms or final , replaced by two fairly simple group projects.

analysis.name: Kurt Weyland
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

The exams and quizzes are all essay based. Loved him, but wouldn't take it again.

Don't take this class if you're wanting an A, the best grade you can receive is honestly a B. Graded on 3 quizzes and 3 exams (no final) and the TA has no clear grading criteria. I went to office hours because his grading was either really high or really low; couldn't explain to me why I got that grade. Doesnt post grades throughout the whole sem.

I really enjoyed Dr. Weyland's class; his lectures are extremely interesting, and it's clear he cares about what he does. That being said, I'm pretty sure I'll end up with a B because your grade is based solely on exams. That would be fine if the tests weren't essays and the TAs were nicer graders, but alas, we can't all get what we want.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU'RE NOT WILLING TO READ OR AREN'T INTERESTED IN GOVERNMENT
Dr. Weyland is an amazing lecturer, but he also asks a lot from his students in terms of reading and grading. Only 3 quizzes and 3 exams throughout the semester, which are graded harshly by the TA
If you don't like reading and can't write, I suggest staying away

It's not worth it. I sold my soul to get an A in this course. The fear that you're going to fail the test/quiz because of a minor mistake really takes away from enjoying the class content. The readings are so long and you're expected to take the smallest details away from them. Don't take it if you're trying to check off your core requirement.

analysis.name: Andrei Straumanis
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

review_highlights.comment: During my three years at UT-Austin I had always enjoyed my professors and excelled in their classes... that was until I made the regrettable mistake of registering for a course with this egotistical man who has the nerve to call himself a 'professor.' You can throw all sanity and well-being out the window if you plan to be a student of his. Don't.
Grades tough and tends to lose his bike.

Dr. Straumanis fails to understand that everyone learns differently because he is so set on his way. POGIL works great when BALANCED with a traditional lecture. POGIL is meant to reinforce ideas, not cause mental breakdowns every week due to unfair quizzes. Quizzes dont accurately represent material and have unreasonable time constraints.

One I asked him a question during class because I was confused. The answer I received was "I think you are confused about something deeper, I am going to go help other students that need me." analysis.name: Stephen Walls

If you're an ADV major like me take 345 & 344 before or alongside and STUDY.. you'll be fine!

Professor Walls is so knowledgable and educated on the class he instructs. analysis.name: William Best

Prof. Best is an amazing lecturer, and he knows why most students are taking his class, so he makes it as fun and engaging as he can. I would recommend this as a science credit for sure, one of the best classes I've taken here at UT.

He knows most people taking this class are not majoring in anything related to astronomy. Still genuinely one of the sweetest, most passionate professors I've ever met. analysis.name: Xuan Ho

High work load and there is 1 paper worth 30% of your grade, the reading is nonsense

Easy 2-page film reviews that once you get the formula down you can just repeat every week and she gave me 10/10 on almost every one. You WILL be paired up with a partner where you need to lead the discussion, but only once. Readings are practically unintelligible- and she knows this. The only bad thing was the strict attendance policy. 3 absences then letter grade drop.

Lectures are pretty pointless. He teaches straight out the textbook. First two exams werent bad and he does a decent enough job of telling you general problems on tests. But, the final was awful. Had an entire problem that was never taught in class and genuinely no one knew how to do.

Weekly homework with a quiz during discussion. The quiz was a homework problem with different numbers. There were 2 tests and a final. Very nice guy as well.

analysis.name: Xiaofen Hamilton

Fitness For Life is such an easy class. You don't need to buy the textbook its basically useless. There is no exams. analysis.name: Mindy Xiaolan

Super nice but soft spoken. Was hard to pay attention during lectures and usually never finished her lectures. She did have the high A distribution though so maybe she gives a nice curve. I think she's also retiring so wont be teaching again not sure though.

FIN 367 is just an incredibly hard class, but professor Xiaolan does a pretty good job explaining concepts and making sure to answer any questions students have. Our class averages were significantly higher than other classes. Overall solid option for 367.

analysis.name: Yunlan Zhang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Zhang taught the class very well, and attending the lecture helped out a lot when preparing for the midterms. 2 midterms, one gets dropped. Get equation sheet for each exam and always has practice test. There are participation quizzes but they're pretty much for extra credit. She goes fast, but not bad. Notes are posted.

For the most part, the homework was straightforward, as were the labs. Her lectures cover everything relevant to the assignments, but she usually moves too quickly to take notes. This is made worse by the fact that the annotated lectures are not posted. Still, as long as you follow the material and read the textbook, this class is an easy A.

Prof Zhang is not good at teaching. She makes everything super complicated when in reality you need to know a few simple formulas. Her exams are just like the practice exams, you can bring a 1 pg sheet from home, and she has pop quizzes by flipping a coin in class. I really don't like how she teaches but the content is fine if you look it up.

analysis.name: Soo Hyun Yang
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work

Dr Yang is genuinely such a kindhearted person and wants you to understand the content you are learning in the lab. Dr. Yang is genuinely the best professor I've had in all my years of learning, she is so compassionate and really great at explaining complex biochem topics in simple ways. She is THE best professor at UT Austin.

analysis.name: Ramesh Yerraballi

Best prof for 306 w/o a doubt, considering both lectures and grading. He explains in such a meticulous manner that anyone can understand. Dr. Y is a really nice guy. He wants everyone to succeed and clearly cares. His lectures are always chill, and I feel that he does a really good job of taking difficult topics and breaking them down. analysis.name: Bill Wolesensky
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

review_highlights.comment: Literally the best professor I've ever had. He is genuine, caring, and really wants your success. ALWAYS makes time for students, NEVER makes you feel dumb or inadequate for not understanding something. One of the best guys I know. I wish he were my father.
Best teacher ever. Honestly so nice and extremely helpful. This was one of the easiest classes i've ever taken at UT but was also totally enjoyable. 10/10 would recommend

WantEasyA?-dont take him. Although hard, this has been my favorite class so far and I truly believe this class taught me how to (actually)learn. Bill truly cares about his students,is always open to questions,and inspires us to learn to think critically by truly understanding concepts instead of just memorizing. AmazingProfessor+WorthTheCourseRigor

peak professor, highkey goat. very caring and passionate about student success, empowerment, and understanding. 3 exams each with 2 parts, indiv. (60%) and group (40%). very clear and concise explanations of concepts, and easy to approach. very kind and respectful professor. literally best professor ive taken, genuinely kindhearted.

He did assign a lot of homework but often times would drop off sections as he wouldn't get to lecture that content in class. He empowered me as a student and I put effort into his class.

analysis.name: Tim Yeh

review_highlights.comment: I'm being so serious, as a STEM major, I think this is the best class/professor I've had and will remain that way for my foreseeable academic career. Real-world applicability of knowledge, genuinely easy to learn and helpful knowledge that can improve many life circumstances, and best of all, the field trips and overall genuine class culture!

The easiest class I took all semester. I got a lot of good information though, and it was nice to check in on our well-being throughout the semester. The class was VERY relaxed, and there aren't exams, so paying attention is fun but optional. Attendance is mandatory though, but it's not hard to get motivation to go because it's a fun class.

If you need a UGS class, TAKE THIS ONE, IT'S THE EASIEST AND BEST ONE. Most of the grade is just attendance. We had field trips and talked about medicine, which ended up being really helpful information when flu season came around. My friend was jealous I was in this class compared to her UGS, cause it's just that easy.

TAKE THIS CLASS. Prof Acosta is super nice, she cares about her students, she's lenient on due dates and she's a good teacher. There are easy weekly readings/discussion posts from a book she provides, 2 papers, and some easy projects. We also went on field trips around campus and she ends class early. The material is interesting too. A PERFECT UGS.

Dean Acosta is one of the best professors that I have ever had. She is extremely caring and genuinely cares if you are struggling or not and will do her best to help you. The semester is super fun and filled with museum trips, pilates and cycling classes, and very interesting lectures. She is an extremely accomplished and real person and is great!!

analysis.name: Ahmad Agbaria
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He was the worst professor I ever had. He changed the rubric on the tests with no clear direction on anything on paper. Avoid at all costs if trying to find a good government class as the GOV366T label for this class is misleading due to this class being solely a history class. He is terrible with technology and does not respond to emails.

The professor is nice and willing to help answer some questions, but wow, his class is extremely unorganized. He posts nothing but the readings on canvas. He goes very fast during lectures and doesnt post the lecture slides on canvas. Doesnt do reviews for the midterm/final. You wont really know your grade until after the semester is over.

Worst class I've taken at UT. "Lectures" are unorganized and rushed slideshows with dense slides that aren't even shared. No Canvas use. Expectations for writing assignments are unclear. Grades rely heavily on the exam and final (no final review guide either). Avoid unless you have prior knowledge on the topic or grad-level writing.

AVOID. While he held office hours, he lied about pretty much anything he said regarding the course format. My grade was up in the air until the final week of the class so that was a bummer too. Sure he was nice but did not teach properly. His lectures were all over the place and for a history class there was no chronological order.

Terrible professor due to his constant rants during the lectures which causes him to rush his lectures. He constantly changes the class format and rubrics verbally and does not post lecture slides or a final review despite rushing. Office hours do not help at all as he constantly changes what he says so cannot trust office hours.

analysis.name: Charity-Joy Acchiardo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I thought the class was fine. The Kahoots are a little annoying at the beginning, but you get used to them as the semester progresses. Exams aren't too difficult... just read the textbook and go over the inquisitives (homework assignments). Lectures are solid as well.

Her class was not that difficult, but she is pretty unprofessional and often says weirdly inappropriate things in class. I'm glad it was online, because dealing with her in person would not be pleasant. It wasn't even really pleasant online tbh. The class is ok, but I would recommend finding another section or professor to enroll in.
Some assignments took me a long time but the tests were an accurate reflection of them. Just study and you'll pass with ease.
She is completely inaccessible. I tried many times to get ahold of her through email and she never responded.  Really disappointing class experience.

Fun&Silly class. I had 2 professors: Mateer and Acciardo. The textbook doesn't worth purchasing because contains a bunch of specific examples. Class participation: kahoots & puzzlers. Homework: InQuizitives. 2 open book\note Exams(50 points each).Office Hours: case solutions with minimum explanations. If u rn't familiar with ECO, it will be tough.

analysis.name: Ahmed Shamim
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Because he was leaving this semester, it felt as if his class was sloppily composed due to his lack of passion for UT. He's great at what he does, but he put the bare minimum into this class's structure. However, he is great at explaining Bangla for non-native speakers and was such a kind and hilarious professor. Smart man, just very disorganized!
Dr. Shamim is a great teacher. He is fun, caring, and laid back. The workload is also very reasonable and slow-paced as he wants everyone to learn on the same page. Take him!

Professor Shamim is adaptable in his teaching methods. If a student is struggling with a particular part of the Bangla language, he will make sure that the student will eventually understand it. This ranges from the alphabet, general grammar, vocabulary, to even dialects. Not only that, he is available outside class if you ask him. Adore this guy!

analysis.name: Ahmed Helal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Take his class. Gives a heavy curve and material isn't complicated
He is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are clear and beneficial to the class. He engages his students with understandable materials. Would recommend everyone to take his class!

analysis.name: Shaherzad Ahmadi
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I did not think she was great at all. Her lectures were very sporadic and they did not follow a clear progression. She had way too many assignments and expectations for a lower division history course (over 20 pages worth of papers for the semester). She was available outside of class but she had clear favorites.

Liked her approach but lectures can be quite hard to follow. Tends to assume everyone is on the same page based on a few vocal students. However it was still pretty easy to make an A in the class, and I felt I didn't need to show up to make the grade. Essay assignments are the majority of the grade and can be done largely independently.
Pretty easy grader, I feel like if you put in the effort you'll make an A. "Shaz" knows her stuff.

Her lectures were highly informative and she encourages independent reading when writing papers. Shaherzad is extremely knowledgable and will guide you in the right direction. If you like the course title and topic, she's the person to take it with!

Like another reviewer said, Shaz's lectures lack any sense of cohesion. She jumps around in topics, time periods and regions frequently. Judging by the lack of attendance everyday, I would say most people agree with me when I say that this class was a waste of time. Shaz is very smart, but a bad teacher.

analysis.name: Ahmed Siddiqi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This course is an introductory survey of the political philosophy of several philosophers throughout the western world. Those who are uninterested in reading antiquated texts pertaining to political philosophy should not take this course. This course contains substantial reading. This course was incredibly thought-provoking.
Professor Siddiqi is very thorough. His class is difficult for a lower division government class, but I found it enjoyable. If you don't like philosophy, you may want to steer clear.

Great guy, great professor. Class is clear-cut & minimalist: do the daily readings, come ready to discuss/debate, and complete the two assigned papers. Final grade comprised of few assignments, w/ each paper weighted HEAVILY. Can be a tough grader w/ sorta unrealistic standards, but final is easy. Very intellectual, pensive guy - great to talk to.

He is really good at leading discussion based courses and helps keep class discussions from getting too tangential.  I didn't do a lot of the readings near the end because I was swamped and got recked by the final.  I liked him though, wish I could take again and try harder.   Really cool to talk with during office hours.

He's a great professor, and the class was a lot of fun. I'm a huge history nerd, and I really learned a lot and gained new insight into politics and philosophy. The reading and the class discussions were great too.

analysis.name: Dena Afrasiabi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is A LOT of work, especially if you don't start with any Persian. Very homework-heavy, flipped-classroom, so you work through the textbook on your own, class is for practice and tests. However, this professor really cares about student outcomes and tries her best to help. You could also see the class improving throughout the semester.

Great class and will really teach you Farsi if you commit to it. Simply doing the homework and making sure to get it right will basically get you literate. It is a time commitment, 2hrs three times a week and it takes about 2hrs to do homework every night too, upside is all the other assignments also take 2hrs so nothing is killer. She is also nice

The class is a mess. First time teaching and she's just as lost as us. Two papers and a presentation account for 80% of your final grade. She doesn't know how to use a computer or any kind of technology. The class organization is absent. Due dates are listed on the syllabus and make sure to remember them cuz no one will remind you. DON'T TAKE THIS!

analysis.name: Omoniyi Afolabi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Afolabi is an interesting professor. I learned a lot from his UGS302 Brazilian Studies class, and the small class format made it more engaging and fun. He can be hard to understand with his accent and his comments on papers dont always make sense, but he is very knowledgable about Brazil. One of the best classes I've taken at UT.

You do not need to read anything!!! he spends all of lecture going through the summary of that happened over the "assigned reading" and gets really off track, but ALL of the assignemnts are super easy and the prompts are so broad that you can just research and write instead of reading the dense material. HE GRADES ON GRAMMAR OVER CONTENT!!!

Dr. Afolabi is a very enthusiastic professor! His class is interesting and straightforward but can be pretty disorganized at times. Many papers are assigned, but the class does carry a writing flag. He grades mainly based on grammar instead of the essays' actual content. Once you understand his writing style, getting A's on the papers is very easy

Enthusiastic, fun, and interesting, but a lot of the content covered in class is unnecessary to do well. Once you understand how he grades papers will be easy A's, he is not tech savvy but genuinely cares about his students and loves teaching

Much of this class is saved by the interesting topic and the professor who presents the information. His regular enthusiasm and willingness to describe a culture which, at least to me, was novel proved to be highly valuable. However, his critiques of writing are at best technical and the stylistic and argumentative feedback was distinctly limited.

analysis.name: Afroze Shaikh
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took the EDP Career Planning course over the summer and enjoyed it! We learned so much—I especially loved our textbook since it was actually fun to read. There were reading/content quizzes, assignments graded on effort because they were focused on your personal career planning, and an interview of someone in your field of interest for the final.

Dr. Shaikh made her expectations for the class very clear and graded content fairly. She truly cares about each one of her students and is always open to talk about any concerns. This class did not require a ton of effort, but you should still put an honest effort into the assignments.

Dr. Shaikh is a caring and compassionate professor. She is incredibly knowledgeable and assigns relevant and thoughtful assignments. With fair effort, this class is very doable and enjoyable. She is wonderful!

analysis.name: Afsar Mohammad
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Presently, I'm in Prof. Afsar's "Modern India and Literature" class. I'm so lucky to get into the class which has a long wait list. And,Prof. Afsar never disappointed until now. He is passionate, fun and clarity of thought. Wonderful insights into the materials.

He is a great professor with lots of passion for his subject! I enjoyed every minute of his class. If you keep up with the work and go to class then you should have no problem getting the grade you want. How much you get out of the class depends on how much you put in!Make sure you meet him outside of class because he is a great person to get to kn

This is the third class I've taken with Afsar. He's a great professor. The subject material is always very interesting, and he doesn't shy away from controversial or 'awkward' topics. He always brings humor to the discussion as well. He is very interested in students' progress and is always willing to meet to discuss papers,etc.

Taking Prof. Afsar's new class "Pilgrimage in South Asia." Heard a lot about Prof. Afsar before, but this is my first class with him. Really enjoyable! Extremely fascinating/ real research experiences! Accessible Professor, loves to spend more time with the students. Values the student voice and he has a great smile!

Really cares for the progress of the student. Makes every class a memorable experience with lot of stories. I've been taking his courses continuosly. Specifically his course on South Asian Novel is my favorite.

analysis.name: Ahmed Gheith
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 99 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Gheith actually cares about teaching, and is very good at it. There are projects every week, ranging from fairly easy (3 hrs) to very hard (25hrs). I've taken 3 classes with Gheith so far, and if he taught any more, I'd take them too.

Gheith is an amazing teacher who knows the material cold (lectures with no notes) and is very nice in office hours. That said, the class is extremely tough, and of the 14 projects, I and most people I know put in 40+ hours of effort on 4 of them. Find a solid group to work with and plan carefully before writing any code, and you will do well

He's an excellent professor, but OS is genuinely one of the hardest classes you can take. It will be really difficult for you. Yes, even you. I'd take it again, but only because of the friends I made in it. I literally lost 15lbs because I was working so much on it. Really. It's 50-60 hrs/week. If you do take it, don't take anything else hard.
Helpful professor and knows the material inside & out. However, his CS 429 Summer class was insanely challenging. The assignments and quizzes were brutal. I think half the class ended up dropping.

One of those classes where you come out with a profound jump in mastery even if you only got a C-. The lectures are an absolute delight, he has immense understanding of the material. Likely the hardest programming projects you will do during your time at UT, but also thoroughly instructive and insightful. May have to no-life this class to do well.

analysis.name: Scott Aaronson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Knowledgable but cant teach. Explains things too fast, doesnt realize students take longer to understand. Assumes complex things to be common sense. I attended every lecture but most of my learning came from elsewhere. Grading criteria was "1/3rd of class gets an A", left me in shock at my grade at the end. Impossible tests and hw, TAs confused too
For QIS, I thought the content was very interesting, and lectures were good and worth attending. Exams sometimes had unclear questions, but other than that, not terribly difficult.

I overall liked the structure of the course—the online textbook had clear explanations and the psets were difficult but not impossible, and I felt like I learned a lot. However, the exams were extremely difficult and worth a large percentage of the grade. You have to be good at algos and solving new problems in a test environment to do well.

Aaronson is knowledgeable about QIS, but is meh at teaching. His office smelled like a dead animal, until I realized it was his breath... He gets annoyed when students cant follow along with his occasional fast paced rants where he hardly touches base. His exams were unfair and took off too many points for small mistakes. Not worth taking ECE 379K.
Don't be fooled by the difficulty of the homework because the exams are infinitely harder and more unfair.

analysis.name: Aaron Rochlen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He asked for my number when I asked for the major project rubric. Very vague on what he expects and often changes it before the due dates. Experiences differ depending on your TA, but if you enjoy the subject, it's not too bad.

There are easier UGS courses, but the live concerts are nice. There's a $40 textbook of random online articles you will rarely use. Many of the assignment instructions have typos and are unorganized, but they expect your paper to be perfect. It seems like the TAs grade randomly and nitpick at random things that the rubric never specified.

He's a hit or miss depending on your personality - I didn't really like him, but you interact more with your TA than him if you don't participate in lectures. He will call you out to read a slide or answer a question if he notices you're not paying attention though. I felt his lectures were kind of slow paced so I wasn't that engaged.

Take the class if you need the credit but honestly professor is a lot to deal with. TAs will make the class much better. Was definetly not a fan of him and so weren't a lot of other people. He might like you he might not and his opinion stays the entire semester.
