He knows what he's talking about and the class is never boring - but he's definitely a hit or miss personality for sure. If the subject matter genuinely interests you, I'd say go for it, because you generally spend more time with your TA in this class than with him.

analysis.name: Aaron Sandel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: [UGS: History of Friend VS Foe] I had Dr. Sandel for my UGS and I loved the class! It was so chill, we just had in class discussions on what love or friendship is, etc. Dr. Sandel seems really passionate about his studying of chimpanzees and it was rlly interesting to hear about his work in Africa. If you want a light + fun UGS, take this class!

Least scientific science course I have ever taken--Dr. Sandel is a joke. I genuinely didn't learn a thing all semester, I just listened to classmates debate about nothing in particular. Easy enough class I suppose, I didn't do anything besides free writes and making sticky note maps. There was no structure and even less learning. Waste of time.
The only reason I didn't hate Ant301. He went slow and made it easy to understand the topic!

(This review is for his UGS 302 class, there was just no way to select that on RMP)

Dr. Sandel is super kind and caring! His class was very easy, and basically, a guaranteed A if you attended the classes (attendance matters a lot). The actual subject, how chimpanzees make friends and enemies, was pretty interesting, although a little confusing.

OO OOH EE AH AH!!! These are the sounds of the Ngogo chimps that we studied in Professor Sandel's UGS 302 class. In this class, I made so many lasting social bonds. This class is my fav class I've taken so far in college, and Dr. Sandel was super nice & caring. This class changed my life. Would definitely take again. Attendance is mandatory.

analysis.name: Aaron Tugendhaft
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Tugendhaft was frequently available to students and was engaging in every single class. Each day was an insightful discussion with peers that garnered a deeper understanding of the material. I absolutely recommend taking any class by Professor Tugendhaft, you will not be disappointed.

Aaron structures his class for the sole purpose of you actually learning something. His class is not designed to put you under immense stress or anxiety about grades, its really all absorbing the subject matter. Even if you are struggling for whatever reason, related to the class or not, he will help you out. His lectures are very enjoyable.

Aaron is the best professor I've ever had at UT. He is an extremely talented, engaging lecturer and the first I've ever had who I feel legitimately cares about his students' academic progress. I'm taking another class with him next semester!

i'm sick of the aaron hate he is so awesome! he's so funny and incredibly smart and adapted what is usually very convoluted and complex material into a really interesting and easy format. i thought i was going to HATE this class--i could not have been more wrong! i loved the readings and the material and prof tugendhaft made it so much fun!

Essays are graded by the TA (who gave great feedback for improvement after I scheduled a meeting), but Dr. Tugendhaft requires a meeting prior to the submission of your essay. Ultimately, you get in what you put out—he expects you to read and come to class prepared, and he can often tell if students haven't been engaging with the assigned readings.

analysis.name: Aaron Moses
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Moses is a very passionate lecturer and cares a lot about his subject. There aren't a lot of assignments, however the exams are lengthy and challenging (the exams ARE open note). We had a 7 hour period to take the midterm and it took me 6 hours. The midterm has 9 essay questions, and the exams require a pretty good grasp of the content.

Professor Moses is an incredibly sweet person who knows a lot and cares about this subject. If you take detailed notes you should be fine but  be warned the tests take around 5-6 hours. They are open note but the questions can be quite hard, also have 9 essay questions. if you don't like art history then this class is def not the vapa for you.

Professor Moses is an incredible lecturer and is clearly passionate about the material. He made me genuinely interested in art history. However, the exams are brutal and both took me at least 4 hours (2 exams, 15% each of your grade). They're open note but 9 essay questions can be taxing. There are 5-6 other writing assignments besides the exam.

He's super passionate and it was interesting, but man, those exams were brutal. You have a long period to complete them (like all day) but they take like 4-5 hours and they're not easy. At some point, writing essays (something I'm very good at!) became physically difficult because I'd been at it for so long. Some other assignments, but not many.

Professor Moses' ARH 303 was very interesting and an easy VAPA. We had two tests that were open note and a few short writing assignments. The tests were easy if you paid attention to the lectures and took notes on the starred topics on the powerpoint slides. There is a textbook, but the lectures are so in-depth you don't have to read it or buy it.

analysis.name: Aaron Baker
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Exams are 30% each for a total of 90%. Difficult but fair tests similar to practice probs and HW. His lectures tended to be a panic-y period where I frantically wrote what he wrote to keep up. Tests weren't too bad as it only included a few topics from lecture -- most of what you learn won't be tested over, but you cant know that before-hand.

Transport is a difficult subject, but Dr Baker really takes the time to explain concepts that people have questions about, and he seems to have a lot of empathy for his students. The exams are fair, and the homework and in-class questions are adequate to prepare you for them. Definitely attend lectures; there is new content covered every day.
His exams are very hard and the averages for those are usually between 65 to 70%, but he gives a really good curve.

analysis.name: Adriana Rizk
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Adriana's enthusiasm for teaching truly stands out. She sets high expectations in a way that is encouraging rather than forceful, creating an environment where students feel motivated to grow. She allows young students to discover music for themselves, helping them develop discipline and autonomy at such a young age. Thank you for this experience!

Adriana is a wonderful teacher. It's impressive to see someone so young balance dual majors while demonstrating such maturity and intuition when working with children. She brings both professionalism and warmth to her teaching, creating a positive and engaging environment for her students. For the kids classroom felt like a room full of friends.

I had the opportunity to take private lessons with Adriana, and she is an incredibly patient, organized, and thoughtful teacher. She approaches each lesson with creativity and is able to adapt her teaching to meet students where they are, which makes the learning process both comfortable and motivating.

analysis.name: Ari Adut
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Adut is kind, approachable, and a very skilled lecturer. Attendance isn't mandatory BUT coming to class helps a ton, especially if you do not do the readings. Three tests count for 100% of your grade but they are straightforward.This class is a breeze as long as you pay attention, take notes, and go to the review sessions.

This class was probably the easiest class I have taken in university, although it can be boring at times. Dr. Adut is a very kind person, so the class felt very relaxed. I would definitely take again.

Prof Adut is very knowledgable/passionate about what he teaches. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you show up and take good notes then you will do quite well on his tests. The course was made up of 3 written exams, no final.

Honestly, I don't advocate skipping class but if you were to only show up to the review and memorized it, you'd pass with a B. No joke. Don't bother buying the book, NEVER miss review day, but don't buy the book.

Dr. Adut was a great professor and lecturer, wanting his students to constantly participate. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you skip class you will miss all of the information on the exams. Don't bother buying the books, I never needed to read them because Dr. Adut was so good at explaining the information. Take this class!

analysis.name: Chris Aarons
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Aarons is hands down the best professor I've ever had in college. I have never learned more in any other class than I have in this class. His lectures are fun & really interesting. He sends out surveys to his students and really takes feedback & caters to what you need throughout the semester. If you have the chance to take him, DO IT!

Prof Aarons is by far one of the best professors I have had at UT. Taking Digital MKT with him impacted me in many ways - landing an internship, growing in knowledge, and being challenged to do my best work. He is an inspiring lecturer, hilarious, and gives priority to help his students even on weekends. His class will change your life! TAKE!

- THOUSANDS of dollars worth of AMAZING guest lecturers? Check. - Learning real-world skills that you can apply immediately? Check. - This class alone is worth an entire semester's tuition alone? CHECK. AND. MATE. You are doing yourself a disservice if you aren't going to take this class. Put your heart into this class and you will thrive.

Chris was the best professor I had at McCombs BY FAR. He is so caring & wise & willing to do anything to help his students & better their learning experience. I'll carry what I learned in his class with me for the rest of my professional life. He will also casually and humbly drop things like how he met Travis Scott or Amazon is one of his clients.

Aarons is hilarious, & the best professor ever!! It may seem like his instructions are vague, but it is all to help you think for yourself & unlock your full potential. He is always available to chat in office hours or even over the phone if u are confused, & his main priority is to make sure his students succeed! Lectures are also super engaging!

analysis.name: Adam Clulow
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Clulow is an excellent lecturer and professor. This course is graded by quite a few components which can pile up fast if you're not prepared. You have 3 free absences throughout the semester, and Dr. Clulow is readily available to work with students on extensions, extra credit, etc. Highly recommend for an overview of Japanese martial history.

Professor Clulow is an amazing professor who obviously cares a lot about the material he teaches. His lectures are engaging, funny, and in-depth. Most readings he makes accessible through Canvas. The course is thought-provoking and interesting, and Prof Clulow makes every effort to make sure his students understand the material.

Loved this class! An exciting approach to a history class with many clear connections drawn between the events of the distant past and present. I swear I think about something I learned in this class at least once a week. Just remember to stay on top of your independent research project because the due dates will sneak up on you.

Clulow is a great teacher and you can tell he loves what he teaches, he's super kind and almost always gives an extension if you reach out to him. Assignments were not too hard as long as you show effort you should get 80s and above. You only really need the lectures for the mid-term, everything else is accessible via online information. Cool Class

Dr. Clulow was one of my favorite professors ever. He is super knowledgable, passionate and engaging. His lectures are fun and easy to get engaged with via watching clips, listening to songs, and tying in pop-culture. He responds to emails super quickly and if you can't make office hours he will work with you. A lot of readings, but not difficult.

analysis.name: Adam Klivans
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Klivans is brilliant and he knows his stuff, but he's not the best at explaining concepts. He records lectures and assigns them as hw before every class. In class, you do absurdly challenging practice problems. Tests and homeworks are VERY difficult. The greatest thing about this class though: he's a very lenient grader and it's curved.

I do not recommend this class. The grading is really tough and it is sorta difficult to ask questions and get a good response. Most of the material on homeworks and exams were never touched on in class. For a class that was supposed to not be so bad, it was my hardest class

Klivans is definitely one of the more difficult 313 professors although he curves the grades at the end. He will be sarcastic if you ask a question, although he does try to make sure you understand. It is a flipped class so lectures are online, problems worked in class. Also gives pop quizzes in class.
Disappointing how ineffective his lectures are for an online class. He is clearly very knowledgeable and smart, but poorly communicates ideas in an easy to understand manner.

I should have just said this to Klivans during class, but if you're going to have a linear algebra/probability heavy lecture, you should give the students a heads-up. Also, instead of saying ""You're not gonna learn this anywhere else better," it would be more helpful to point us to other resources (b/c he's very bad at explaining stuff).

analysis.name: Adela Timmons
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very knowledgeable and kind professor. I enjoyed the examples she'd give of real-life cases she worked on. She takes attendance for points at the end, so I'd say show up. No textbook, she provides the readings needed every week, and we needed to complete a weekly reflection about them. 2 exams non non-cumulative. 2 essays, thought they were fun.

Professor Timmons is super sweet! Sometimes the class can get loud and people talk over her but not for long because everyone likes and respects her. I love that she uses real world examples that she has experienced on her road to where she is now (obviously changing info for anonymity). Grade is based on attendance, reading reactions, and 2 exams!

Great class with interesting lectures and readings. The professor is very kind and approachable, and she cares deeply for her students. Work load is manageable and the exams are not difficult as long as you attend lectures regularly. Attendance is mandatory and a part of your overall grade, but there are some drops.

I am a senior at UT and this has been my favorite class I've ever taken. The material is heavy but it teaches you real life skills if you apply it. The readings are usually very interesting and I actually look forward to them each week. I can not recommend this class enough but you must attend to get something out of it!

Dr. Timmons is very sweet! Some of the material may be heavy for some people, but she handles it tactfully and compassionately. There is a lot of reading, as well as a one-page reading reaction each week. There's a study guide for exams, if you complete it you'll do well. There are also two longer papers. Overall great class, super interesting!

analysis.name: Adam Kraus
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If you need an easy science credit, take this course. Prof. Kraus teaches astronomy in a super simple way, using minimal amounts of math and illustrating his lectures with film clips. Exams are short and based heavily on homework questions and in-class instapolls. Prof. Kraus is also kind and always willing to help students with course material.

Professor is really nice and the class is super manageable. Drops 1/5 of instapoll attendance questions. Homeworks take a whille to do but not super difficult. The first exam was hard but after that its easier. You just need to study for 2-3 days before the test and study the instapoll/homework questions and occasionally read the textbook.
A good professor, his lectures sometimes feel repetitive and he will sometimes go over the same information twice. He is nice about grades and passionate about the subject matter.
Easy class. Fairly interesting lectures, with instapolls that are mandatory for a grade. Homeworks were a little long but tedious.

Great class, attendance based on instapolls that are easy to find online, and you can discuss with others. Tests are the homework questions + instapolls, so just memorize those. I never read, and there are drops (drops 1 test, lowest 1/4 of instapolls, and 3 homeworks). Great guy and easy credit!

analysis.name: Enrique Aguayo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: an amazing professor, i would highly recommend to take this class. he is a very patience person and a very fair grader. show up to class and you'll do well. because of the material of the class and how it is taught dont take this class as a freshman which is the mistake i made. would retake this class still.

Professor Aguayo is extremely understanding. He is also a student, so he understands the stress of finals season. Attendance in his class is for extra credit. His assignments are clear, and I literally ended with a 100 by turning all the assignments in. Definitely take this class if you need the credit!

This class was easy, but I  learned a lot. There's some freedom in how you complete the assignments. He doesn't post any information for each lecture until like an hour before class, so there's not much time to review things before class. Great class for people unsure of their career path or who want to learn how to prepare to enter the workforce.

analysis.name: Ashish Agarwal
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There's no way to get around it; this class is hard. Homework will consume a lot of your time (8+ hours per assignment). But the workload does get lighter through the semester. Dr. Agarwal is nice and cares about his students; lectures could be more engaging though. Read the cases to participate in class, and study well in advance for the tests.

A challenging yet rewarding class based on Harvard Business School cases. Agarwal teaches MIS concepts through real-world examples and cold-calls often. Homework is independent and helps build Excel skills, especially for beginners. Exams are tough and oddly worded, but you learn a lot and  Agarwal is an excellent professor overall.

professor agarwal is a great professor. The concepts covered in the class and inherently difficult and directly apply to real world scenarios. Go to class and actually listen to lectures/discussion. Professor agarwal is also very approachable and willing to help you with any questions you may have.
Passionate about what he's teaching, but needs to be more structured. Also, the tests were worded weirdly and did not test how well you understood the topics discussed in class.

MIS301H will consume all of your time and if you don't study three times as much as you think you need to, you won't do well. While he is nice and generally decent at presenting the info., understanding the material falls solely on you. Do not take this class if you don't want to read thirty pages a night or spend less than 30 hours on assignments.

analysis.name: Seema Agarwala
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Agarwala is knowledgable and explains concepts well. However, she can be intimidating and impatient with students if they come unprepared to class or don't answer questions a particular way. Sometimes, the lectures seemed disorganized. Overall, not a hard class. Make sure you're prepared because she will ask questions about the previous lecture

Her lectures are dense and can be hard to follow, especially if you lack background knowledge. Attendance is mandatory, so if you'll miss more than three classes, this course may not be for you. Exams are application-focused with more points allocated to the FRQ. Overall, I wouldn't take this course again.

Dr. Agarwala is so knowledgeable and her lectures are very concise without fluffing up any information. The discussion sections led by her TAs were also incredibly helpful and everyone involved in the team ensures that you're ready for the exams. The exams and analyses of research papers ensures success in and out of her class. Take her!

Neuro development is an amazing class that absolutely improved how I read and write academic papers. This class is completely worth it if you are ready to put a substantial amount of effort in. She does cold call and her quizzes are hard, but you only need a 90+ to get an A and something like an 86+ to get an A-.

Dr. Argawala is incredibly impatient with her students and creates a hostile learning environment. She gets frustrated when students ask questions and is overall condescending. She does not promote a safe place whatsoever and will mock and embarrass you for saying the wrong thing in class.

analysis.name: Kamran Aghaie
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Terrible professor. The class had no structure and the lectures were whatever he came up with that day. The only way to do well in the class is to write to what his preconceived opinions are about the given subject. You wont learn anything from him only on your own.

Professor Aghaie was the opposite of helpful and supporting. His lectures consisted of him going off on tangents about whatever he felt like discussing that given day so most of the learning was up to you as the student. It often felt like he was making the class structure up as he went along and he never responds to emails. I q dropped.

I think getting an A is pretty manageable if you do the readings and go to all the lectures. However, I didn't really feel that his lectures were very organized, and having to take notes on literally everything he says because it'll end up on the test becomes annoying when, on the test, you're having to remember his jumbled trail of thought.

Lectures were really random and didn't relate to the assigned readings often, had to mostly self learn/ study with the textbook. Primarily about history of the middle east, not gov, which was still interesting, but the random lectures and quite difficult timed essay mt/ finals were still difficult.

The class was just weekly readings and build up to a final research paper. Readings were long and often went undiscussed in class because Dr. Aghaie would go off on long tangents (he is clearly VERY intelligent on this subject, and makes that known). He was approachable, but was often unhelpful with feedback. Course was unorganized. TA was useless.

analysis.name: Yukie Aida
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Unorganized schedule that we were behind on Homework. Overall, she posted assignments late as well as exams her format did not help in studying. READ the textbook and take good notes on her class. Late on grading as well, and quizzes every day so try not to miss her class as much as possible cause those points will save you. Choose Wisely

I can see why she has so many good reviews because at heart, she is such a nice and caring person. However, I found her lecture pacing incredibly slow, especially in the first half of the semester. At times it felt like "Okay let's move on, but we'd spend too much time on the SAME thing. She also tends to keep class over the allotted time.

Amazing professor. Extremely kind and genuinely wants to help you learn Japanese. The course load is what you expect for any language learning class; lots of homework, quizzes, and exams. Still, this was one of the funnest classes I've ever taken and that was due to how great Aida-sensei is as a person and a lecturer.

Aida-sensei genuinely cares about her students, and their learning. Additionally, she presents material in a clear, easy to understand manner, and encourages active participation to learn the language. An added bonus: she is incredibly energetic and her class is fun to attend.

One of my favorite teachers. She is super sweet and makes class fun. Homework and quizzes every day, but it's manageable. She forgets to upload things sometimes, but nothing that can't be found on the JOSHU website. She's good at getting you to practice speaking and repetition in class, so you retain quite a lot. Really good for starting Japanese.

analysis.name: Aimee Hosemann
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class is super easy and interesting. No final, just a book report, so a lot of people stopped going to class after the midterm. I went to every lecture though because they were honestly fun. Discussions were kind of a waste of time but attendance is mandatory. No text book but a few cool, short books are assigned, as well as journal readings.

Professor Hosemann is a pro! She is a super smart, well cultured professor. Everything is fair game in lectures, this course is really entertaining because you get to explore so many things that are otherwise taboo. Really glad I took this class, it almost makes me want to be an anthropology major.

Extremely easy class. She is a very engaging professor. You really don't need to show up for lecture after the midterm. Discussion sections: go to them. If you go to lecture, no attendance, it'll be a very interesting discussion, but I didn't find them extremely helpful after the midterm. No final exam! Only a book report, so as long as you read...

She is DEF one of the best professors at UT! I loved her class, if I wasn't a Sr., I'd probably switch to Anthro. She really cares about what students think and assignments are "discussions" with her on paper, which she responds to via Canvas! Not to mention EVERY lecture is interesting. Even if you wouldn't normally think its an interesting topic.

It was a summer course, so it was a little more compacted, but still great. There were only 3 "journal entries" which are written in third person. She wants to hear what you think ALWAYS. In lecture and on paper. She was a seriously great lecturer and sincerely cares about her students. I could tell she LOVES her job. I am so glad I took the class.

analysis.name: Aida Torabi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Let me just preface this by saying that as a professor, Dr. Torabi is pretty nice. However the biggest problem with her class is that the exams are designed for you to fail because they are completely different from all the HW problems we get and are significantly harder. Honestly just take someone else if you can.
Very hard!!!  I literally got a like a 58 on first test

She's lowk rude sometimes and I swear she goes over the easiest examples in class and then the exams/homeworks are way, way harder. She confronted the class after the MEDIAN on MT2 was a 57 and told us to study harder… lol just admit you're not a good prof it's fine. It's fine tho, she gave us 0.5% extra credit at the end of the semester, how kind

Idek if she could get a A on her own tests. Other professors make midterms more conceptual but she spams math questions. puts questions on the test that she hasn't taught the class how to work. We're supposed to learn to solve the questions thru the HW –> the crazy hard test questions aren't covered there. dont take her if you value your gpa/time.

Good reviews on here will just say she's nice –> she is but she's a terrible lecturer. Shows simple applications of concepts in lecture but on exams and HWs tests on very complex applications of concepts. 1% EC but that's if you show up to all lectures and do 12 extra HW assignments (all with over 15 questions). No curves on exams w/ an avg of 60!

analysis.name: Akash Kanojia
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is a fantastic class to get an in-depth understanding of markets. This is completely an open discussion class, but Akash does a great job of explaining everything in a fun and detailed way. There are two exams which are difficult, but the class gets curved anyways. Highly recommend taking this class and getting to know Akash!

By far my favorite class I've taken. Half the grade is participation and the tests are heavily curved. If you show up and participate you are almost guaranteed an A. He's extremely smart and has great real world experiences, and he really cares about his students. No better class to learn about what is going on in markets AND how to talk about them

Great class to learn about markets and keep up to date. There are 2 exams that are pretty difficult but the class gets curved to a 3.6 anyways so it doesn't matter as long as you get within the average (~65). His class emphasizes participation so show up and try to contribute as much as possible its worth 30% of your grade. Overall, great professor

Great professor and lectures, sensible content to address markets from different perspective (and each week has a market lecture too). Exams aren't too hard, it's like 2/3 general understanding from lectures and readings and then 1/3 hard/nitpicky questions "to make a curve." If you listen in class, a day's studying probably enough.

Akash is an excellent professor who is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject matter. If you really want to learn about markets, you'll absolutely love this course. The tests are tough, but the class is heavily curved. He's one of my favorite professors I've had at McCombs. Just show up, participate, and you'll do well.

analysis.name: Deji Akinwande
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The exams are multiple choice but not much partial credit is awarded if you select the wrong answer for whatever reason. Lectures didn't feel that helpful either, so I would recommend reading the textbook and/or watching the relevant Razavi Electronics I and II lectures on YouTube and doing the assigned practice problems to succeed in this course.

I loved Deji's lectures, he made funny anecdotes about his life and somehow strung it back to transistors and circuits haha. The exams were very chill, but since they're mcq, its a bit unforgiving if you make small mistakes. He does pull questions  from the textbook though, so theoretically you can just do all the book problems. Labs are good too.

One of the best professors in the department!
If you get 100 on the final exam, you will automatically get an A in the class.
I have had such an awesome semester with him. Definitely recommend, I wish I could take another class taught by him!

Dr. Akiwande was an amazing professor! He cracks funny jokes and tells his life stories sometimes during lectures. I learned a lot about how transistors work in his class. Although it's a lab class, the tests still make up 60% of your grades. But they are all MCs and very doable! This was an excellent class, and he was an amazing guy to talk to!

analysis.name: Erin Akins
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Erin gives amazing feedback & understands most students are not english majors. She makes class inclusive, fun & engaging, one I always woke up to go to. Her feedback is super helpful, drops quizzes, and grades super leniently, while also wanting you to stretch your understanding. 4 books to read, and 3 papers, only hw is reading. AMAZING PROF

I took Banned Books with Erin and she is probably one of the best professors i've had. By far my favorite class of the semester and I'm sure everyone else in my class would agree. She takes the books to new levels and is phenomenal at explaining she may act like she's all over the place but she knows what she's doing. Cant wait to read her books.

Class was Rhetoric of Apology and it was very interesting & doable! Akins is currently a grad student, and the only issue was the slow grading and limited feedback as the course progressed. There is no TA so that's why grading multiple essays took a long time. Rewrites for points back are available and its overall a great class for a writing flag!

analysis.name: Manasicha Akepiyapornchai
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: (I took ANS379 Translating Asia. I'm not sure why there isn't an option.) Mana is truly a student-centered teacher, always willing to help, really cares about her students, and listens to their concerns. One thing to be aware of is that her course requires a significant amount of reading. Her grading is very nice, rarely loses points.

Pretty easy class, however for a non-hindu may be confusing. professor is very friendly and always willing to help. Her understanding of Hinduism and its philosophies/beliefs is a little off. So if you are a hindu you may be confused or even heavily disagree with her approach to some gods. Overall she is very kind and I enjoyed this course

I took Prof. Mana for South Asian gods and goddesses....her class is an easy A. I never even did the readings when I was taking this class (I was born and raised Hindu) but for someone who wasn't it may be more difficult...she assigns bunch of readings in class. She often also rambles on during class as well but overall this class was an easy A.

Honestly such a sweet and informative professor. There's a lot of reading, but you could get away by just skimming through them. She's also very accommodating as long as you communicate with her! I had no real knowledge about Hinduism, but it's very doable.

I genuinely enjoyed taking this class. Mana always made an effort to allow students to take control of their learning, and made the environment very comfortable for her students. I really enjoyed coming to lectures and always looked forward to hearing our in class discussions. She is a professor, I truly recommend to take if you have the chance.

analysis.name: Akemi Katayama
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Katayama may seem a little intimidating at times but she overall cares for her students very much and you can tell she really wants you to succeed. Pay attention in class and be ready to participate. Reading the textbook before class really gets you a head start on lessons in class. 601D is easy but 610D is a little more difficult

I loved Katayama-sensei when I took her for 601 and 610. She's a little strict at times but it shapes you into a good Japanese speaker. Show her you care and that you like Japanese and she'll love you. Read the book before class, study your kanji, participate in class, and you'll do great, especially for 610D

Sensei is a great teacher but you do have to put effort into the class. As one of the previous comments said, she doesn't care for slackers. But she does care that you get an education and really immerse yourself in Japanese, so try in class and take the time to talk with her in office hours

Daily Quiz at the start of the class( at the start of your day too) won't spend time on Kanji, force everyone to shut their mic, go over things too fast but again and again, daily homework is also a pain

Nice but plain. I had her for and 8 am class and she was not the most exciting person to take up to. She does't care much for slackers but she's very helpful if you go to her office. It's a pretty easy class with a lot of quiz and homework grades. If you show up everyday, you also get +2 points on your overall grade.

analysis.name: Karen Akre
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are mandatory due to partial iClicker grade but are not very helpful. She just lectures off of slides It is better to just take notes from the book while going through the slides at home. Her tests are very unpredictable, no reviews, only a chat session the night before the test. Generally 25 MC, T/F, and about 5-8 free response.

A very disorganized class. would rather take another professor. Was very nonchalant regarding helping students study for exams. R Great at explaining but you could NEVER know what to expect on exams. Just hope your T.A. prepares you well..
Just read off her slides the entire time. I only went because of the clicker questions. If you do the readings, you can pass her class. Honestly, I was really bored in class. Not engaging at all.

analysis.name: Richard Albert
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Albert is one of my favorite professors at UT. This lectures are mostly discussion discussion based, so be sure to participate! Tests make up 80% of your grade make sure you know the material or go to office hours. His lectures are very interesting and makes you think about stuff you normally wouldn't care to think about.

Dr Albert has been the best teacher I have had at the university. He is very passionate about his work, and you can tell through his lectures. At first, the three-grade criteria was scary, but engaging in class and creating a study group helped me succeed. I cannot recommend this class enough!

I highly enjoyed this class, the lectures were engaging and small group discussions were always fruitful. Note taking is simple and Albert loves to talk to students as long as you put in effort to talk to him. This class is graded on few things however. Your final is 50% of your grade, so prepare wisely (the exams and essays are all open note).

Professor Albert is one of the most knowledgeable people I have ever met. I started off not liking him, but the more I was in his class the more I began to enjoy it. You are graded on 3 exams and 1 essay, which are graded pretty harsh, but its not impossible. The content is a little boring, but its worth it because you will feel so smart after.

Professor Albert was truly one of my favorite professors that i've had at UT. His lectures were very insightful and made you want to learn. You are graded on 1 essay, 1 midterm exam, and 1 final exam. As long as you take good notes and study up before the exams, an A is definitely attainable. I 100% recommend this class to anyone!

analysis.name: Alex Hanson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Hanson is one of the most passionate professors I've had, and his lectures were both engaging and informative. He was also really responsive outside class. It's worth struggling through the homework/midterms if you want a solid foundation for ECE going forward. If you're going for straight A's, however, this may not be the class for you.

Probably one of the greatest lecturers you'll meet. Somehow makes complex circuits relatively easy to understand. HOWEVER, test difficulty ramped up noticeably in fall 2025, and will probably only be tougher in the future. The tests are very difficult with averages around 50-60, and grading is strict. Be ready to be humbled by this class.

MY GOAT!! Amazing lecturer who can break concepts down to a conceptual level and help you understand the topic intuitively. He's super funny and genuinely cares about students and their success (you can reach him outside of class through discord and he does a career lecture). This class is comically hard (tears shed) but the prof made me love it.

The professor is great at lecturing and breaking down the concepts to the most fundamental level in class, however the examples he provides does not line up with the difficulty of exams and homeworks, which are SIGNIFICANTLY more difficult than the lecture. I wish he showed more examples of difficult questions and show how to navigate them.

Dr. Hanson is an amazing professor and very accessible outside of class (join the discord). His lectures are thorough, intuitive, and well-rehearsed. That being said, this class is not easy. Expect most of your grade to be determined by difficult exams with failing averages. They are curved, but this class will seriously challenge you.

analysis.name: Megan Allen
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Yes, I know I got a C+; however, Professor Allen is truly a sweetheart! She cares about her students and her teachings and is always willing to help during office hours! I feel like just going to the office for hours helped because I received extra credit for it! I highly recommend taking Professor Allen!

The professor is very nice, gives a lot of extra credit, and is very easy to follow. The first half of the class is fast paced, but you'll get used to it quickly. There's not really any pop quizzes but the assignments you work on in class can get taken for a quiz grade. Exams can be tough but extra credit covers it and there can also be a curve.

Tax is hard itself but her lectures and notes make it a lot better. She explains things well and does alot of examples in class so the concepts are understood. There is alot of material and it does become dense but her exams generally use practice exam questions and test on the easier of materials for any unit. She also does alot of extra credit.

It was a tough class, but shes the GOAT. Class was fun and engaging, I know how to do some taxes, how to evade them while avoiding detection from the service, and how to make that money clean through investments in restaurants or laundromats. she provides plenty of resources to prepare for exams, answers any questions, and is just great! recommend!

Professor Allen is great if you come in with knowledge about financial accounting. For someone who isn't familiar with the course, it's hard to catch up at the speed at which she goes in class. Her class is kind of set up like she expects students to come in with prior knowledge. Also, she does pop quizzes for a grade along with attendance.

analysis.name: Hal Alper
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I just don't even understand how this class was so bad. I went to every lecture, did all of the readings, did all of the hw and studied like hell. I didn't do good on the second exam but figured I could make it up on a later one, but they just kept getting worse and worse so I couldn't raise my grade. Ended up having to use my OTE and switch majors

He is a good lecturer and I rlly feel like I understand the material so well. However, the curve scheme absolutely punishes ppl who try and do well in the class. He basically made it so that if you were in the 50-60 range you would get bumped up to a C and won't take final but if you had an A you would be taken down to a B and have to take final

The actual material in this class isn't even hard, but this man decided to shift the curve at the very END of the semester and make it harder to get an A. I thought I had an A all semester but the last week of class it went away. All my friends who took other professors thought the class was easy but he gives sm hw, makes exams insane, and LIES

Just take Edison at this point, this man is absolutely praying on your downfall. The hws were graded wrong every single time. Exams just kept getting worse and worse so if you do bad on first two you're so cooked. Quizzes are honestly just impossible ngl

Look at his grade distribution on utgrades+ and see for urself how awful he is. Over 40% of the class q dropped or was failing by finals season(final is optional). Even with this he made the curve harder (A- to B+ was a ten point difference and C- to C was 1 point). HW was graded incorrectly, exams were impossible, and he loved every second of it.

analysis.name: Dananjaya Appulage
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took Dr. Dan at ACC for Chem 2 Lab. He's very kind, wants you to succeed. Thick accent and speaks fast, so his lab lectures are a little hard to understand, but he is a generous grader. He will try his best to help direct you to the correct answer and even lets you redo work. Be cautious taking him for lecture, might be hard to understand content.

They removed my rating before, but I stand by what I said. This was the worst science professor I have ever had in 3 separate countries. He was rude, homophobic, spoke constantly and handed out papers during active exams, and treated his students as less than. 
This man shouldn't teach.

I went to every class. I aced every online quiz due to 2 attempts, and I aced every homework assignment. I stayed for 1:1s. I went to tutoring. I did group work nothing worked. I found the professor to be really hard to understand with his thick accent, but equally hard to understand his concepts when he broke it down and that becomes your problem.

I wish professor Dan used the board more. He is super chill and understanding but just goes through the course contents on the presentation. At the end of the semester, the presentation wasn't working and when he taught on the board, it was so much more informative. Great professor overall. Easy to get As if you invest enough time.

He cares about his students, offers flexible schedules, and inspires us to do our best. He shares his experiences, gives helpful advice and encourages questions if we don't understand. He's available during office hours and is passionate about learning. I'm glad I took chemistry with him. Amazing professor!

analysis.name: Brendan Apfeld
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Awesome Professor. Chill, young dude. Does not grade hard. If you actually do the assignments then you can expect an easy A in this class. There are 2 multi choice tests and a paper at the end of the semester. The paper is only 4 pages tho! I got a 90 and an 80 on the tests with only a few hours of studying for each. And a 95 on the paper.

Apfeld's class is fairly easy, though the tests are more difficult than you might expect. He makes occasional jokes and his videos that he plays during lectures are generally very entertaining, though the lectures themselves are sometimes boring. Attendance is not mandatory though your alternative is the most boring set of books put to print.

Took a risk taking a first-time teacher and it paid off. Very fair exams, fun assignments and great teacher. Glad I took him. Only con is the textbook sucks, but he said he hates it and won't use it again. The exams are fairly lectured based, but he puts the powerpoints online so its not life or death if you miss some classes!

I LOVED Apfeld! He really wants his students to do well. It's 25% midterm & 25% final (both curved), 25% a paper (he'll give you 100 if you check all the boxes he's looking for), and 25% a series of community engagement things (5 for 5% each). I was nervous about it but I was really glad he made us do them. He's a great guy and a good teacher!

I took a chance on Professor Apfeld. This was his first time teaching a college class so he had no reviews or anything. That said, this is a very talented young dude and a great teacher. Readings are long, but study (memorize) the lecture slides HARD for every quiz and test and you can get fairly easy 100's. It's April and I have a 99.3 average.

analysis.name: Jamie Aprile
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Completely unrealistic expectations! This is an Intro course and half or more of the students are non-majors and she expects everyone to memorize the what, where, when and significance of EVERY SINGLE artifact, building, and sculpture we have EVER SEEN in class or in the book. Absolutely ridiculous! This is like an UD Art History class! Do not take

She does read off a paper but that's because she is telling you the stories of mythology. If you think she is rambling then you aren't paying attention. It's not too much, but you have to write down EVERYTHING! Then reguritate it on the test and you will get an A. Sometimes I would have to read the book for discussion post but it was easy enough.

Very poor teacher. Reads off a sheet for the entire 50 min and mumbles her sentences. Worst of all, when I had her she designed her tests so that no one could finish (not even on purpose). She's new and I think she got flustered and didn't know how to conduct the class during those 4 days we missed because of the weather. AVOID

She is ridiculously passionate. Honestly, it really is a TON of information in only THREE tests, so there's a ton of studying needed for each test. That being said, people grumble about it being super hard, BUT it really isn't If you take decent lecture notes a ton of those too!) and read the SUMMARIES online, NOT the book. Study SMART. Easy A.

She was a really good professor. After a few classes though, the class (which comprised of 9 students) figured that we have to ask questions because she literally can talk non-stop for an hour straight. She used power points for her slide so there is at least some visual aids in the class. There will be a lot of reading though.

analysis.name: Andrew Butters
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I looked forward to professor Butters's classes every week! I learned so much about journalism from the stories he told of his experiences as a journalist. We wrote 3 stories throughout the semester and he offered much guidance and good feedback. Attendance is definitely important!

Professor Butters was so kind and passionate about journalism. I looked forward to the lab every week. Professor Butters was very accessible and always willing to help and share experiences from his past that were humorous and inspiring. I wish I was a journalism major so I could take more classes with Butters, his lectures were very engaging.

analysis.name: Alessandro (Alex) Rezende de Macedo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 195 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Alex is, without doubt, the best math instructor I've had at any level. After taking his class, I feel that I have a better understanding of not just calculus but math as-a-whole. Although Alex tends to meander on from topic to topic, his lectures remain interesting due to his charisma and the prof has a unique ability to make math UNDERSTANDABLE.

A great teacher but not an easy A. If you put in the effort you can get an A. Alex is available for countless hours several days of the week to assist his students in their studies. Take him if you want to work hard and become a better mathematician as a whole. Lectures often funny too.

Very interesting subject matter, but don't be fooled by the fact this is an "intro" class. The course started off really easy during the first couple weeks and eventually became insanely hard during the last 2 weeks. However, Macedo is an engaging lecturer and is very patient during office hours and review sessions. Don't expect an "easy A class".

Interesting pure math class. Alex is a caring professor. Available outside of class to help with reviewing HWs and exams. Adjusted the workload based off of how the class was doing. Even though this was an intro class, it's nowhere from easy. The last 3rd of the class was insanely difficult. Have to be very familiar with a new way of thinking.

The LOML. Alex is such an amazing professor and a great friend. I fell in love with him at first glance. He's so smart and knows how to "dumb" the information down for us. He is so funny and has stories for everything. The material was complicated but he was always there to help me. He helps you out while taking tests and guides you through.

analysis.name: Angela Beasley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took her data mining class the when she was teaching here for the first time. She really really cared about the students and enjoyed teaching a lot. She always asked the students for feedbacks. The class got harder I heard but shouldn't be too bad. The projects were fun and challenging!

The online class is very very bad. The lectures are recordings from the in person lecture, so anytime an example is done on the board, you cant see them since only the screen is recorded. Also a ridiculous amount of hw (3-4 a week) to only account for 15% of your grade.

Very good intro course to ML. Beasley takes out a lot of the complex math behind concepts and makes them very understandable. Projects are easy, exams very doable if you study (just have to worry about time crunch a little bit). Social impact presentations are graded easily and provide some insight. Overall great class.

Angela is a great professor and explains things clearly for students new to Data Science and Machine Learning. The tests are rehashes of the in-class assignments and programming assignments are very straightforward (most of what is needed is given to you, you just need to do what the assignments say). Learned a lot from this course.

Pretty fun and chill class. The lectures were a little slow, but I didn't mind it personally. The projects and homework are easy, especially if you already know Python. I liked the tests most about this class; they weren't free, but were very easy to prepare for and no surprises on the exams.

analysis.name: Anindita Bardhan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: absolutely terrible professor and instructor. graded on extremely few things and expected to perform damn near perfection with averages for most tests and quizzes being failing. she is just a terrible professor and made this already difficult class more hell so please avoid her at all costs. exam was NOT reflective of any class content and harder!!

One of the worst professors that I have taken. Lectures are very hard to follow since she does not use the class slides and she is very rude if you have questions. She cold calls a lot, and does not explain things well enough for students to answer questions.
Its a really hard class. Notes are unclear, and tests are way harder than what is learnt in class. She claimed she would teach it as if we were accounting beginners, but that was not the case at all.

“Every class day is game day” I mutter to myself as I drag my feet into this class. That's the motto she told us. Just a warning, if you are a visual learner, don't want to learn the material before class, and hate speaking up in a lecture hall, do not take this class. She's a good professor but she expects so much effort, even when you're lost.

Professor Bardhan explains difficult concepts well and has a good sense of humor, but she sometimes gets sidetracked answering questions and covering obscure hypotheticals. Participation is part of your grade and she tends to cold call, so be prepared. She does move quickly and exams are tricky, so it's on you to speak up if you're confused.

analysis.name: Andrea Baer
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is pretty straightforward and is like a simpler version of I305. Tuesdays are lectures (not required) and Thursdays are small group (required). Starts off pretty slow and simple but assignments part of the research process towards the end of the semester are more time consuming. Make sure to do quizzes and journal for easy points

The class was an 8 am and was just really, really boring. The concepts covered are very elementary. Attendance was taken, which sucked. The workload was minimal except for a research project in the last few weeks
Lectures are very lengthy and the grading can be sort of nitpicky with essay assignments.

analysis.name: Anthony Conway
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Prof: 

Conway is the best professor out of the many subpar ones in UT math. His teaching: show/tell/apply format.

Class:

Exams based on HW QB. HW:10 problems weekly. Attendance is not required. Great online notes.

Ad. Notes:

UT shows a grading curve with a few C's, D's, and F's. Those are students who do not show up at all, or skip every exam.

Don't take this course (at least w/ this professor) unless you are knowledgeable in notation and proofs. I took this after multiple stats and upper division math courses, and I'm so lost. He rarely goes step-by-step. Tests are representative of hw, but are still difficult if you don't memorize every proof. Professor is clearly knowledgeable though.

Fall 2025. Lowest 3 HW and lowest midterm get dropped. Midterms and final are multiple-choice and based on HW. Discussions are for extra practice, not mandatory. Super easy if you've taken calc before and still very doable if you haven't. In lecture, I like how he proved why everything makes sense. Overall great guy, definitely take him!

Best math course I've had in my life. I've taken Calc AB and BC in high school, but felt like I needed a refresher. I love how he explains things and I genuinely wanted to go to every lecture. He proves how everything makes sense there was really no memorization needed. He drops the lowest midterm and lowest few homeworks. Super cool and funny guy.

Probably best professor I'll ever have. Went to almost every office hour and enjoyed every moment talking to this Swiss guy. Could tell he's very passionate about math and answered questions about anything. Explained concepts in a way that proved everything he taught but no proofs. Clear class outline and almost no work to be done. Wish he did 408D

analysis.name: Amanda Garrett
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Assignment instructions can be ambiguous. Adds a lot of unnecessary assignments to the course that do not help enhance our knowledge or performance in lab. It seems like their purpose is to waste our time. The professor is very nice, and when she lectures, it is helpful. However, she only lectures for 10-15 minutes once a week.

W Prof Seminars always introduced to us new things for research/ECs. Lab quizzes were tricky as they tested on some random specific details in the protocol. My TAs were THE BEST (shout out to Janice and Tu-Quyen), always super helpful. Labs were longish, a lot of EC, PyMol project was fun, practical was light, a lot of busy work (my only complaint)

Dr. Garrett makes it very easy to succeed in this class, if you're willing to put in the effort. Certain weeks can be very assignment heavy (never more than 3-4hrs outside lab), but you always know what to expect and there's never any surprises. Canvas is organized very well, and Dr. Garrett/TAs are very kind/receptive w/ questions and feedback! :)

This class is well-organized and an easy A, but the workload for a 2 hr credit is considerable. Weekly reflection essays & PyMOL activities often took hours, plus there are weekly lab quizzes to study for and pre-lab assignments due. Labs are helpful but incredibly long. She offers lots of extra credit and drops your lowest quiz though.

Dr. Garrett is genuinely the most kind and caring professor I've had at UT. The course can have a heavy-ish workload if you leave everything to the last minute but the TAs are so understanding. So accessible outside of class if you have any questions about the major, career plans, etc!!

analysis.name: Haseeb Ansari
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class can genuinely be super easy as long as you put in the work, I just left studying for literally the last minute before exams and completely gave up on trying to understand integrals at the end. Overall many opportunities to save your grade. Honestly all props to my TA too because I didn't really understand lectures.

Amazing professor to take for multivariable calculus! He has very clear grading criteria, the lectures are very good (content is somewhat hard but he makes it manageable). Knows names, is very accessible outside class, and is a very nice person. The exams and homework are fairly easy, and he works through examples very well. Definitely recommend!

Professor Ansari is kind and caring, but his lectures are dry as he mostly reads directly from the textbook. Multivariable Calculus requires a conceptual understanding of how 2D math generalizes to 3D, but he often skips the intuition to focus on repetitive practice problems. I had to learn how to conceptualize the concepts outside of class.

1 Quiz/Week. 2 Mid terms (got a 100 on both) Final (100) ended with 99.57. The class was the easiest math class ever, without sacrificing quality of lecture. Dr. Ansari deserves a pay raise, he makes expectations so clear, tells you what the quizzes and tests will be, hes kinda funny too. go mandatory lecture do wtv study 1 day before test, aceable

Dr. Ansari is truly the easiest math prof I've had. Plenty of quizzes & HW, 2 midterms and a final. If you have trouble with this class go to office hrs and make sure to have questions ready for discussion, TA was amazing. Practice problems from the text book helped me out a lot to understand the concept better. Amazing class and amazing faculty!

analysis.name: Amanda Koltz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Koltz and Wolf, along with the teaching team were nice and knowledgeable. The class itself wasn't bad, it's mainly memorization-based and exams are heavily graded. However, the class was harder than what I had expected it to be. There are a few projects that the TAs grade strictly on, and exams are a mix of MC and FRQ. Content is interesting!

Dr. Koltz and Dr. Wolf were great lecturers! The content was mostly memorization and the exams were not too difficult. The exams did take a long time to be graded and there are outside projects that are easy but you do have to still do them. Very interesting class and content overall and both professors were kind and understanding.

The content of this class is not TOO difficult, but the course structure is set up a lot harder than it needs to be. Grades are almost completely based on exams, and each exam is graded atleast a month after it's taken. Grades aren't posted until LAST minute. They mentioned a curve, didn't apply it. So stressful not knowing how you're doing.

Dr. Koltz was a great lecturer, and she and Dr. Wolf made sure to cover everything needed for each exam! It's mostly memorization, but as long as you stay on top of the content it's manageable. The discussion projects are also a good grade boost, just make sure to actually try on them.

I personally did not enjoy this class, I felt that the lectures weren't that intriguing. The grades are hidden throughout the semester so you can't see how you stand in the class, and assignments can take 2-3 weeks to return to you. At least there's no final. If you really like ecology then this class might be for you, but it wasn't for me.

analysis.name: Amrita Kaur
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 110 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: read all of this. I'll start by saying she is an amazing teacher, just not a good professor. She's really fun in class, but she loves handing out zeros on her homework assignments, which is hard to come back from. I enjoyed the class before we were given back our homework grades (1 month after submitting!), but she was not helpful after that.

I personally enjoyed the HWs even though they were challenging because they were quite enjoyable to code up. However, I feel like most of my effort went into doing good style and docstrings. Sometimes we don't know about certain style requirements until after it was graded, especially at the end unless you asked the TAs. Final was hard, but curved

Professor Kaur has really good lectures. The programming assignments are long and you can lose a lot of points because of poor style (especially at the semester start), but since there's so much lecture/feedback form extra credit it's easy to get full credit. Tests are really hard and worth a ton but there are practice tests posted, so study a lot!

Professor Kaur is a great teacher, and her lectures are engaging and informative. The tests are difficult, but are often heavily curved. The TAs are helpful, but their grading can be inconsistent. If you attend lectures, study, and don't use AI to generate your code, you will do well. Beware of using outside material, because it's an automatic zero

Pretty good professor. Lectures and weekly assignments are engaging and interesting. Weekly assignments are graded harshly but there's a ton of extra credit so its not hard to offset the tough grading. If you do the practice tests she gives you its not hard to get 90+ on exams. If you did UIL CS this course will be extremely easy for you.

analysis.name: Amy Liu
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great UGS to take! The topic of the course was interesting and engaging. Dr. Liu is very kind and a good lecturer. The weekly quizzes are exactly what is covered in lecture, so if you take notes they will be very easy. There are multiple in-class essays, but they are pretty straightforward to prepare for and write. Gave extra points at the end.

Easiest UGS ever, the only negative thing was at 8am. Attendance is not mandatory, but quizzes are based on lectures which are not accessible outside of class so...you miss out a lot if you don't attend. My TA Meiying Xu was the sweetest person ever and I got 100s on all essays that I personally thought were very mid when I wrote them.

Dr. Amy Liu was a very good lecturer that kept her students entertained and intrigued throughout classes. The weekly discussion sections were also a great time to go over lecture materials and the quizzes often got content directly from the lectures so if you paid attention you were fine. She was very generous with her grading and often gave 100s.

Dr. Liu is an amazing professor! I took this class for the credit, but the content she covers is honestly really interesting. Write down what she says WORD FOR WORD during the lectures, because the quizzes are fully based on what she says. My TA graded a bit hard on the first essay, but after that you'll figure out her expectations for the essays.

Great UGS! Lectures and class content were extremely interesting, and weekly quizzes were almost rote what was taught in class.  Dr. Liu is also wonderful. She brought us breakfast burritos and pineapple bread to sweeten the 8 AM once! You will need to write 4 essays in class, but follow the rubric and you will be fine. No quiz makeups, but drops.

analysis.name: Amanda Hager
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 127 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Hager is the best professor I had during my freshman year. There is a extra credit opportunity that is worth 1 % added to your final course grade by using Piazza frequently. On the last day of class, she gave us 2 points on our final exam just by showing up. She is an amazing lecture and really nice. There is HW due every week. I love her!!!!!!

Amanda is by far the best professor in the math department. She is so nice and cares so much for her students. Her exams are not hard at all if you attend class and do your homework. Exams are quest based with a few free response questions. I took her for M305G AND M408N and it was a great experience. She's amazing.

Dr. Hager is the most involved professor I had during my time at UT. She is absolutely rooting for students to get an A in her class and makes it very possible to do so. Attendance is required once every week or so for the in person assignments, but I'd say to go as often as you can because she'll give hw answers in lecture!

She is my unicorn. Her lectures were always well prepared and easy to follow. I always felt comfortable asking my questions in class, and she was also accessible outside of class. I genuinely believe she cared about me, and she graded a lot of work with individualized comments, which I appreciated.

hager gives a lot of resources throughout the year (hw, textbook questions, in class practice, test reviews) for you to succeed. would recommend going to class as much as possible for proper understanding of the material. pretty content heavy after midterm 2, but doable if you keep up with hw and do the final exan review. overall, def recommend!!

analysis.name: Amy Thompson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Easy class with clear grading expectations. Make sure to put effort into the weekly discussion posts, show up to section meetings, and go to most lectures because attendance is taken randomly. I wasn't super interested in this class but Professor Thompson did a good job teaching and I would definitely recommend her if you need to take this class.

One of the best classes I've taken. Only thing you have to worry about is your participation grade in the discussion sections since they weigh heavy. Most of the class work is made up weekly DBs over the topic of the week. Exams (2 total) are easy if you follow the review provided.  Keep track of deadlines, attend class and you should be fine.

Sweetest prof and truly cares about what she teaches + she's pretty quick to respond outside of class. There are short participation assignments at the end of lecture once in a while and the exams are really easy if you prepare (class Avg. ~90). Around 10 EC opportunities, each worth 0.5 pts for a max of 2.5 pts on your overall grade.

The professor is a great lecturer, and the class is pretty easy. Not a lot of homework, just reading and discussions. The worst part is that she takes attendance on random dates, so you really want to go to every lecture, and the discussion sections feel a bit useless to me. Overall, though, really good professor and class, 8.5/10
Very sweet, engaging lectures, comprehensive, kind. Reasonable with grading and assignments. This was a very good intro GRG class.

analysis.name: Amy Howard
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's very caring! There are three exams (40%) that are fill-in-the-blank. The rest of the class is composed of daily discussion boards at the end of lectures, a few in-class assignments, and a few outside-of-class papers. They are great buffers to the hard exams. If you put in the work, you will succeed (don't rely on the study guide, though).

She has been one of the kindest professors I've had. While the material can be challenging, if you pay attention and study, you will be fine. You can tell that she cares a lot about each student and wants to see everyone succeed, so utilize office hours if you need! She is also funny and very relatable, which makes class enjoyable.

She is super sweet and kind, as well as funny and relatable!! Class consists of 3 exams, the final one being cumulative; it's a lot of information given to you in lectures, so study well because the exams are the majority of the grade. There will be extra credit, I suggest doing all of them.

analysis.name: Amy Meeks
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Meeks is a very good intro teacher; the class is very lecture-heavy, and you have to pay attention to succeed on the tests. She offers a lot of extra credit, but there is a lot of McGraw-Hill.

Dr. Meek is the sweetest lady ever! She treats her students like they're her children in a way. Anyways...she is very EASY! Tests are basically just like her powerpoints so reading the book is not really necessary but it does help. It was an easy A for me. I would reccomend her!
Had plenty of time to take notes by hand. She's adorable, and grades fairly. Show up, take notes, and you'll be sure to get an A+. Ended up with a 100 in the class.  Loved her.

I love all things psychology and I couldn't handle this class, it was so boring. You just went to class and filled in powerpoint slides she would give you, you also have to use a laptop because she goes way to quickly to take by hand. Her lectures go along with the book so if you don't go to class you can use that. She gives a lot of extra credit.

She was a  nice lady. The book is not necessary as the exams are mainly based off her PowerPoints. They're very straight-forward, so as long as you pay attention and read your notes a couple of times, you should EASILY get an A. Only issue about her is that her lectures usually ended late. She gives extra credit for papers and perfect attendance.

analysis.name: Aquasia Shaw
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
(-) Seems like a cool person ig but that's all I can say
(+) Terrible at letting us know if class was in-person or zoom. Bad at giving instructions for in-class assignments & knocked off points for instructions she never gave. Never posted slides or study guides despite exams being lecture heavy. Same as last years reviews, just overall, bad.

Worst class I have taken. It is EXTREMELY unorganized, does not follow the syllabus, gives major assignments with hardly any guidance, horrible communication, and tough grading. She never posted lecture slides. Not to mention she threw a dry erase marker across the room at a student for whispering with no previous warning. Awful class.

I feel bad giving her a poor rating, but I feel like there were a lot of things wrong with her class and teaching style. She didn't really teach us anything. She was more of a facilitator for our group projects while grading us unreasonably hard and giving little to no instruction. I feel like with time, she'll get better, but 355 was a disaster.
