such a hard grader and her feedback makes 0 sense. She will take off 10+ points off of a paper for the SMALLEST thing and papers are a large percentage of your grade. assignments had absolutely no criteria or guidance. VERY political and I was afraid to speak out for the opposite position because she would've taken it out against me and my grade.

She is really disorganized and you really don't know your grade in the class until the end of the semester. The class does not follow the syllabus. She threw us into assignments and projects with little to no guidance and she grades harshly. Not a mean lady like the other comment claims, just really disorganized.

analysis.name: Arturo Jimenez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He cares very deeply about film and teaches it well. He also is slightly eviI. He has high expectations and tweaks if there's low engagement  He treats this as a weed-out class, forgetting that he actually teaches an INTRO class.

Arturo was a good professor. He kept the class engaged and did his best to encourage student participation. Students sometimes won't answer, and it'll make the atmosphere awkward at times, but other than that, as long as you have a good TA, you should be good. Be sure you take this class seriously and make work you're proud of.

Arturo is an okay professor! His lectures are often surface-level but sometimes he goes more in depth on some interesting industry topics like film festivals etc. He often seemed uninterested in teaching the class and like he hated it LOL but this class definitely does teach you vital things to go into film production. Just wish he dived deeper :/

Professor Jimenez is my favorite professor I've had so far! His lectures were so informative and helpful to get an intro understanding of the industry. 
He is so passionate about film, which might be his only flaw. It seems like he expects everyone to be as passionate as he is, which is understandable since he's teaching hundreds of film students.

Prof. Jimenez is extremely passionate about the film industry, sometimes to a fault. Lectures are informative and fun, but he will get verbally upset if students do not engage with his lecture/answer questions often enough. The 3 film projects are tough to organize but are graded fairly, and the TA's give lots of incredible feedback on your work.

analysis.name: Arjun Sobnack
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sobnack doesn't know what he's doing at all, ever. If he's as good at rock climbing as he is at teaching, he's a subpar climber at best. It is possible to do well because of the generous curve, especially if you've taken Calc BC before. He is so creative, he can make even the easiest topic seem impossible.

Sobnack does have super hard tests/quiz, mainly b/c he uses odd symbols and sometimes Q's are more theoretical than hard calculations (lot of proofs, Q's don't use numbers but symbols instead) You might be shocked by the first quiz, but literally trust the curve and you'll likely be ok. This class WILL make you smarter & I appreciate in retrospect.

Nice guy, but unable to communicate his knowledge of math to students. He kinda fixed this and started a curve (60->90). No recorded lectures. Practice sets weren't provided until the night before a quiz/exam, and often came w/o solutions & were unreflective of the exam. Homework is unreflective of exam. Graded only by tests, quizzes, and homework.

VERY difficult class to stay motivated in; NOT recommended if you're new to Calc 2. Very DIY w/ resources beyond lecture. It's you, Quest, & the textbook. Exam Qs are hard to understand & impossible to solve in time. Exams: 3 FRQs with 2-4 parts each. If you miss one, the next may be impossible. Nice Prof. Avoid or commit to a life of uncertainty.

chill guy but makes me want to kms so bad. genuinely got diddled by every quiz/test in this class. the in class examples are like not too bad but then the quiz and tests have GENIUNELY been dug out of the deepest depths of his bootyhole. he meekly chuckles and tries to be helpful. silly guy but AT WHAT COST. he also rock climbs which is pretty tuff

analysis.name: Arielle Woznica
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of my favorite classes I've ever taken! She's a great lecturer and the material is interesting itself. Course is a bit more self driven because the grade is mostly exam heavy and homework/instapoll is completion, but she provides a lot of help if you seek it and she is constantly available. Exams are fair, and she offers a bit of extra credit.

Really great professor, it's obvious she's very passionate about cell biology and as long as you keep up with the material throughout the semester you will do fine. Super knowledgable and very approachable outside class. There's a big emphasis on designing experiments that demonstrate cellular processes so the class isn't just brute memorization

Taught cell biology in a cool way. You need to go to class to do well, attendance isn't "mandatory" but it probably is in order to be prepared for exams. Very accessible outside of class and was always willing to explain things in class and not make you feel silly.

analysis.name: Arianna Avalle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Avalle had been my all time favorite professor. Throughout the semester, she not only wanted me to succeed, but she went out of her way to make sure that I understood the material. She was very reachable outside of class and during office hours. I cannot say enough nice things about her. Often, she brought homemade treats to class.

I noticed that one of the reviews stated that Professor Avalle “tries too hard to be liked”. This is actually a positive! Professor Avalle goes out of her way to get to know the needs and ambitions of each individual student. She always tries to form a bond with each of her students and it is evident that she deeply cares!

I would definitely take intro to Italian with Arianna again if given the chance, she is such a kind professor and understanding! You can tell she has a passion for what she does, I really enjoyed this class despite having zero previous Italian knowledge. I found that the class flowed nicely and modules were easy to follow! 10/10 recommend beginners

analysis.name: Arvind  Ravikumar
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Worst Prof Ive had so far. Super unprofessional, did not release a guide to our on paper coding midterm until TWO DAYS before it, so we had no idea what to expect. Kept saying he would release solutions to final guide and NEVER DID. failed to prepare us for HW so AI was a must even though it was 'forbidden'. I maybe got an A but I learned nothing.

The professor is knowledgeable in the subject and is kind to students. However, the class focusses so much on the math and the theory behind numerical methods that when it comes time to do real problems it often seems impossible to accomplish by oneself. Homework at the beginning of the course easily took 4 hours each week however lighten later.

Lectures do not help you with the homework or tests. He spends much more time explaining the intricacies of numerical methods than teaching you how to translate word problems to coding problems, which is really what the tests are about. He doesnt teach coding well, but expects everyone to know how to do it, then he is surprised when no one does.

analysis.name: Astrid Runggaldier
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I accidentally took an upper-division art history class as a freshman, so this class was a bit tough for me. Dr. Runggaldier is pretty vague in her directions and I received some pretty poor grades because of misinterpretations. She uses lecture slides but they don't have text on them, just photos, so it's not really helpful for exam reviewing.

She obviously is very knowledgeable in her field; her class is reading, and lecture heavy. The majority of your grade is dependent on a multi-part project throughout the semester, and if you are not accustomed to writing for art it can be a learning curve, if you are thinking about this class for your VAPA I would recommend something easier.

This professor is a very harsh grader. EOY project is worth so much, but she has never given anybody a 100 on a single section of the project that was submitted (I checked the Canvas median). The tests aren't that hard, but what kills is you are the essays that are apparently "never perfect". Please don't take if you scared of getting a A- or B+.

AMAZING PROF!! Best choice I could have made for first semester VAPA. She cares about student understanding of the material and constantly asks for feedback. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll have to attend every lecture and read the textbook to do well. Material is incredibly interesting and she makes lectures engaging. Would take again!

I have never felt so disrespected or afraid of a professor in my entire life. I genuinely dread going to class and facing her wrath and I am a good, dedicated student. I do NOT recommend taking a course with her. She's not blunt, she's demeaning. Does not shy away from humiliating students, so the discussions are usually silent out of pure fear.

analysis.name: Ashley Matheny
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr Matheny is the sweetest professor and really cares about her students. She tells you pretty much exactly what is on the exams. Two midterms and a semester project, easy peasy. She moves due dates if she feels her students are too busy. Great lecturer as well, definitely recommend!

Dr. Matheny is an incredible professor! I thoroughly enjoyed taking her Intro to Hydro course. Although I got a B, I would absolutely take another class with her, as my B was due to my own personal issues. She was very helpful and understanding, and her lectures were entertaining even online. You can tell she is very passionate and knowledgeable.

Dr. Matheny is a great professor. She is easy to listen to, and makes her lectures interesting. The class isn't super hard, as long as you pay attention during lecture. Assignments were always graded quickly and fairly, and she is super accommodating if you need anything. Would definitely recommend taking any of her class, she is such a gem!

I loved this course and Dr. Matheny. She worked with students to make sure that everything was fair, assignments were graded within a week (usually within a few days), and she is just such a fun person. Definitely one of my absolute favorite professors. You can really tell that she cares about her students over grading

Amazing lecturer and always ready to help everyone understand anything, inside or outside of the classroom. Gives lots of examples for 'real life' career/scientist skills. Creates a community feeling around projects and research! Would definitely take her class again!

analysis.name: Ashley Farmer
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Farmer is one of the best professors I have had. She has so much passion and energy for African American history. Lectures were so engaging and insightful. There is a-lot of reading that is assigned, but most of it was interesting and it is helpful to do well in the class. You will learn alot. Put in effort and it will be worth it.

Dr. Farmer is an amazing professor who really just does it for the love of the game. She can be a little bit harsh at times but its always out of love. She is a relatively easy grader and her classes are amazing. I hope i get to take her class again. Only gripe was one of her assignments required use of AI.

I took AFR 360 (black freedom movement) and this was one of my favorite classes, being a math major. She made the class amazing with her genuine personality and being so funny. Lots of reading but she makes sure you succeed if you demonstrate that you're trying. Easy exams and easy papers if you spend at least a few days researching and writing.

Very good professor and class. She lectures very well and profoundly. She knows the material very well, and it is easy to succeed. Instapolls, short in-class assignments, and a couple tests make up the grade. I wish she gave us more material to study with for the tests, but not really necessary.

My favorite professor I took this past semester! Dr. Farmer is an amazing teacher, and her enthusiasm made waking up early completely worth it! She's a fantastic storyteller, and she's able to help students realize the importance of learning from history. Attend class, take detailed notes, and study before quizzes/tests - you will do great!

analysis.name: Ashley  Moran
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Moran is awesome, very knowledgeable in her field, and cares about her students. Participate in class discussions, as she keeps a very close eye on who talks and uses that to determine participation grades. Tests are short answer questions that aren't hard if you pay attention in class. The readings will help but you don't NEED them to pass.
She is a very caring professor, but the class it pretty content heavy and tests can be tough. You definitely have to do the readings and work hard.
Kindest professor ever! Easy, fair grader and very caring of her students. The content is very interesting and presented in a way that is easy to understand and remember. Would recommend!

One of the best Professors I have ever had. She genuinely cares about the content and her students and is an amazing lecturer. Weekly discussion posts over assigned readings are due every Sunday but are mostly completion grades and cover material discussed in the following lectures. I've never retained so much from a class I loved it!

Professor Moran is a great professor who is extremely knowledgeable about the course content. There are lots of dense readings every week to get through and a weekly reaction discussion post. Lectures can be a bit slow at times, but the course is super interesting and enjoyable. Professor Moran is very helpful and wants you to succeed!

analysis.name: Mihran Aroian
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 163 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment:
The workload is so much for a 3 credit class that it's borderline disrespectful to students. 
I had a 6 credit class with the same amount of homework, if not less. I will lose my scholarship if I drop it but if I could go back and not take it, I would 100% avoid it.

This class was the most annoyingly difficult course I've taken. Not because the material is difficult to understand, but because the exams are near impossible due to the sheer amount of detail and random topics included from a vast amount of readings, articles, case studies, and slow/long/boring debriefing/lecture videos. DON'T take this class!
I got 60 points taken often for not writing my name, are you serious?? dude needs to get laid. please do not take this class, like run rn. literally take any  other class.

Currently in his class and he is easily the worst professor I have ever had at UT. Has the highest materials fee of any professor ($150) and gives way too many assignments and homework for a 3 credit class. I have a 4 credit class with less homework than his. Dude is so paranoid about cheating he mentions it in every single paragraph and assignment

The most expensive, time-consuming, and confusing class I've taken here at UT. The exams are heavily opinion-based, and the course content is relatively easy. The issue lies in how the course is structured, how things are graded, and how the lectures and exams don't align in any sense.

analysis.name: Ashley Coleman Taylor
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Taylor was very organized and clear on her expectations. Was graded on 4 short papers (1 page or so), a video, and a reply video. As long as you read the assignment in detail and hit each point, you will succeed.

Dr. Coleman Taylor is an exemplary educator. She embodies a pedagogical ethos that is in alignment with the intersectional feminist theory she teaches. She treats students as people first, which can be rare to find at the university level. Her feedback is insightful and she challenges you to always dig deeper. You will leave class a different you.

THE BEST PROFESSOR IVE EVER HAD! It was an honor to be taught by Dr. Coleman Taylor. She teaches a thought-provoking, inclusive curriculum that expands upon typical cis, white, male narratives She is also incredibly knowledgeable, often invites amazing guest speakers, and truly cares about her students. I highly recommend her classes.
Very little details or feedback and she doesn't keep up with grades so you never know where you stand in the class. I was scared to speak up in class because she could be very condescending.

analysis.name: Ash D'Harcourt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was fun and engaging. The way Prof Ash structured and paced the course was intuitive and low-stakes, allowing you to focus on the content without stressing about your grade. Grading was very fair, and the TAs consistently provided helpful feedback.
rtf308 is so easy and the TAs are pretty lenient on grading!! be prepared to write essays but other than that its a great vapa

This class was low stress and taught in a way that made it a great intro to going to college. The lectures were all genuinely amusing, and the asynchronous format was really accommodating. The exams were open note and easy as long as you took good notes from the lectures, and the grading criteria for the writing assignments was incredibly clear.

I loved Ash's class! Ten out of ten - one of the sweetest profs I've had at UT. There were at least 10x during the semester that I laughed out loud at a joke they cracked during lecture. Super entertaining to listen to and the lectures were pre-recorded which was great for my full schedule. You can tell they really care about their students.

I love Ash!! Such an incredible professor who really cares about their students. They were always super responsive to emails and there were at least 10x during the semester that I laughed out loud at something funny they said in the lecture. TAKE ASH'S CLASS!! It's asynchronous online, so watch the pre-recorded lectures whenever in the week.

analysis.name: Lucy Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: No tests, we don't even take notes in class. Just come and listen and engage in the lecture, and you're all good. Homework and projects outside of class aren't too bad either. Definitely take her if you can.

They fell kind of behind so felt like everything was pushed back at last second but outside of that the professor is nice but this class was just a class I decided to take outside of my major so any grade I may have gotten because of that is on me.

The sweetest professor ever, take this class!!! Her class is so laid back and chill. Assignments are simple and easy, projects are also very straightforward. This class is a relief and I actually learned a lot.
0 extra credit. Will give an A- if 0.1 decimals off an A

As an engineering major, this was a nice class. laid back, discussion based. Just do your part in group projects and keep up with assignments. Dr. Atkinson (who prefers Lucy) is witty and engaging with her lectures. Breath of fresh air.

analysis.name: ATILA NOVOSELAC
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Only thing I disliked about the class was the enormous 1" = 1' model we had to make, which cost like $100 (divided by 5 people). Other than that, the class was chill and easy with cool speakers.

Professor Novoselac is an outstanding introduction to architectural engineering. He is extremely knowledgeable, friendly, understanding, and very approachable. The guest lecture panels throughout the course were especially useful. One time, when our projects were accidentally thrown away by a janitor, he even bought the entire class Ferrero Rocher!

Professor Novoselac is a very nice person, and he tried to help all of us navigate the beginnings of ARE. The guest lecturers were interesting. Sometimes the material was disorganized. The group project took a long time to complete, so think ahead for that. Very nice beginning to Architectural Engineering for me!

This is a great guy. Super chill and easiest class I've taken. Tests are all open book/open note, project 1 was a little tedious but everything else was super easy. Even though this class was really chill, I think I got a lot out of the guest speakers. Take advantage of the opportunity to learn in this class!!

Lectures included guest speakers who has slides we would take notes on. Notes would be turned in at the end of the year (I love that he made us take notes because I could not tell you one thing a presenter said from the top of my head but it was useful ArchE stuff). Group project was somewhat hard, but office hours helped and buy materials aheaddd.

analysis.name: Wang Atlas
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall this was a really great class. Prof posts all of his slides with the concepts very clearly described. Wasn't the best lecturer imo but going to lecture isn't necessary to gain a lot from the class. Homeworks and final project took a lot of time, but overall were worth it.

Professor Wang is a true legend and perhaps the smartest person I've ever encountered. 

Unlike many professors who just read textbooks, he teaches effortlessly from his vast knowledge. He's engaging, incredibly kind, and adaptable, always happy to take questions and meet student needs. 

Such a pity UT cannot keep him teaching longer!

Besides the fact that he is one of the best researchers in his field, Prof. Wang is also a great teacher! He has very well-organized lectures and is a grandmaster describing the intuition of the material.
Lectures are fun. The class is not all that difficult, but Prof. Wang does go in depth in lectures and is very willing to dive deep into specific things the class asks.

analysis.name: Nigel Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Do not take Atkinson. His lectures are so convoluted that you can easily get confused even if you already understand the material from the textbook. You have to decipher what his tests are asking and you probably won't pass unless you memorize the whole book or have his old exams. Thankfully I had a wonderful TA so that's the only reason I passed.

Neuroepigenetics- This is a hard class but if you do the homework and the study guides (which are basically the tests), an A is very achievable. He is very knowledgeable but a little hard to understand, will clarify when asked. We had 2 group poster projects that are worth as much as the test, and are easy to get an A for if you follow the rubric.

Hard class. If you can read for yourself and understand the material, you can get an A. The tests are difficult. He doesn't add anything to his lectures, so it is almost pointless to go; it'd be better to just spend that time reading the book. Half of the test question are from old homeworks/old tests and the other half are new.

CONS:
The epigenetics class was: VERY DISORGANIZED, had no clear rubric/expectations, and the grades were returned WEEKS later. It is PROJECT HEAVY ( 4 presentations and a Wikipedia article). 
PROS:
He grades presentations/ article relative to others/yourself/ and level of effort. The practice exams ARE the exams (still hard though). An A is doable

He is a nice guy, but his lectures are painfully boring. His tests are difficult, and he writes them aiming for a 70-72 average. He does not curve or use plus/ minus grading. The class was disorganized and the expectations were unclear. You pretty much learn from your book and TA. I consider myself a strong bio student, but struggled in this class.

analysis.name: Lucinda Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Her lectures are really helpful and easy to understand. She is engaging and gives you bonus questions that are super easy if you came to class!

Dr. Lucy is the BEST! She makes the lectures interesting and provides plenty of in-class extra credit. You do have to read the books for the tests, but luckily they're pretty interesting. She really enjoys discussions too, sometimes we would get so busy discussing in class that we would end up having to cut information off of the tests!

This class was okay. It definitely was not hard by any means but i will say there is a lot of work you need to do. Each module takes an hour to two hours to complete so it definitely sucked doing those but most of the stuff is things you will see on the exam. I read the textbook sometimes but mostly never and still got an A.

I loved this class and i loved her as a professor. She makes the class fun and easy to understand. Also the tests were easy as long as you read your notes and sometimes textbook. Attendance not mandatory but the bonus questions were based on class lectures. it was an easy A.

I'm not a business major, was thrown into this class (since another was cancelled 2 days before classes started) but could not be happier. She really kept this class interesting and fun, and gave plenty of opportunities to succeed. Read the book, take good notes, and you'll get an A+, and you'll actually enjoy yourself. Favorite professor so far!

analysis.name: Rowland Atiase
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Atiase is by far my least favorite professor I have ever taken. His sarcastic attempts at humor seem to demean students more often than encourage or amuse them. You come to class to copy down verbal notes which could be posted online instead. Homework is explained, in a confusing, hard to understand manner, leaving you to learn on your own.

This class consists of you doing a ton of reading and written homework/handouts before class (at least 2 hrs for each "lecture"), coming to class to copy notes verbatim that he won't post online, and then getting called on to answer the questions you did before class without a good explanation. You have to teach yourself--just avoid altogether

Don't do it! Claims that he doesn't give us busy work, but that is all he gives us. Teaches too fast, and has the audacity to call exams "parties". He is a very smart guy, as he's worked at some very high up companies in the world, but teaching just isn't his thing. Avoid him at all costs please, unless you are feeling like a risk-taker.

Prof Atiase may not be my favorite professor ever, but he definitely is not as bad as the other reviews here make him out to be. There is a lot of written homework due before each class, but it is completion and he just wants you to attempt it before actually seeing the solutions in class. Tests are very similar to the review problems which is nice

Homework structure supports memorization, not learning. Lectures are worthless fill-in-the-blank notes that he reads from. He either assigns busy work or problems that he has not prepared you to complete. Hard to understand due to accent. Only reason I did okay was bc his test was near identical to the review. Lots of wasted time in class. ACC 312H

analysis.name: Florence Atiase
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is pretty tough and not just because of the subject matter. It's how she grades. I really wish I took this class with a different professor! Avoid, if you can.
Sometimes hard to understand and hard to follow in lectures. Also, very uninteresting to listen to because of the way she teaches
Her class was very difficult but she did a great job of making difficult material more easy to understand.
A very good professor, helpful, good explanations.

analysis.name: Athanasio Papalexandrou
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The prof is great but the older reviews exaggerate how easy the class is- you need to work for an A. Lectures are recorded & there are mandatory labs w/ weekly response papers (completion grade). TAs grade the first exam harshly, and you need to rewatch the lectures and pay attention to catch the details they want you to mention on exams

Definitely not as easy as the previous reviews have claimed, but the class was doable. T/F and MCQs felt like random trivia questions at times, but the writing portions were easy as long as you keep up with lectures and discussion sessions. Grading varies by TA, mine graded harshly initially but became more lenient as the semester progressed.

You can tell he really cares about what he teaches, he's passionate and that makes lectures interesting. There is a lot of reading needed for the class and the lab but it's very manageable if you're good at writing. The workload is light! I very much recommend the class, you don't need to go to the lectures as long as you watch them online.

Took two semesters of his art history classes. Easy grading; wrote a terrible-quality paper and still got a B on it. Incredibly kind and genuinely wants to get to know his students. Very thick accent that is both endearing and a bit hard to understand. He is super passionate about the subject, which helps if you are not interested in art.

Such a cute prof. Kind of funny, referred to Augustus of Prima Porta as incredibly sexy. Was absent one day, and came to office hours once and he spent the entire time going over the presentation. Caring prof. Greek accent takes a while to get used to. ATTEND LECTURES!!! Grading is P/F for lab questions and from tests. No final either.

analysis.name: August Shi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Useless lectures, self-taught course/no guidance, unclear project requirements, no announcements on canvas, expected to check Piazza to do well/pass, harder projects than other profs, unreasonable expectations, not understanding/flexible, no Test reviews, unorganized exams, doesn't use IDE, unlear answers to questions, taught like a grad course.

This Prof has useless lectures and is not understanding at all. He doesn't have practice exams and doesn't send out announcements that are crucial to passing assignments/the class.The lack of coordination among the professor and their TAs has negative consequences on students' grades. Take a different professor if you can.
The best faculty I've ever met.

He's definitely knowledgeable and speaks with coherence and confidence, but I found that I had to do a lot of learning after lectures to comprehend the concepts. Granted, that could be an issue on my part. Workload was manageable, but there would be 0 feedback left on assignments, which was odd. Advice: watch Coding With John and Bro Code!!

Definitely take Nando over him
-Next to no review material for exams, only one previous exam. Actual exam was way harder, ~70 avg no curve
-Tests and projects are much harder than other profs
-No in class test review or exam prep guidance
-Useless lectures, don't help with projects, just end up self studying 
Overall way harder than it should be

analysis.name: Celest Austin
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is SOOO nice. Got super lucky with registering for her class for Fall 2024. Individual exams are 45% with the rest of the grade being group exams, group work, and instapoll. IMO the groups were big enough so that at least a few ppl could be on top of things, and even though the exams were hard, they weren't weighed heavily + small curves!

She is such an amazing teacher and lecturer. She breaks down every concept completely from scratch so that everything is very digestible and easy to understand, and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students understanding the material by the quality of her explanations and slides.

Dr Austin is so kind and a great lecturer. She's so smart and passionate about physiology and teaching. She makes it attainable to know the material and understand it. The way she did group homework assignments was helpful and group exams were extremely helpful as well. She's so accessible outside of class as well as her TA's and they're so helpful

Dr. Austin was awesome. She encouraged us to truly understand physiology by forming connections rather than simply memorizing facts. Most of our grade was derived from group assignments (weekly homework, iClicker, group exams). As much as I dreaded physiology entering the class, I left with a love of the subject and a deeper understanding as well.

Dr. Austin is THE BEST. Study for exams by using HER lecture and exam review slides, explaining the concepts to yourself, as well as doing the practice problems for math-related topics/questions. She has learning objectives from another prof which you can do for extra practice but you should mostly focus on her slides and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Jennifer Austin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved Austin as a professor and she made the class more intriguing and forced you to be involved. Charismatic and light personality and brough positive vibes into every lecture. Take her for any class that you can because if you mess up, she is very generous and tells you exactly where you went wrong. Avg/easy HW and Exam difficulty, long HW's.

A very nice professor. The homeworks are insanely difficult, but she has tons of documents available to help with the homework. The tests are exactly like the test reviews and she is very helpful in getting people prepared for the tests. She doesn't explain some of the in depth concepts the best, but you at least understand how to do the problems.

One of the few amazing teachers at the ut math department, She breaks down complex proof topics into easy to understand lectures and practice problems. Tests were not too bad if you studied for them, and did the review problems. A lot of extra credit was given if you participated in class problems and presentation problems, definitely a must take.

Dr. Austin is really nice and creates an environment where you can focus on learning without worrying about your grade. Her guidance is great, and she is a must take professor to enjoy your intro to proofs class. Overall 100% recommend taking her.

This review is for M 175T, Being You in Mathematics. It is indeed rather boring. However, I cannot deny that it is applicable to math majors, even pure math majors. Take this class to get your ethics flag done and perhaps learn a bit more about the major in the process.

analysis.name: Andrew Augustin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Media and Technology. Very interesting class! Learned so much about level design and the art that goes into making 2-d games in Unity. Definitely great for beginners such as myself. It was a lot of work but! It was fun work and not agonizing work, very simple and got a 100 in the class, very easy grading too.

I don't want to be biased, but honestly professor Augustin is the best teacher that I have had in my entire life. He goes above and beyond not only for his work and projects, but also for his students. He is always watching out for you and may come off as having high expectations, but genuinely its because he cares.

Design&Interactivity is focused on creating a character, an environment, and then making a game based off of that in Unity. I never attended the in person sessions (class was held once a week online) and despite taking that blow to my grade, still ended with an A. As long as you try you'll do great. Prof Augustin himself is super cool and laidback!

Love Professor Augustin! He makes it clear that you will get a good grade as long as you try your best, and he is super understanding when you have other things going on. He's also generally very cool and funny. I'm taking another one of his classes next semester because he was so nice to be around.

analysis.name: Audrey Duarte
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
*This rating is for PSY 332S*
 I was very optimistic about taking Neuroscience of Sleep; however, Professor Duarte was extremely condescending when I asked for feedback. She had daily quizzes over readings, and you had only 5 minutes to answer the question in full paragraph form, which had to have extremely proper grammar that made sense to her.

I did really well in Psychopharmacology with Duarte but not because of any help she provided. Her lectures are really interesting and the topic is fascinating, but Duarte doesn't provide ANY resources to study except for in class slide shows. I  passed with an A+ by making hundreds of flashcards for each test covering every sentence on every slide.

I found her class harder than expected- it definitely requires studying to do well. There were 2 lectures a week (which were fairly dense), but she was very willing to help out outside of class hours with more than just the class, which i appreciated. She's a good professor and knows what she's doing- just make sure you put the time in the class.

She is really smart but just doesn't know how to teach a class. The only assignments in the class was a paper and a few in class quizzes with one question. The tests are like trying to win trivia. No emphasis on what you need to know, and she tests very randomly. It is a strange combination of neuroscience, history, etymology, and geography.

Grade is based primarily on 4 exams. While you can drop one exam from your final grade, her exams are very difficult. She is very lecture heavy and so you need to be prepared to be a good note taker as her slides aren't sufficient and she doesn't record her lectures. Took a huge chunk of study time and effort. I wouldn't take her again.

analysis.name: Audrey Blood
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Audrey made me fall in love with printmaking. Truly the perfect professor for intro to print. Jumping between four types of printmaking in one semester seemed overwhelming in my head, but audrey and our TA noah made it so doable and fun. She is so knowledgeable about processes, concepts, and history of print. You must take print if she's teaching!

I love Audrey. She is incredibly well prepared always and organized. Is knowledgeable about almost all printmaking but especially Intaglio and papermaking. She gives fantastic support, feedback, and suggestions (artists, films, books, poems, research, etc.) Her class discussions were so insightful and fun. Such a wonderfully kind educator as well.
Loved this class!! Audrey is so nice and is so helpful. She definitely helped me with my drawing skills. I would recommend any art class given by her.

analysis.name: Audrey Shaffer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Shaffer is very kind, and is a very good professor. She gives very specific feedback, and provides extra credit. She's also willing to work with every student. Attendance is mandatory, but it makes up a big chunk of your grade and is easy points. She's amazing, I love her. My speaking has improved a lot because of this class.

Prof Shaffer is a professor that really only wants to see you do good. Understands all the pop culture references and is really respectful to all her students. Can have a good laugh while still being productive and will answer any questions you have. Class is not difficult, but it is time consuming.I do recommend mainly due to Prof Shaffer.

This class helped me (mostly) get over my fear of public speaking! Prof Shaffer was very kind and encouraging to all of her students and allowed us to give speeches based on our actual interests instead of just boring assigned topics. If you're going to take this class, make sure you get Prof Shaffer as your instructor.

I wish I could stay in this class forever. I loved Prof Shaffer so much. She cares for her students like no other professor I've had, and her feedback was always helpful. This is an amazing class that I think everyone should take (and definitely try to take it with Audrey Shaffer)!

analysis.name: Javier Auyero
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 82 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Javier is HILARIOUS and so knowledgable. He explains things incredibly elegantly in a way that's super easy to understand. Pop quizzes can sneak up on you, but if you listen, he usually gives the answers in lecture. There's a lot of reading, but you can get by just using his explanations. Definitely one of the coolest professors ever.
This class was super intensive and not as easy or a blow-off class. You seriously have to put in work. ALOT of reading and be ready(and beware) for POP quizzes.

Very interesting (albeit boring) class and the prof was great. Attendance during main lecture isn't mandatory, TA sessions (required, but chill). Quizzes were light (gives answers in class usually), reading was so long and boring but you can get away w/ not reading (goes over in class),and essays were long but light. better than other ugs - easy A.

He is amazing, I will always recommend. You have 2 papers and like 4/5 quizzes, lowest one is dropped. He gives you all the answers before the quiz. Show up to every lecture and you will be fine. He is so amazing and funny. The best class I had all semester. TA meetings seem a bit useless but it was nice getting to know them. Overall, take Javier.

Attendance is only mandatory for discussion sections. Very generous and understanding to students. I didn't actually read because he would always go over the answers and readings for the quizzes (he was discussing maybe changing that, but he may not). Very easy and interesting UGS. More controversial topics but if you're into sociology I say do it!

analysis.name: Luis Aviles
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took his beginner level (6week long) Spanish course and was forced to pay 62$ for a program to do work that wasn't even graded. Yet he expected everyone to finish (literally) 12 assignments every day. His lectures were unfocused, and I spent most of my time in breakout rooms w peers. Despite him saying he cared it was abundantly clear he didn't.

The quizzes were a little tricky but he really offers a lot of content to study for both exams and quizzes, and makes class really fun to go to. He engages with each student and genuinely cares for each person's wellbeing. Most fun I've had taking a class in college for a long time, and I will miss this prof

I took SPN 314 with Prof Aviles in summer 2021, and I really enjoyed it. He is super enthusiastic and helpful, and he really cares about the students' learning. There was a lot of homework because it was a summer class, but it wasn't too challenging. Overall, it was a great course and I highly recommend taking it with Prof Aviles!

analysis.name: Kiril Avramov
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Avramov is one of the best professors I have taken at this school. This class is interesting at times but can often be boring and he kept everyone engaged. There is a lot of reading but quizzes and tests are open note/book so you don't have to do it all the time, but it helps. Other assignments are short discussion posts. Take this class!

Avramov is one of the greats! Engaging lectures, fascinating material, really genuine guy. My only critique is that the class allows students to succeed without learning the material. Ex- tests are online, hw only covers part of the reading. Bc of this, his class ended up on the back-burner. I wish he demanded more, bc I know I had more to give!

Professor Avramov is super awesome, the lectures are very engaging and this class is super relevant to current events. Discussions are lively and students are super welcomed to share their opinions. Would hundred percent recommend for everyone to take it - one of my favorite classes and professors here at UT!

Dr. Avramov is definitely one of the best professors at UT!! He is the most caring and passionate professor I've had. Cares more about the students actually learning than the grades. There were three exams and two discussions a month based on readings. However, he is pretty lenient and doesn't want to add stress to his students. Take his class

He was one of the best professors I have ever had in college. He is so passionate about these topics that he is teaching which makes it so enjoyable to go to class and learn. Even though it is a big lecture class, he makes an effort to get to know all of his students. Great experience. I am taking another one of his classes next semester.

analysis.name: Avigail Noy
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took her arabian nights class, and really loved it. the class is interesting, and Noy is very knowledgeable. she is a hard grader, however, and sometimes frustratingly so -- a few times i thought about throwing my computer out the window. LOTS of reading. too much. not burdensome, though. overall, id recommend for people interested.

Honestly one of the best professors I've had. The content was phenomenal and she is such a kind professor. It is reading heavy and discussion based so make sure to read or at least skim. No tests however there are 4 written assignments and weekly journals, but so far they have not given me any issue and 2 of the papers are only 2 pages long.

Took Arabic Lit. Highly difficult class yet rewarding -- you learn a lot! Readings are super difficult. Noy's lectures are amazing and she is easy to reach outside of class and understanding. PLEASE CONTRIBUTE IN THIS CLASS. It's small and discussion based, don't take it if you're not ready to talk. DO THE READINGS, she likes to see effort!

analysis.name: Ronen Avraham
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Uses Socratic method to a fault, basically to have students teach for him. Grades are completely arbitrary and he provides no feedback. I received high A's on all homework papers (no feedback provided), and this was completely inconsistent with the final grade. He spent half a class arguing he should be allowed to buy votes. Not approachable.
Prof. Avraham is really sweet and loves torts.  He explains a lot of things at a level even a 5 year old could understand. Some other readings were hard to understand.  Overall, highly recommended.
Avraham is funny and makes class enjoyable.  I had him for Torts. He really covers everything he wants you to know during class, so don't miss class!

analysis.name: Nicole Awai
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Nicole is one of the most understanding and caring teachers I've ever had. She tries to make you a better artist even if you cant see it in the beginning you understand at the end of the semester. If you have any concerns about your progress she'll sit down and talk with you even if shes busy. She's really amazing I would take her again in a second

Her assignments are the blandest possible drawing curriculum and being in it is a waste of time. If you are studio major the core class was better than this. Color is rarely allowed, and she makes you draw simple subjects and lighting exercises as if you are a basic beginner, not an art major. Feedback and focus in the classroom felt lacking.

My painting really improved! However, she does not put any feedback or grades into canvas. You have no clue how you are doing until your course grade has been submitted to the registrar. I was excited to take painting 2 however she was extremely rude over email after I asked a genuine question regarding feedback so I dropped the course.
Amazing professor. I went from never life drawing to being amazing at it all because she knew exactly what she was talking about. Highly recommend.

analysis.name: Gigi Awad
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Awad's "Psychology of Women" course was amazing and informative. The topics we went over were really interesting and relevant. There are 3 exams, several pop quizzes throughout the semester (if you pay attention in class, these are easy). Most info for tests comes from lecture, with some material from textbook. Also she's a really cool person.

Dr. Awad is extremely down to earth and understanding. She is very knowledgable on both subjects of the psychology of women and psychology of race/racism. During COVID, she encouraged cameras to be on and attendence is graded. Assignments were critique papers, journals, and tests. I really loved Dr. Awad and feel like I genuinely learned a lot.

Overall, psych of women was great! Interesting and engaging lectures. The exams were challenging and many questions seemed there solely to confuse. Also, Canvas was a mess for this class as it seemed like it was not updated since the previous semester-assignments had multiple due dates and prompts. I was happy with my grade but it was not easy.

Smart. Knows her stuff. Fantastic choices in readings & a diverse array of them, and very up-to-date on the subjects (unlike some profs who reuse old material to the point of absurdity). Very liberal and will expand your (even if already open) mind.

she ROCKS really funny if youre not a liberal just be warned but she is really funny and is a fair grader. she wants her students to do well. PARTICIPATE it shows her you care and she will fight for you more if she sees that

analysis.name: Axel Turnquist
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I sincerely believe a higher power sent Axel Turnquist to punish me for any wrong doing I have ever committed. While Axel is a jolly fellow with clear passion for mathematics, the very last thing he should be doing is teaching. With a current RMP score of 1.9 and difficulty of 4.6, UT should find another use for him immediately.

This professor is a RED FLAG!!! Avoid this professor at all cost. He lack the ability to teach at all, he does not explain concepts, nor does he actually provide resources. Unless you are trying to drop out of college, DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Genuinely might be the worst professor at UT Austin

This is hands down the worst professor I have ever had. He rants about concepts that won't be on the homework or exams for the entirety of class and then grades everything like it's a dissertation. If you think you can teach yourself an upperclass math go ahead - but it will not be fun. He isn't mean, just a terrible professor. UT please fire him.

Regardless of what other reviews say, his grading is NOT lenient. His tests will not match the material and if you want a chance at passing you must read the textbook (which again, is almost as bad as his lectures). 
My grade is wildly different from my peers who took other professors. This seriously needs to be addressed by the Math Department

I thought I was always good at math. I easily surpassed the A grade in every class I took, until I got to this class. This class was a pain. Very theory heavy, and if you don't like that, do NOT take him. His exams are not for people who like applying math, and solving equations.

analysis.name: Omar Awapara
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He uses a powerpoint for all his lectures, which he uploads so it isn't crucial to go to class. However, there are pop quizzes.

Omar is a really nice guy. He uses powerpoints for his lectures, which unless you do the assigned readings, won't make much sense. The assigned readings are kind of a lot, no actual homework or quizzes. The bummer is though, that your final grade is dependent on 4 assignments. Exams are easy if you do the readings, its a make it or break it class.

Really kind professor!!! Make sure to go to most classes because there are pop quizzes sometimes and they are pretty easy so you don't want to miss them. I feel like a lot of people took this simply for the requirement but ended up actually liking the topic a lot so you should definitely take this class! Overall good experience!

Omar is a really great guy, and you can tell he cares about his subject a lot. I was annoyed for most of the class, just because it was a mandatory 8 am with a large amount of reading, but the subject is very interesting. Omar is super friendly and helpful inside/outside class. It doesn't hurt that he's pretty cute as well.

Awapara was a great professor and gave really great lectures. The tests are fairly doable if you pay attention in class and read the assigned readings. You'll also need to do an essay, but it is not that bad.

analysis.name: Marcelo Azambuja
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures were often hard to stay engaged with, and exams were difficult to prepare for. The professor taught this as a second job, so office hours and communication were limited. He was lenient on some assignments and seemed to care about students when approached. I'd recommend relying on the slides to study for the exams and note every detail.

As others have mentioned, Dr. Azambuja works full-time at TxDOT and teaches on the side... but he should probably just stick with TxDOT. He's a pretty unengaging lecturer and is very monotone. The project management material is pretty easy, but his engineering economics lectures are almost unbearable. Exams were straightforward and fair, though.

I went to maybe 6 classes over the course of the semester because it genuinely pained me to listen to this man speak for more than an hour. The content is relatively easy and can be self-taught. I recommend going to the classes before exams because he will talk about what will be tested. Study for tests with hw problems and examples from slides.

If you want a professor that cant teach and will lie to your face and say that he will curve the class but doesn't, Azambuja is the one! All jokes aside, worst teacher I've ever had. All he does is read off the slides with the most monotone voice ever. Doesn't upload slides before class so a lot of ppl skip. All exam avgs were under 75. Good luck.

Honestly one of the worst professors I've ever had, he will not work with you and clearly does not care about the class whatsoever. There's no practice tests so you only have 2 MAYBE 3 homeworks to actually use to study, most of which don't really correlate to the test whatsoever. The most nothingburger class that shouldn't have been difficult.

analysis.name: Dewi Azizah
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's a great and well-intentioned person, but I felt like her lack of organization put me at a disadvantage at times, which I didn't feel was made up for with extra credit. We were given details of the assignments much later than we should've been, and we waited months for grades.

Professor Dewi has been one of my favorite professors on campus. This is a presentation-based class where you will give speeches, typically 1-2 per month. Exams are in person, she provides study guides, and allows us a page of handwritten notes. Assignments are very easy and straightforward. Highly recommend if you want an easy class.

Don't listen to the bad reviews, she's a really kind professor and wants all of her students to pass the class. She is lenient with assignments and understands that we all have busy schedules. This class improved my presentation skills and was also a lot of fun.
She is not a good professor at all. She is completely unorganized, has absolutely no reason for giving the grades that she does, and she does not seem to care about her students
She didn't grade any of our assignments until the very end of the semester. I had thought I was doing well in the class b

analysis.name: Flávio Azevedo
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Flavio is awesome; genuinely cares about students. Class itself consists of readings which can be long and pretty dense. During lecture, there is A LOT of group discussion. Not hard as long as you do the readings and put in some effort!

Dr. Flavio is a great professor! He really knows his stuff and cares for his students! There were even times he brought cake for all of us! The class isn't difficult! Yes, there is long readings but those can bring you get. 2 drops for it! The midterm isn't that bad since there is a review. You will get to know your classmates! Participate/enjoy it

This grad class is by nature difficult, as a review of cognitive research. Flavio is cool, very laid back. His style is not for everyone (looking at you, A-types), but he makes sure you get what you need out of the class. You are treated as a colleague and beginner researcher, with respect and also support. Your head will explode, but worry not!

Dr. Azevedo is brilliant and you will learn a lot from him. He doesn't really care about grades (it is not really that hard to make an A if you do the right things) but you will care about doing well in his class because you will be inspired to really learn it.

analysis.name: Azfar Moin
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Moin is .. interesting. His lectures are good if you care about the material and he definitely cares about the info he teaches. The class is graded by few things and the criteria are VERY vague. The class itself was fine. the worst part was the TAs. One was RUDE and graded us like grad students though the class is only an intro class.

He's okay. He's funny and likes participation. Lots of reading, but most of it's interesting. Only 1 quiz, 1 paper, 1 midterm, and a final. All essay and short answer. But he gives prompts and choice of words in the test review which he chooses from. It takes work for sure, but it's not impossible. Definitely read & take notes & you'll be okay.
- Only his view is valid - When you ask for help his answers are vague - Rude, criticizes students in class in front of everyone (very unprofessional)
He's an okay professor, he kind of acts like an desi uncle. There is a quiz, a paper, midterm and the final and everything is essay/short answer. Randomly does attendance.

There's a lot of reading but you don't really need to do it to pass the class. I'd recommend doing it and then participating in class discussion; it's an easy way to stand out. The course material is interesting, but Moin expected so little of us that it was hard to care.

analysis.name: Adnan Aziz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Aziz is an amazing professor. I highly recommend taking this class with him. The labs are really fun but get harder as the year progresses. He really like students to engage in real applications that can be used to show to future recruiters. We made our own Google app. Labs are easy but tests were tricky. Overall, Aziz is awesome.

The lectures slightly boring but the labs are interesting.  I did minimal studying for the tests and make high B's.  Aziz is very helpful during office hours.  During class he often makes careless mistakes during examples, but usually is quick to catch them.  Overall good professor for this class. I would recommend taking him.
One of the worst professor's at UT. Teaches about software and tools that he himself does not know. Recommend not to take this course.

analysis.name: Hina Azam
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very difficult and time consuming class, but not impossible. Attendance and participation are required. Daily 6 question open ended book quiz's. Very strict grader but revisions on papers are allowed. So is 6% of extra credit. She's very passionate about this course and a sweet person but I did not enjoy taking this class.

The class is very hefty and for a UGS there is an unnecessary heavy workload. The professors and TA's are very nit-picky graders and most of the time their comments and feedback is not helpful. The books/content is interesting but the class if fast paced and your work is graded slowly. I would not recommend this class.

This class is unnecessarily overdesigned and beyond disorganized. There is an unnecessary amount of assignments that serve no purpose but to lower your grade. It would be okay if the feedback was helpful and the assignments were graded fairly, but critiques were ambiguous, and points were deducted for small mistakes, which became very discouraging.

I do not recommend Dr. Azam. She assigns 3 500 page books in your first semester of college. While you are learning to be a successful student she grades harsh and does not give leeway. I also find the content unrepresentative of an accurate intro to Islam and can give students the wrong point of view of what the religion is.
Just don't take. No reason for a UGS to be sinking your GPA as bad as this. No matter what you do it won't be right. Absurd grading. Poorly organized. Save yourself the sanity

analysis.name: Barbara Chisholm
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: really fun professor and helped me ease into college as a freshman. classes develop a sense of community within peers and the professor. overall really fun and great class

Took this class as an elective so I can fill my schedule & I'm SO glad I did. Barbara is very sweet and funny and has been one of my favorite professors at UT by far. Attendance is mandatory (you can only miss 2 classes unexcused) but don't worry bc you won't want to skip. TD 303 definitely helps break out of your shell & interact with classmates.

I took this class to fulfill one of my elective requirements as a senior. The assignments are easy as long as you get memorized, and there is definitely a sense of community within the class, as everyone is new to acting. Attendance is a huge part of the grade, but Barbara is easy to reach outside of class if you really need to skip for any reason!

One of the most fun classes I have ever taken in my academic career. There are 3 assignments where there are lines to memorize throughout the course, the first 2 are collaborative and the last one is a monologue. Nothing difficult to memorize at all. The class is small and meets so frequently that there is def a sense of community at the end. 10/10

This was a really fun class and you get close to everyone in there because it is a small class. Only 3 scenes throughout the semester but it really helps with public speaking. Barbara is super nice and cares about her students and gives really good feedback on your scenes. All you really have to do is show up and participate and you'll get an A.

analysis.name: Efstathios Bakolas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is pretty doable if you stay on track. You might feel a little lost as to why you are doing certain things, though. He's a nice guy - expect to learn the content, but don't anticipate interesting lectures. A little boring and monotone at times. Tests get harder over time, and the final is designed to make you think hard.

very light work load, only 6 hw's, 2 exams, and a final. exams were weighted heavy, but the final was online. beware though the first exam is way easier than the second one, and very time consuming. was very difficult to finish both the 2nd exam and the final because of the lengths of them. overall prof was fine, hardly ever went to lectures tho

Well-documented lecture notes and spends a lot of time explaining concepts in-depth. Course starts off pretty easy, but if you don't keep track of and connect concepts they WILL sneak back up on you. The final exam was pretty brutal. Spends a lot of time talking about career/professional development topics if that's your vibe

Great lecturer. Presents material in a great way. Even though it's not required, you need to go to lectures. That's the only way to succeed from my experience. Lectures are never boring either. Midterms are okay, final exam was a bit harder.

His teaching style is a little weird where its super hard to follow, understand, and really get the main picture. You can go the entire semester even doing well in classes but not understand what or why you are doing what you're doing at all. The content itself is reasonable for an upper-level aero class, and tests get progressively harder.

analysis.name: Samy Ayoub
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's a great prof who genuinely cares about his students. He is absolutely brilliant and I love his lectures. However, you are graded on very few assignments and if you don't test well, I would avoid this class. He always dresses really nice. He's kinda fine ngl.

Great Professor. He is very knowledgeable. If you are pre-law, take his classes. I got into many programs because of his rec letters. He teaches at UT Law. Attendance is mandatory. Two tests: midterm and final. He gives exam reviews for both. Take this class!

Was not familiar with Islam at all coming in but this class is interesting and well structured. Plenty of opportunities for extra credit and easy assignments. Professor Ayoub made it clear that he cared for his students.

He jumped around a lot and was horribly hard to follow. Instructions for assignments are unclear and graded harshly. He doesn't make any sense if you don't know the subject then you won't have any idea what he is talking about. I NEVER DO RMP RATINGS, but this class and professor is not worth it.

He's a very smart guy and cares a lot about the content. I was able to find the book online for like $10, and while the reading was helpful, it wasn't completely mandatory to do well on the test. He gives a study guide a week prior and there are no curve balls on the test. I'm not even a gov major and pulled an A with an average work input.

analysis.name: Ayse Gursoy
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely such a nice person, she's one of the kindest professors at UT! Her class is super easy, and even though there are some group projects, it's really doable. You learn pretty useful things when it comes to the digital world too. She really accommodating to students, and is accessible even when it's not class time.

This class is super easy, one open note quiz every week and a couple of other assignments here and there. Definitely go to class because there are random attendance checks, and missing too many can add up. Overall really easy class but the professor can be really boring.

Amazing teacher. Very approachable and caring. Open note quizzes and several projects using the UT Library resources. Interesting digital topics during the course. Gives extra credit for early submission in assignments. They can become heavy, starting early is a must.

Professor Gursoy was extremely kind and understanding. She will be lenient with you as long as you talk to her in advance. Extremely easy class. A quiz every week, open note. Two projects. As long as you do your work on time, you will pass.

analysis.name: Patrick Badolato
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

Hands down best professor I ever took. He prepares you for life and uses real examples as material. He's not a tough grader. If you are solely a business student this SHOULD be your center of focus. Will say not to get overconfident after first exam, the final is much harder and with no extra credit this time. Wish I had taken more advantage of him

The conceptual basis of the class makes lectures confusing, and the tests are very different than what you do in class - you will need to study every bit of the material and do the practice questions a lot to stay afloat.

Take this class if you actually want to learn accounting. Classes are very engaging and actually get you to learn instead of just memorize all the boring parts of accounting. The more you go to class the better you'll do on the tests. The extra credit is also super easy to get if you want a boost to your first test.

Take him! If you want to learn content & gain value from class, you have to take him. Not too much outside class work. accessible & funny

review_highlights.comment: Professor Ayvaci is a nice guy but his exams are very difficult and he has some very backwards policies. This is a SQL coding class and exams are all multiple choice, so they are not a good measure of what you know. No chance to actually write code in exams. He doesn't let you even see graded quizzes, so it's impossible to know what you got wrong.

Professor Ayvaci was a nice guy to say the least, but he had trouble keeping the lectures interesting. Luckily the material is fairly easy and he provides all the slides you need, so if you just read/memorize the slides before the tests and quizzes, you should do fairly well. He definitely knows what he's talking about, but has trouble clarifying.
He should learn that teaching doesnt consist of preparing and showing slides. As a teacher his value should be more than that. Your learning will be mostly limited with your capacity in his class.

I really didn't vibe with this guy's teaching style at all. Every example is taken directly from the book, and he rarely, if ever, leads the class step-by-step on a block of code, and this is nominally a CODING class. By far the worst MIS professor I've taken thus far at UT. He's just not an effective teacher when the goal is programming knowledge.

He's a nice guy, but not so great of a teacher. I stopped going to class because I couldn't understand his style of teaching and the test was straight from the book anyways. Right before the test I would memorize the powerpoint slides and textbook chapters, and would do ok. Aside from that, the homework assignments and quizzes are really easy!

analysis.name: Ayelet Lushkov

review_highlights.comment: Definitely one of the best professors out there. She is there for her students and provides helpful feedback. If you make an effort to show her that you care about the class, she will reciprocate. She is also extremely easy to talk to, and overall an amazing person. I enjoyed her humor & enthusiasm very much.

For a course with a writing flag, it is, in my opinion, a surprisingly small amount of writing overall. There is fair bit of reading though, but nothing awful. Participation is graded for the class, but if you're quiet she understands that and just wants to hear your thoughts every once in a while during discussions.

She's a really interesting teacher with great lectures. She made reading classic texts a lot more fun and she introduced many themes and elements of the stories that I never realized were present. Lots of reading, but you do get to read Game of Thrones a lot in Classics and Modern Fantasy. Essays were rough but debates and discussions were fun.

analysis.name: James Ayres

review_highlights.comment: Wow. This jerk taught my first UT course in 1989 & I'm dismayed to see he's still up to the same sadistic garbage. He knows Shakespeare but wd rather bully than teach. On the 1st paper, he failed every student in the class (all had placed out of fresh comp) except 1, whom he gave a prize for a C.  I dropped (along w 1/2 the class) & took Prof Velz.

He failed my entire class on the majority of our papers.  But EVERYONE failed on the first essay.  He gives at least 35 pages of reading per night, and then a quiz over the readings the next morning.   I dropped his class along w/ 19 other students and we are working on a petition to have him removed from our college.  DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!

I was one of the lucky ones in his class and scored an A but most of my class failed. He was so confusing if he was going to take the original paper/test or the retake one for the final grades. You were one pins and needles waiting for your report card. He really shouldn't be teaching Intro to Shakespeare, expects far too much.

took his class one semester and found shakespeare completely innacessible, failed it. took it with another prof the next semester and she presented it and breathed a life into it  in such a way that I understood it and enjoy it to this day. made a B.

I took this professor in the mid 1990s, and from these reviews, it sounds like he hasn't changed much.  Terrible instruction.  Abusive to students.  Loves to give Fs.  He certainly knows Shakespeare, it's just a shame he can't teach it.

analysis.name: Benjamin Brower
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
