review_highlights.comment: Professor Brower has very enjoyable lectures that are easy to follow. He is incredibly knowledgeable on the subject and seemed to have the answers to any questions asked, no matter how minute. He was also able to direct me to outside resources to supplement the lectures and readings. Great class.

Professor Brower is one of my favorite professors. He is incredibly knowledgeable, and its clear that he loves what he is teaching. It's somewhat lecture heavy but I really learned a lot through this class. I wish I could take him again, and I highly recommend that you take his class if you can.
He clearly loves what he teaches. His lectures are funny at times but always engaging. If you do the readings and pay attention to the lectures you should do fine on his written tests.

Actually HIS310P idk why it's not an option. Can't say enough how nice & genuine of a guy he is, super approachable with good vibes all around. Lectures are mostly him talking from a few slides, so go to class and take heavy notes. Make a group to compare stuff with and review consistently. If you're a good writer and study well, you can get an A.

I loved Professor Brower, he's genuine and sweet and very respectful of student opinions. Class is very lecture heavy with some discussion involved. He's very passionate about the topic. Main grade comes from 3 exams which are just an essay question, and he never gives out 100s but I also don't know anybody that scored lower than an 85 so.

review_highlights.comment: Participation is 50% of grade which is easy. However she gives two tests that require lots of reading and are randomly hard. Also she assigns a long video project. The class is less of an exercise class and more about teaching students how to teach conditioning especially focusing on teaching it to kids. Not what I expected. Gives extra credit

Incredibly hard to listen to her lectures, too boring. Have to take notes in class cause its on the exams and she moves too fast to write things down. Doesn't post lecture slides either. Tough grader. Seems like no matter the situation you may be in there is little to no sympathy. She is not going to set you up for success so you must be on it.

Dr. Beckwith's class is fairly straightforward: attendance is 50%, and the rest of your grade is from exams and a group project. The workout component wasn't too bad most of the time, but every so often, it would be intense. Exams require lots of close reading, so make sure you keep up with the textbook and articles posted on Canvas.
Easiest class I'm taking. Two free absences and she offers extra credit. Beckwith's super helpful too.

Classes are relatively easy, workout component isn't bad. You get 2 absences, which you should leave for the end of semester because those workouts are TOUGH. 3+ absences tanks grade 5% each time, so DONT SKIP. Tests are ridiculously tough for a pe class, do NOT take for a PE credit, but if you NEED it for coaching specialization, you'll be fine.

analysis.name: William Beckner

review_highlights.comment: Absolute chiller and the goat. However his lectures make no sense and his handwriting is not very legible. This class was a journey from which I emerged a better person.

It's almost all about lectures. He replies emails very slowly, but eventually you will get it. Some people don't like his style: old man talks in old-fashion. Personally, I think his teaching reveals perspicacious understanding. If u R self-motivated, he can also introduce topics that you strongly recommend (if the topic is relevent to the course)

Beckner is incredibly smart and he provides an unconventional/sophisticated perspective on his topics. Due to this, a lot of the material goes over the young students' heads and he doesn't realize it. You will struggle in this class. But he grades easily: show that you care about learning and you will be rewarded, both GPA-wise and intellectually.

If you're one of those people on their phone/computer in class, then you will be confused by his lectures. If you pay attention, you still probably will be confused. HOWEVER, the parts you do understand are more enlightening than any other teacher you have, and give you the insight of a real mathematician. Also he grades super easy so dont worry.

He's a lot better at teaching than people say. Very accommodating, significant extra credit on the tests, interesting content problems. Good class to take if you don't want to learn differential equations in the boring engineer way. Unfortunately, no idea if he'll be teaching this next spring, because he stopped teaching M 427L-H.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Stepp

review_highlights.comment: Professor Stepp has amazing lectures and she even has a Zoom set up before every class starts for those who might need it for whatever reasons. The notes themselves are amazing. When it comes to what the grade is broken into, the tests do play a more significant part in the course, but if you do all the learning modules and hw, you should do fine.

Prof. Stepp is a great professor, though she sometimes speeds up significantly, which can make her difficult to follow. She's also a generous grader and very funny. A substantial portion of your grade comes from homework, so be sure to complete it correctly and submit it as instructed. She also provides a review for every exam.

I definitely think Stepp is one of the best math teachers I have ever had. Even on zoom she was engaging and SO FUNNY. She makes sure to break down concepts. Her exam could be tricky but at the end she adjusted the grading scale and bumped up a ton of people because SHE CARES. 1-2 Quest Homeworks a week, 2 midterms, and a final. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

Having no calc experience in High School and having to take 408C and 408D for the first time here at UT, 408D was tough. She goes really fast, and the tests are worth a lot of your grade. I had to drop it due to academic and personal reasons, but she was an amazing professor. She is super kind, funny, and knows her stuff. :)

Dr Stepp is a good professor - you can tell that she really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Participation and attendance aren't mandatory but may be rewarded with extra credit. Her lectures are fast and the content is difficult. I often had to supplement lectures with textbook readings to get a full understanding.

Slow, boring, intro level course. The final was too long and like only one person in the room finished it in the time allotted. She's really kind and seems very approachable, but honestly if you can help it, don't take this class at all.

Doesn't care about you at all

review_highlights.comment: This is a hard class in general, but I would say he is the best professor to take it with. High stakes exams (Midterm 40% and Final 50%). No recorded lectures, but lecture notes are posted. Homeworks (10 total, 2 drop) are good practice for the exams. Midterm and Final are curved for fairness for those unable to attend midterm (Final 90%). I would recommend staying on top of the course material as falling behind can easily overwhelm you.

Bhaskar is a smart man which is why it's so easy to get confused when he explains. Watch videos for clarity and DO additional practice problems. There is one midterm worth 40% (avg ~60) and one final worth 50% (avg ~68). I got below average for both exams and got a B so he curves good. DO NOT WAIT LAST MINUTE FOR STUDYING. Keep practicing activley.

The class is very interesting and the problems are fun.... when you are given effective material to work with. Homeworks do not prepare us for exam questions and often take multiple hours to do. I got myself sick once because of how much time it took to do one homework. The material is very interesting, just study as much as you can!

review_highlights.comment: I never took the course. He seems like a chill guy, though. A fantastic professor, who genuinely cares about the well-being of his students. In his lectures he gives you important background knowledge and information about the assignments. Perhaps my favorite professor at UT, knowledgable, approachable, caring and well-prepared. The project can be a lot of work but is also fun, you learn so much. I would definitely take another class with him.

He is a great prof! Super nice, cares about students, explains concepts well. However, there is breakdown in grading with the student grader being SUPER harsh and Dr. Bhat did not accept any feedback on that. Material can get confusing, homeworks are easy but the exams are incredibly hard

He really cares about his students. There's are one midterm (30%) and final (40%). If you understand how to do the homework and you go to class you'll be fine.

Awesome prof, super fun and great music taste. 610D is the heaviest homework load in the Spanish sequence, but Prof Luke makes it worth it with great, engaging lectures. He's clearly passionate about Spanish and I definitely recommend taking a class with him!

Awesome professor and taught the content really well. Just a super nice guy as well. He gives great feedback and is very approachable. There's homework every day, but if you do it there's no way you won't do well. I really enjoyed being in the class.

This class, as with the Spanish classes at UT, comes with a lot of outside work due to it being a 6 hour credit! Although the textbook did awful job at explaining the grammar, Luke was great at helping you understand. If you didn't get it he would rephrase his explanations until one stuck. Very helpful office hours.

While this class is interesting and Professor Bisett clearly knows a lot about marketing, the grading scale of this class is one of the worst at UT. OK professor. Easy quizzes and exam. Complete all possible extra credit because he will try to give you the lowest final grade possible. I ended this class with a 91 and received a B freaking plus as a letter grade.. because of his unfair grading policy. The final presentation policy is a nightmare.

While the lectures can be interesting at times, the grading sucks. He wants his students to compete in order to get a good grade in the class. The final project is worth 30% of the grade, and if you are not a finalist, you can only get an 80%!! He also cleary has favorite students!!

analysis.name: Douglas Biow

Don't take him, just unnecessary stress.

There are no exams but there are essays, but you can choose the topic of each essay and which film it's about.

Dr. Biow is a great guy, and I enjoyed his lectures for Films and Filmmakers of Italy. All you have to do is watch the movie and be able to write about it. He will give you great feedback and extensions if needed. Mandatory discussion sections with TAs sucked, though, and were not very helpful since nobody would speak or show up. Good UGS choice!

All you have to do is watch the movies, attend the lectures, and write thought pieces/ essays on them. Dr. Biow is passionate about film and the history of Italy, which made his lectures so enjoyable. Discussion sections were unenjoyable because people didn't talk much, though.

analysis.name: David Birdsong

Joy of French truly was joyful. Took for Power of Words UGS. Such a fun class and insanely easy. Professor does tend to go on random tangents/talk about nothing. Very little work and it is hard not to get an A.

Birdsong is a very enthusiastic & fun teacher- gets you excited about what he's teaching. He was not originally supposed to teach 317C, so he did not create the material and tests. Great class to really learn about pronunciation. He's engaging and fun. Writing recommendation letters for multiple people in class. Cares about your individual progress. A knowledgeable and fun professor, if you need to fulfill your degree plan or need a history professor, definitely take him

absolutely incredible professor!! wish i could take more classes from him!! he's new to ut this semester but great class regardless. took the time to get to know every student individually. essays are graded tough but very clear that he's looking for a very straightforward and structured analysis. avg class is only 30 mins and ec opportunities!
BLANTON IS AMAZING! He gives out plenty of extra credit, and has engaging lectures, as well as he cares immensely for his students.

If you treat the course like an in-person class, meaning you actually watch the lectures, it'll be fine. The two exams are decently challenging and worth 20% each, but not outrageous. Professor Blank is engaging in lecture videos and has a good sense of humor.

Worst class I've ever taken in my life, the sheer amount of work that this class has is abysmal. There is an insane amount of weekly lectures that range from 15-60+ minutes each PLUS all of the work from the online webtext. The professors provide ZERO methods of studying and often contradict themselves for what information will show up on the test

Decent Teacher, HARD CLASS. Exam format is extremely lop sided (1 exam covers 2 months of material) and questions deviate DRASTICALLY from weekly instructions. Also, video instructions are long and 95% unnecessary, but you need to pay attention since the 5% WILL be tested. Overall, not hard class to pass, but HARD to get an A in.

The weekly reading has about 200 comprehension questions + 7-10 lectures a week. It's annoying, and professors aren't helpful, telling you to study everything. Exams are Honorlock and have frequent typos and formatting issues. Might need a thesaurus to understand test questions. only 2 exams worth 40% of grade

This class is not as bad as people are making it out to be but you do need to actually watch the lectures! Lectures will be more helpful over the readings and the readings can be done in abt 15 minutes. Not a class you can breeze through but definitely do able to get an A

analysis.name: Blair Johnson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Johnson is great at explaining difficult concepts and often presents simpler, clearer methods. Homework is time-consuming and challenging, so be prepared. Exams are structured differently but not bad. Many extra credit opportunities. IMO one of the better fluids professors at UT, would definitely take again. Shoutout TA Alex for being awesome

Anyone who dislikes Prof J just hates when professors expect their students to learn. She is a good teacher, and the class is manageable. It is easy to succeed in her class if you participate in lectures, go to office hours, do the homework etc. Only gripe is all homework assignments were group work which I hated, but overall, I really liked her.

The only way you can do good is by attending office hours where you can receive further info the rest of the class is unaware of. She was not prepared a lot of the time and taught straight from her notes, often making mistakes and not correcting them until the next lecture. Not recommended if not passionate about fluids, as she expects you to be.

Honestly she's my fav prof I've ever taken. I'm not really an outgoing person but she makes sure to get to know her students well and make them feel comfortable. It sounds silly but I was really touched that she remembered my name(which she pronounced properly) and face after I introduced myself once. You can tell she really cares which is nice.

She preaches about mental health but denied our group an extension when we were overloaded. She uploads assignments as announcements (rather than in files), and many of the time are uploaded as word docs instead of pdf. She assigns groups where you have to give a presentation over a scientist and work on weekly homework with that same group.

analysis.name: Cheasequah Blevins
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She essentially reads off the slides, but the course itself is not difficult. You can teach yourself what she skips over. She is friendly and it is better to ask questions in office hours. Grading is nitpicky for minor lab and homework mistakes, points off add up over time. She also gives extra credit for coming to class, that helps.

Nice lady, but this course is heavy for an introductory statistics class. A lot of people thought this class was a breeze because they took AP Stats in high school but if you didn't take it, it's not a walk in the park. Blevins definitely has good material and resources but the quizzes are a lot harder than what she teaches

Super sweet professor, loves giving feedback and regrades, but emails vanish into the void and lectures were insanely long. You can easily self-teach, she posts annotated slides and lets you use cheat sheets. Extra credit is HUGE but only offered if you show up.

Love this professor! She is very clear about what she expects. Your grade is made up of a lot of different things, so exams aren't super stressful. The homework is very tedious though sometimes. Overall, I definitely recommend this course!

Dr. Blevins is a great professor, and she cares about her students. Her lectures are clear and straightforward without being dry. You don't get a lot of time for quizzes, but they aren't too difficult. TAs grade strictly on homework and it's not always apparent what they want you to include. Overall, not a difficult course. Some extra credit given.

analysis.name: Lauren Blondeau
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Blondeau breaks statistics down really well. She has plenty of resources for your success in this course. Her class is graded by quizzes (where you can have a 1 page cheat sheet), homework, labs, and a major project that isn't too difficult! She is pretty flexible and understanding and responds to emails pretty quickly too!

The most understanding professor ever. I slept in for the final quiz and told her the truth, and she let me take it during office hours on Zoom. The quizzes are very easy (7-8 questions per quiz, 4 in total). The final project is split into parts where you're given a template to fill out, so you're not lost. She is an angel and a GPA savior

This class is very easy if you've taken AP Statistics in high school. Overall, the material is boring, but Professor Blondeau does a good job organizing the course. The workload is very light, though you should be cautious with quizzes. Even though you're allowed a page of notes, they are graded strictly. Overall, it's a decent class.

There is only 4 quizzes and 1 major project. The reviews she gives are very different from the actual quiz questions. She does allow a page of notes for each quiz, but it's not very helpful. Attendance is not mandatory, but you are graded on Instapolls during class. Try not to fall behind at all and do show up to every lab meeting.

Blondeau is a decent professor, and the project was easy to get a full score on. However, I could not manage to do well on a single quiz this year because of how difficult they were and it sunk my grade because they were weighted heavily. Also the TA was very strict on grading. Lectures were helpful in studying.

analysis.name: Mary E. Blockley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I had her for History of the English Language. She is socially inept, hard to deal with, and not interested in undergraduates.

Blockey's class is insanely difficult and poorly taught. As the other posts say, she's nice, but very unhelpful. Half the class failed the midterm. She continues on like its our problem. I'm an Eng major. I freak if I get a B on a test. This midterm, I got a D. I spoke to her. She acts like it's my failing. My 3 A's on my other 3 midterms disagree.

I've never had such a horrid "educator." It's mind-boggling how she advanced in her career, incapable of organizing a coherent classroom discussion. Students talked in circles, and she adamantly shut down any critiques of the main protagonist. I honestly would rather drop out than attend a class with her as the professor again. Still passed.

Professor Blockley is just very odd. Her course has absolutely no structure, and she does not match her syllabus. She changes deadlines and cancels exams on a whim. There aren't clear rubrics or prompts given for papers. It just feels like you're blindly showing up to class, and you don't know what you're getting when you arrive.

Prof Blockley may be a sweet woman, but her class is HORRIBLY organized, most days we had no lesson plan and I'm not even sure why we needed to show up. She is a bit...quirky... and seemed to like reading gross, sexist books so she could make a spectacle out of how bad they were. If you need an Eng. credit, there are way better options.

analysis.name: Blanca Ramierz
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't take this class with her period. TA's were rude & inconsiderate, while the professor read off of a script without expanding on the topics/terms. I didn't learn anything from the lectures since she didn't give time to note anything and didn't post the slides. Attendance via instapolls was the worst

If i can deter you from doing anything during your time at UT it is having this woman as your professor. She takes an intro class way too seriously and has a terrible structure. I have never rated a professor before but something had to be said. She cares more about stopping you from cheating than helping you learn.

The structure of this course is terrible. The professor does not post the slides and gets upset if you try to take pictures of them if you can't write fast enough. Most of the learning will be done through the reading since the lectures are all over the place. The one thing I like about this course is the fact that the textbook is free.

Horrible teacher. She read from a script and did not know her slides at all, Guest lecturers were better than her. Didn't post slides and no extra credit. Cutoff for an A was a 94. She doesn't want you to do well. Exams aren't hard. Papers are graded by TAs, so they decide your grade. I didn't learn anything it was about the level of a hs class.

Professor Ramirez was a great teacher. Her class was very engaging, with interesting topics, and was definitely one of my favorite classes. Although there were few assignments, as long as you studied, you would do great. My TA was also great and very helpful during office hours. Highly recommend this class!

analysis.name: Kirk Blazek
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 220 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Wow. What an eye opening experience to the savagery and absolute bonkers max-tier class the Dr. Blazek has created. The homeworks are redundant, tedious, and mind-numbingly difficult. And the tests are really, really hard. Lectures are scrambled up so that even Einstein couldn't figure out what is going on! Pls don't take :(. Save your soul.

Worst professor I have had. Be prepared for lots of homework. He does not show basic respect to any students. When asking questions in class, he gives off an impertinent attitude, answering in a sarcastic and condescending tone. Expect to learn everything by yourself; his notes are illegible, and he barely records his lectures.
very awful professor. doesn't clearly explain concepts and the homework is incredibly redundant and tedious, do not take

Tests do not line up with what he teaches, and he goes SO fast in lectures that it is impossible to follow. Notes are not even helpful because there is no structure to the class. Curses every two seconds. Not sure how he is still a professor at UT with how unprofessional he is.

Blazek has revamped the ECE M340L section to make it incredibly difficult, tedious and not easy to understand. Beware of taking the class as it is not as easy as other sections. Very unfortunate to experience... I cannot emphasize enough how bad my experience has been.

analysis.name: Bjorn Hegelich
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: what he teaches is not on the test
All he does is stand at the front a derive equations. He does not help at all in the way of actually learning the concepts of physics which is what this course is supposed to be about.
Does not use class time effectively. Does not explain the material well. Doesn't even teach whats on the exams.
Definitely the least caring professor at UT. The averages on the tests are a 55. Good luck my friends.
Does not teach, test are extremely hard

analysis.name: Anna Bjurman-Pautz
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't let her casual demeanor lure you into thinking the midterm and final will be simple. Expect to put some effort into understanding the concepts bc they aren't always explained well in class. Students asked questions as if the views she was suggesting were her own. They'd debate her, she wouldn't be able to get on track, and we'd get nowhere.

She follows the slides and explains things pretty well until someone asks a question. Then I stop taking notes until she goes back to talking about the slides because any response to a question seems to make her uncomfortable. She pauses a lot while thinking how to respond. She really is a nice woman and very intelligent, though. I'd say, take her.

Human Nature: The teacher is amazingly lenient and super nice. The problem is that she reads DIRECTLY from her slide shows and the class was at 8 in the morning MWF. Her TA was VERY nice and lenient also. There is a midterm (essay answers) and a final (essay) and there are two Response papers and about 10 in class assignments. Hard to pay attention

She is not an  awful professor by any means but does lack the ability to make the lectures engaging and it's common to even find her looking at the clock. Her pauses  between statements give the appearance that she doesn't even know what she's talking about; but that isn't the case because she does in her own capacity. Paying attention is hard.

It's like Einstein said: "if you can't explain it to a 6 year old, you don't fully understand it". She answers questions in a convoluted, round about way and often mixes up her terminology. The book is no help either; nothing is explained in an introductory way, not in lecture or from the book. HW problems are out of the book so its essential

analysis.name: Oyvind Bjoru
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Best professor ever. I took his Planet Word course, and it was so good that it almost made me switch my major to Linguistics. Very little work and amazing lectures. There's one midterm essay (which you condense and revise for the final) and a short 4-minute presentation, both easy and fun. Lukas Rudzinski, the TA, was also great and very caring.

I had Professor Oyvind for Planet Word and he was extremely passionate about what he teaches. The class itself is an easy A, there's weekly hw quizzes that take about 3 min max, only one essay, and a short presentation for grades. Attendance is mandatory but the class is a super easy A if you spend even a little time on the assignments.

If you need a language credit TAKE NORWEGIAN!! Prof Øyvind is genuinely one of my favorite professors I have ever had. He is incredibly patient, kind, and empathetic and wants you to succeed. He will work with you if you need help and is understanding and flexible with illness/absences. This class is a gpa BOOSTER and the timing MWF 11-1 is ideal.

Prof Øyvind is the best! If you need a lang credit, take Norwegian! He is so thoughtful & patient and just wants you to have a positive experience. Attendance is mandatory, but he is forgiving about sickness. Exams are online/at-home & there are only a few in class quizzes. It's one of the easiest languages for English speakers.

Oyvind is probably the best professor I've had at UT. He's incredibly understanding and cares about his students, but he's also an amazing lecturer. I didn't care about the noir genre, but understanding all the intricacies now has given me a newfound appreciation. I'm taking Norwegian because I just wanna have him as a professor again.

analysis.name: Clayton Bjorland
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I liked this prof. He was very helpful to students, and worked lots of examples in class. Also, I took this class over the summer, so we were moving pretty fast, but I nevers struggled with his pacing. As mentioned by someone else, he does mess up a lot in examples. This can be annoying, because he writes very fast and taking notes is hard enough.

It might have been the class material was easy (math 408M is suppose to be inbetween 408D and 427L) But when I took his class back in spring I remember it being very easy. His lectures were nice in that he'd work examples in class, he sympathized with students and graded very leniently. I'd recommend this professor and I hope I can take him again

He's a good math professor, willing to work with students, accepts questions immediately and tries very hard to reconcile misunderstandings. Has good lectures, organizes very well. Grades haven't come out yet but for the midterms there appears to be quite generous partial credits awarded, not really any curve though.
Constantly messes up while giving examples. His lectures are boring and the only reason you will get a decent grade is  because everybody else does poorly.
I don't attend class at all. but there's really no need to. Just rework all the homework questions before every exam and you'll get an A!

analysis.name: Larissa Bougleux
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: the bad 601 reviews aren't relevant anymore. lectures are engaging and she wants to hear your perspectives and help you improve. daily hw can take forever and she doesn't announce assignment deadlines so you have to be proactive. the class can be intimidating but she is super nonjudgmental no matter your proficiency.

Very empathetic, caring and understanding. If you ever have an issue, talk to her and she will try to fix it. However, this was her first time teaching the course, and it was obvious. Did not know how to share google docs and was not familiar with test questions or the syllabus. Easy grader but sometimes you get a 50 with no feedback.

Hey... do you really want to take spanish here? Be certain about this now, that ACC isnt a better option for you. 
The faults w Bougeleux can largely be attributed to the fact that spanish at UT sucksssss, and the dpt. is trying to kill you. She did her best, but man, this is a trying class. Strict and fast, but thorough and understanding.

Prof Bougleux was an incredible professor! She's very approachable and will take the time to explain any topic/question you have difficulty with, inside or outside of class. The class itself is challenging simply because you are learning a new language, but if you do the homework assignments, practice exams, and take notes - you will be fine!

The professor is indifferent and unorganized most times. Responds rudely when students ask questions in class and is unwilling to accommodate when issues arrive for students whether during tests or being absent due to sickness. I highly advise avoiding this class if Bougleux is instructing it. She simply throws content at you and fails to help more

analysis.name: Henrique Bolfarine
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is always accessible outside of class (even offering to meet up with students through Zoom) if they cannot attend his OHs, gives credit to students he sees actively engaging in class, and prioritizes every minute of each class (also sometimes gives hints before a quiz). He is also very kind and funny, and extremely knowledgeable in STA 235!

Not the best at explaining and lectures were hard to follow, but made up for it by allowing group work on quizzes and offering extra credit. Homework is challenging but you get multiple attempts, and exams are not worth nearly as much as in other McCombs classes. Using the slides to study was helpful, and he gives plenty of practice material.

Professor Bolfarine is very passionate but it leads to class going over the allocated time usually. There is a quiz at the beginning of each class which is hard. His slides and R-scripts are very helpful and class is well organized. Tests can be difficult too but there is a curve. Overall, it's a difficult class but R is better than using excel.

in Spring '25 paper exams were absurdly hard also no curve after avg 58. Exams had such a wild range of topics and the class did jack shit to prepare you for it. On top of that Bolfarine's lectures were ass and he would make the r script while lecturing resulting in about 25% of the class being actual content and the other 75% incoherent ramblings

He's so kind and adorable!  He gave group quizzes and got rid of Perusalls.  When I emailed him about any slight issue, he gave me a take-home quiz or another way to open Lockdown.  He can be kind of confusing to pay attention to because he says so many things, but he repeats the things that are important to know.  Best 235 Prof by far.

analysis.name: Kimberly Boddy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The final exam for this class had an average of a 33. She ends up boosting the scores by a lot, but you it fails to properly test her students. She also just regurgitates the textbook and doesn't expand upon any of its material. There are few resourses to excel in her 336K course and its the same for 315. Just wait for another professor to teach it

Imagine you're at the beach with your friends. You run into the ocean and get hit with a big wave. You get back up, go deeper into the ocean, and get hit with an even bigger wave. Then when you get back up, a tsunami drowns you and the whole class. Then, you get back up and out of nowhere your 60 became an A-. 10/10 professor, would drown again.

Never again. Got our midterm 2 grades back today and the average was a 40. She says thats good… like girl. The exam questions are unreasonably difficult and she grades without mercy. I couldnt even get 2 points back even tho i had the right answer written. I literally have a better grade in QUANTUM. Mechanics should never be this hard.

Multiple students took mid-exam breaks to faceplant on the table and/or pray for their grades. This class was a waking nightmare and I loved every second of it. Dr. Boddy is also very kind and willing to help students in office hours.

Professor Boddy's lectures are very bad. You will have to teach yourself virtually all of the material. My biggest gripe about Boddy's teaching methods is that she does not really connect the material to the math concepts used for it. This makes it very hard to learn. Grading criteria were also not clear at all. Avoid this professor if you can.

analysis.name: Brenda Boonabaana
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Course is heavily disorganized. The work isn't difficult, but she'll post on random timing during the weekend and you have to scramble to summarize a reading/video with your group. Rambles too much. Group presentations are expected to cover the entire class time, prepare to lecture the entire class. Grades are nonexistent until the end of the year.

She is a very passionate and kind professor. There were very few assignments, but almost all of them are group work or presentations. Also, she posted readings to the group work on short notice, so be prepared to work with your groupmates the night before a presentation. No exams or a final, but there's two quizzes. Attend class and you'll do fine.

She's a really nice professor and it's really clear that she's extremely passionate about sustainable tourism. The grading is kinda iffy because there isn't really a clear rubric (especially with the TA), but it's extremely easy to get a good grade, especially if you just show up to class. She's really caring and understanding, so DEF take this.

Felt a little unorganized at times but overall not difficult. Not graded by many assignments and the A cutoff is a 95, which was pretty doable. Lots of group work, you get assigned to a group at the beginning of the semester and work with them a lot. Only two exams, one with mostly MCQ and a few FRQ and one thats all FRQ.

Seriously, do NOT underestimate how easy the sustainable tourism class is. Whatever you're thinking of I GUARANTEE YOU it's far easier - even the facilitation is graded extremely generously. That seems nice at first, and I suppose it's better than having a harder class with the same schedule, but you will learn almost NOTHING in the whole semester.

analysis.name: Kayla Booth
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Booth is an excellent professor. This research-focused class taught me how to conduct literature reviews, evaluate whether ideas are viable, and approach research thoughtfully. She is always available after class or during office hours and actively helps students find research opportunities. She genuinely cares about student learning.

Dr. Booth is very thoughtful and organized. She explains concepts clearly and brings real industry insight into the class. The course feels intentionally designed and she creates an inclusive environment where students feel comfortable asking questions and going to office hours. She also regularly asks for and implements student feedback.

Prof Booth's passion for research & teaching is clear in the way she leads lectures & structures the class. She genuinely cares about her students, adjusting the course & assignments based on student feedback and interests. Lectures are very interesting & applicable outside of just research. There's a good mix of simple and intensive assignments

Class is only helpful for freshman who never took an AVID class in H.S. 97% of lectures are regurgitated common sense (S.T.A.R method when interviewing, basic resume tips). Only helpful thing was creating your own personal brand.LATE grader. Participation is mandatory, same w attendance. Homework is doable but long. Take a beta-blocker before class

Professor Booth is great! Compared to other professors in the iSchool, she is one of the stronger public speakers and consistently comes to class well prepared, she puts thought into each class. Group work is a big part of the course, so having a reliable group really affects the experience. Overall, she's a solid instructor.

analysis.name: Matthew Bowers
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. B was one of my favorite professors. He always made class fun and interesting every day. This UGS was one of the best on campus (you pretty much just talk about what makes a good sports team). There's tons of extra credit, and he really wants everyone to succeed. If you show up to class and pay attention, you'll get a decent amount out of it.

You genuinely have to try not to get an A+ in this class. Attendance isn't mandatory and the exams are ALL online and OPEN BOOK. Never studied beforehand and get all 95+ on exams. TA's are lenient graders and sometimes I would be too lazy to do the full assignment and still get a 100. This is the easiest class I have ever taken in my life.

Such an easy class. I never read the books, or showed up to class and still got an A. As long as you do the canvas assignments online you'll be fine. The book quizzes were one question, no lockdown browser on anything. The only class you wanna pu to is the discussion. Every assignment is so easy. No tests. Highly recommend.

Dr. Bowers was great! I would definitely recommend taking this class with him if you need it. There is no final exam, but there are four 50 question exams throughout the semester that are open-note and can be taken outside of class. If you do the readings, pay attention in class, and take good notes you should do fine on the exams. Love him!
Such a great professor, lectures are super engaging and non mandatory, Bowers is a very funny and chill person, I'd highly recommend this class

analysis.name: Daniel Bonevac
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 139 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Not too sure why everyone is raving this UGS. So if you have to pick a UGS literally pick any other one, especially if you don't care about philosophy. this UGS was scheduled 4/5 days a week and you have something to read before each class. The assignments are easy yes, but the TA's grade so harsh for things with no rubric. He's nice but it's a no.

Do not take Prof. Bonevac if you want to pass UGS. He gave a final with 65 quotes that is worth 15% of your grade. He is also pressed that students do not show up to class in an attendance optional class and grades students unfairly. UGS should be a course that is passable for students who put in the work and accessible for non-philosophy majors.

I had a 96 in the class. After the final, my grade dropped to an 87. Don't underestimate the final. The quote part was easy. The MC after the quotes was the hard part. out of the 45 MC I knew maybe 10 of them. It was straight up guessing after that. Quizzes every week. 3 papers. Not to mention a lot of the stuff you learn is boring.

He is a very good lecturer. There are a lot of assignments based on readings, but as long as you do them, you should be fine. In class quizzes can be more difficult, but they are a smaller part of your grade. Majority of the grade comes from essays based on books. Overall, if you put effort into this class, it's not bad at all.

Outstanding lectures, he is genuinely skilled in that regard. Attendance is not mandatory but you will want to attend, every class is like watching a well-produced documentary. Has a lot of passion for what he teaches and you learn a lot being in the room. 2 book essays and no exams, would definitely  recommend this as a UGS.

analysis.name: Katherine Bruner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors, if not the best, that I've encountered at UT. Its rare to find a professor who goes out of their way to help students so much on an individual basis. You can tell she really cares about her students.

Lowk flopped on that first exam which brought my grade down a lil but i dont even care because i literally love Dr. Bruner so much. Please take her. Grades are made up mostly of participation, lab quizzes, hw, and 2 exams. Make sure you watch the lecture and you'll literally be fine. Genetics is cheeks but this lab made me like it slightly better.
Dr. Bruner is awesome. The lab TAs here are super informed on what they're doing as well, and you genuinely feel like you learn something. Perfect level of difficulty for an UD Bio lab.

Best professor I've had at UT. She is so nice and caring! Lectures are optional, but if you go to them the weekly quizzes are really easy. There a no lab reports, but you'll spend the semester doing writing assignments as you work towards a 6-8 pg research paper. Easy A with a little effort. Labs usually did not last the entire 4 hours.

one of my favorite labs! dr. bruner is very kind and cares about students' understanding. lecture attendance is not mandatory but either go or watch the recordings to prepare for the in-lab quizzes (they can be a bit hard). exams are reasonable, homework takes effort but doable. i enjoyed the lab activities and found the experiments fun! highly rec

analysis.name: Ryan Briggs
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you're looking for a VAPA that's fun but also easy, take this class if you can! The lectures are interesting and you will only have to write two essays and take a couple quizzes that aren't very hard. While attendance is mandatory, he won't take it every day. He does not allow devices during lecture but don't let that be a dealbreaker!

loved briggs! do not be a goof in class or he will stop lecture and call you out. no technology in class and if he catches you... good luck. however, i really enjoyed how he was not a push over and was passive aggressive in a good way. he would call out people who were talking during lecture, something i loved! watch films + take notes = success!

one of the sweetest professors, please take her!! participation is required but we had rly interesting discussions in class and Prof. Cifuentes-Ramirez was very encouraging and patient so don't be afraid to make mistakes in spanish :) other grades are the HWs, exams, speaking assignments, and group presentations but it is very doable to get an A

She is a really caring professor and she made Spanish easy to learn. The class was hard with a lot of homework but that's the Spanish department's fault, not hers. Exams online. If you have to take Spanish at UT I would highly recommend her! She is super nice and wants to help you learn. She is funny and builds positive relationships with students.

analysis.name: Gustavo Cepparo
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 191 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Cepparo is hilarious! I took his class at 8am MWF  and he made it energetic and informative. His notes are organized and briefs you before exams. Expect a rather heavy load of weekly Quest and textbook homework. TA sessions aren't mandatory but you need to go to turn in your homework to be graded. Must work for an A. Most enjoyable class so far.

CEPPARO IS AWESOME!!! If you do and understand his homework, study his online material, go to class, and go to his office hours for questions, you WILL do well.  He is a very generous grader and cares about his students alot.  This is also a fantastic class to take if you must take an 8AM! Very funny! Very entertaining! He made Calculus amazing!

Definitely not an easy class, but Cepparo is a fantastic teacher. His explanations in class were clear, although he did run through material very quickly so it was difficult to keep up at times. There's one book assignment and one quest per week, so workload is a bit heavy. I had only taken Calc AB prior, but I did all the work and made an A.

Cepparo was amazing. I loved every second of his class. He gave a lot of homework, but it really helped me tremendously. I had taken calculus before, so it was pretty easy for me and I made an A on every test. He is very willing to help and loves his students. Take this guy, you won't regret it.

If you screw up just one of his exams, you grade will be affected. So beware! I had 3 tests overall and though I improved from 66% to 96% to 104% (you see how good that improvement is), I could not make an A. :'( Work from the beginning. BTW he stammers on one phrase (always): OK WITH THAT? lol. And he loves coffee.

analysis.name: Cindy Meston
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 96 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely loved her and respect her so much. The lectures are very interesting and occasionally gives you bonus points. No homework , each exam weighs 20% but the lowest out of the 5 gets dropped. Very easy class as long as you watch the lecture and read the assigned chapters. I loved this class and literally aspire to be Dr.Meston.

I really enjoyed Dr. Meston's lectures as it was clear she was passionate about the subject and easy to listen to. The lectures were even better in 2x speed and easy to digest. The information isn't for everyone but it was interesting and lots of extra credit plus a pretty straight forward test, no final, and drops lowest test score.

Funniest class I have taken to this day. With that said it is actually kind of difficult so make sure you attend the lectures. If you attend lectures you will not only get EC opportunities but you will also get at least a B. I made the mistake of not going to class for half the semester and it killed me on half the tests.

Super easy free A, but only graded on 5 tests. She provides bonus points opportunity in almost every lecture to bump your grade up 10 points. Attendance not mandatory. Really nice professor who's knowledgable about the class and lectures themselves had interesting topics.

This was one of my favorite classes I've taken at UT! The lectures are super interesting and the required reading is relevant and easy to digest. The tests are not hard and cover exactly what is discussed in lecture. You can also earn bonus points by logging into lectures at the scheduled times. Very engaging and an easy A if you do the work.

analysis.name: Erica Cizsek
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: They are such an amazing professor! Super kind and welcoming. They provide super insightful lectures as well. Genuinely learned so much but in a fun and interactive way. Would 100% take again. There are exams and a good amount of writing assignments but they're pretty simple! Attendance is not required 100% of the time, but often.

Cizsek is the sweetest; you can tell they care about their students and teaching the material. This class wasn't difficult at all either. Def don't hesitate to take this class if Cizsek is still the professor!

Although I ended with a C (totally on me because I completely missed a quiz), Professor Cizsek had such great lectures that really helped with understanding the field of advertising and it was a really easy class

Love love loved this class. Super easy with fun lectures and collaborative discussions. Dr.Cizek is clearly passionate about their profession and does their best to ensure their students are being educated about important current issues. Lots of extra credit and exams were stress free with no final
MY FAVORITE TEACHER AT UT!!!! Genuinely cares about her students and the material. Great and engaging lecture! Take her class, you will not regret it!!! Loved every minute of her lectures!

analysis.name: Circe Sturm
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Sturm is clearly knowledgeable in her subject. But, she needs to explain things slower and more interestingly, keeping in mind that it's an online class and people can't reach her as easily. She tries to keep people in the loop by engaging in group chats and instapolls. The quizzes are easy.

This is a great course. Dr. Sturm is very organized, and the TAs are helpful. You'll need to study for the three midterms, and there's a project too. Keep up with Instapolls, and you can easily earn an A. The only reason I didn't earn an A is because of the midterms, so watch out!

Lectures are boring --- she just talks in circles and TA's are pretty bad (lacking basic canvas skills). Class is easy, all online prerecorded lectures with occasional instapolls. One project with a 2 page paper. There is extra credit opportunities (~2 points on final grade). Overall --- good class if you just need the credit and an easy A.

Dr. Strum talks in circles, her lectures tend to be boring and not coherent. They also used recycled lecture segments from a previous semester which was frankly negligent. This class is very content heavy, so only take it if you absolutely need it. One of her textbooks is completely irrelevant to the content of the class, which was vexing.

Professor Sturm is really nice and takes the time to explain vague concepts thoroughly which shows how genuinely interested she is in her field of work. There isn't too much work in the class right now and you basically only have to keep up with readings. Tests are manageable, but not as easy as you'd expect them to be. All multiple choice tests.

analysis.name: Cindy McCreery
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I promise you need to take this class! It's so fun and interesting! She's very helpful with all your work and always open for questions. She cares so much about all her students and if you just do your work which is pretty easy you will get an A. It's literally impossible to not unless you just don't do the work!

Ask questions anytime Cindy is super chill and is always available and gets back to you, I've never had a teacher/professor care this much about their students :) the work is super easy and fun and it really helped me for my future of wanting to be a writer especially TV writing if that interests you!
This is a great class if you love to write and be creative! This class 100% made me a better writer! Cindy is the NICEST women you will ever meet.
Although there's a lot of participation I feel like this class really created a community for RTF majors and I'm thankful for this class:)

Cindy is a very nice person but there were many things that made the class frustrating. The class was disorganized and assignments could be confusing at times. I felt I was teaching myself most of the time and had to learn how to do something in the span of a week. Also, we don't know what our grades are two weeks before the end of the semester.

analysis.name: Mirela Ciperiani
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Condescending professor. She was/is a mathematical prodigy without humbleness and this didn't translate to excellent teaching. HARSH grader on exams but HW's are always full credit with little feedback. I walked out of the class with a 100 on the final, an A, and a lot of resentment for making algebra not fun. Just save yourself and take Keel.

Lectures are unbelievably dry and suck the life out of the subject that is group theory. Pretty much follows the definition->theorem->proof cycle you would find in any old textbook, except in lecture form. Provides essentially 0 intuition and is pretty much all about deduction and symbolic manipulation. Exam problems sampled from homeworks.

The HW is the exam with the caveat that she expects you to be perfect on the exams. Most of your grade comes from exams but she replaces one and also 2 out of the 11 HWs. Presentations of HW are a big part of this class so expect to present math. She is a phenomenal professor if you expect to take algebraic structures 2 with Sean.

Not the worst but also not great. The homeworks were long and while the tests were based on them, she chooses the hardest/trickiest problems from each assignment, and it feels like there's not enough time to finish the exams. She's not a great lecturer; I just read the textbook or watched YT videos since I got nothing from her lectures.

Super knowledgeable & gives you everything you need to do well. Homework is difficult but exams are pulled from the homework so it's clear what you need to know for exams & exams are easy as a result. Lectures are really informative without being overly dense. Overall a really solid choice for number theory.

analysis.name: Cinzia Russi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Awful professor. She's hysterical and confusing. Makes a fairly easy subject matter very difficult to understand. She also giggles when she gives you bad grades. I would never recommend her to anyone.

Textbook readings can be long. Quizzes were either very easy or very hard. You don't learn much Italian in the course; it's a regular course taught in 70% Italian. Very open to working with the class on what material is difficult and changing the course structure during the semester. Friendly professor, encourages participation.
Lang Truths, Myths, Mysteries was a very interesting class! We covered many different topics and had fun working together in class. Take this class for upper div LAH!

I actually took LAH 352E, Language Myths, Mysteries, and Truths. Great class. Work was straightforward. Class was mostly relaxed group discussion. Dr. Russi was great! Easy grader and class was really interesting. She was really funny and nice!
Very nice, knowledgeable and helpful. Not sure why some other students are whining. I had zero problems with her.

analysis.name: Jessica Ciarla
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great Professor!! Very Knowledgable!  Very fair, if something is unclear she does not penalize you for it. It's nice to hear about her personal experience in the fashion industry as she is very credible having years of experience in New York and owning her bridal shop in Austin. Makes class interesting with relevant fashion clips from youtube.

She understood you're new to the software and will give critiques and guidance if you ask. She doesn't bite. Grades pretty easily just do the work. Class takes a lot of time outside of hybrid meetings.

Very straight-forward classes. Lectures are usually always the same - her giving a powerpoint presentation, with some relevant video clips every few slides. It gets a little boring but she gives you everything you need for the test. VERY friendly and answers all questions. The only thing I didn't like was that class got repetitive.

One of the worst lecturers I have had at UT, un-engaging. Copies her powerpoint slides from the book and read them to us while standing in the same place. Assigns 5 point assignments in class which are a total waste of time. Constantly asks the class inane questions of obvious definitions.

analysis.name: Christian Claudel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The professor was pretty chill on many assignments, and his discussion times always provided help to work on the codes. I learned how to code in Python fairly easily in class and he was pretty helpful in office hours as well. Unfortunately, his exams shifted to in-person after our TA complained about the use of AI in assignments (excluding final).

The lectures were kinda boring but very helpful with homework and labs I would recommend watching them online at 2x speed. The tests switched from online to paper during the semester but they were still
Pretty easy. He went over the study guide the day before in class and I would recommend you go to that because it was very similar to the test.

Dr. Claudel is a very nice guy. It was my first time learning Python, but it was not as hard as I expected. He asked us for feedback on his lectures and how he could improve them. No attendance grade, but I would go to understand material and ask questions in person. Also it is helpful for the quizzes.

As someone who has never coded before, this class was my biggest nightmare. I learned nothing from it because the labs were so difficult that it felt like you had to have been coding for 3+ years to know what to do. Everything is basically open-note so you can get by if you need to, but I wanted to learn Python and ended up not being able to.

Dr. Claudel is a nice guy who does seem to care about his students and makes himself accessible in many ways, but he's not super great at teaching programming (Python, in my case) to people who have never done it before. The lab TAs were a godsend in this regard. Claudel is pretty funny and at least he made the lectures enjoyable.

analysis.name: Hemant Chhajwani
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Chhajwani is an outstanding, knowledgeable, and caring professor. He checks in during lectures to ensure everyone understands, is always available outside class, and his in-depth lectures thoroughly prepare you for exams. He's approachable, explains complex material clearly, and provides helpful Excel supplements. Highly recommend!

I'll tell you what, I had no business even getting a B- in this class. I'm a Sociology major who has barely any experience regarding business classes. Yet so long as you try, I promise you Hemant will help you every step of the way. He's there to help you learn, not to make you worried about your grade (just give it a lot of effort).

Professor Chhajwani might be the best professor at UT. His class is super interesting and very insightful if you are interested in real estate. The material is difficult, but he makes it easy to understand. He also grades leniently  and makes the class enjoyable with great guest speakers and case projects. Take him 1000% if you have the option.

Chhajwani is awesome. Very nice professor, and probably the best for FIN357. Lectures focus on exam-related topics, something not universal to all FIN prof. apparently. Reading textbook is mandatory for a good grade, in any FIN class. Occasional question days, where class does problems together. Cold-calling involved, he can be a bit hard on you.

Professor Chhajwani is terrific. I had him the first time he taught FIN 357 and I learned so much in his class which built a strong foundation for Finance (thanks to both the class and prof). 

Be ready to read the book, engage in lectures, and put in the effort. It won't be easy, but you will learn finance and set yourself up for future success!

analysis.name: John Clarke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: An utterly unpleasant man.  He has no quealms about treating you as though you don't deserve to be in the art history program.  So dictatorial that you wind up not being inspired enough to take anything away from what would otherwise be a compelling and useful class.

I enjoyed the subject matter and was very excited to give my own interpretation guided by the textbooks and readings. Unfortunately Clarke is the kind of professor who prefers that you regurgitate back to him exactly what he has written in his own books and anything that strays from that is considered highly subjective and wrong.

If you're taking this for a VAPA or upper division elective, do something else. He is rude and condescending, and makes little to no accommodations for ANY situation. His sensitive lecture topics (sex, gender, etc) were talked about as if they were a joke. If we didn't remember a specific thing from the reading he'd get angry and say we don't try.

Professor John Clarke teaches a performance work in his Modern American Art course that contains sexual assault, and he presented it without warning. When I emailed him that I was triggered by this piece, he asked me to tell him in person why it was triggering for me. I declined, and he put the piece on our midterm.

Clarke is such a sweet guy! Not the most tech savvy. Clear lectures that go right along with the exams. Exams aren't hard at all, just need to watch the lectures and memorize the pieces. I never did the readings and got 96+ on all exams. Also some small writing assignments, but they're easy 100s. Go to class to succeed. Would love to take again.

analysis.name: Chad Landis
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Chad Landis? More like DAD Landis. This guy was awesome. The material was presented in an interesting and engaging manner, making it a pleasure to show up to class everyday. Tests are fair and pertain to what you learn in class. Homework is optional, but helps you with quizzes and further understanding. I HIGHLY recommend my dad.

I struggled a lot in Statics, but Landis' grading scale really helped. A C was around a 65, so even low exam scores counted. The class isn't easy, but many still got A's and B's. He provides lots of past exams and quizzes. He seemed grumpy a lot times due to cheating scandals in our class and sending attendance codes.., but overall he's fair.

Take Landis! His class is very well organized & he provides all the material you need to succeed. dont take early semester warnings lightly-- falsely filling the attendance form is -5 pts off overall grade. exams are fair, study at least 4 most recent past exams and you'll be set. but expect to put a little more effort in for exam 3. quizzes are ez

THE GOATTT. As someone who barely passed eng physics 1, I learned so much from this class and did surprisingly well despite being worried. Loved this class so much I signed up for his solids class next semester, and super excited. The material is difficult sometimes, but he provides an ABUNDANCE of HWs, past quizzes, and past exams.

By far the best engineering professor at UT in my opinion. Very organized lectures, always guide students to fully understand the materials. Course contents are incredibly accessible outside of class; Past Exams, Quizzes, and Notes. 5 Weeks, 4 Midterms, 1 Final, 5% Attendance grade. Time challenging, but do a ton of practices, you will get the A.

analysis.name: Cameron  Cler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She had mediocre lectures and loved explaining random Chinese things wrong. Doesn't grade until finals week even though class ends in like October, and even then the grading feels arbitrary. Never gave out a single 100 on an assignment, mostly gives 85s-90s. Attendance is a grade, even if you have an exam that falls during class hours. Mid.

Loved this professor! Even though the class was late in the day, it always flew by because she made the material so engaging. The assignments were straightforward and manageable, and I still walked away learning so much valuable information. Would definitely recommend taking this class with her if you get the chance!

I took Cameron for MKT 174 and she is such an amazing lecturer. She's one of the nicest people I've met at UT, so if you need a 1 hour course take this one!! participation is crucial to passing, but she tries to make each class enjoyable! Loved her!
Very good professor. Explains everything very well, would recommend the class. Also provides very good feedback.

analysis.name: Alexandra Clark
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I loved Dr. Clark's lecturing style and I can say that I learned quite a lot from her! I love that she is passionate about what she teaches and stands for what she believes in. However, I will say that the 3 exams are quite tricky, as they are long free responses. There is a lot of content discussed and no study guide/vague ideas of what to expect.

Dr. Clark is very condescending - when people ask questions in class she acts frustrated and as if the answer should be the most obvious thing in the world. I went to office hours once (Friday 8 AM only) to go over a test and ask for advice and she complained that students "just want to be spoon fed". The TAs were much more helpful.

The 3 exams that make up the majority of your grade require lots of studying, but are doable. She may seem intimidating, but is incredibly engaging and refreshingly honest about her views on what's happening in the US right now in relation to the course content. I learned so much and highly recommend her as a professor.

Dr. Clark's class is very informative. I learned so much about dementia and Alzheimer's. The lectures can be science heavy but she does a great job of explaining it so you shouldn't feel lost. There are 4 free response quizzes that can be a bit tricky so make sure to study ahead. But as long as you put in the work it's totally doable.

I enjoyed Professor Clark's class and learned a lot, and she can answer any question. She does present a lot of information but the way she lectures makes it easier to remember. Quizzes are doable if you keep up with lecture material.

analysis.name: Kevin Clarno
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Clarno is a groovy guy. He is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. Concerning the class, if this is your first class on nuclear, it might be rough as there is a learning curve. Exams also are difficult but are graded on a curve so there is less pressure. Reason I am giving a four is because the class was too disorganized. Very swag beard.
Great guy, great class. Study with the slides... Tests are a challenge, but meant to stretch you

analysis.name: Gregory Clark
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I highly recommend taking this course for the UGS requirement. Dr. Clark is super cool and into what he is teaching. The course has some reading reflections, three essays, a group presentation, and an individual presentation. It is very interesting to learn about different plants and what they do. Compared to other UGS's this one is much better.

Dr. Clark is so chill and very understanding! He truly helps every student succeed in his lab, and he doesn't force anybody to do too much work each week! However, the partner system during first semester can get a little frustrating if you're stuck with a bad one, and he doesn't really use canvas, so it is hard to determine your grade!

Awesome professor. So nice and understanding, easy to talk to, cares about your learning while also making sure not to stress you out. His FRI stream is great and provides a great exposure to the basics of research.

Dr. Clark was absolutely amazing! His Hidden Treasures of Plants UGS was really eye-opening and a great learning experience. Discussions were very chill and essay assignments were not too much of a challenge. Dr. Clark was super understanding and spent time learning about his students. I enjoyed his class and learned a lot!

Dr. Clark is THE BEST! Such a sweet guy and is extremely passionate about his research! His lab is interesting but pretty laid back! Not work heavy and he's so forgiving and approachable! LOVE DR.CLARK AND HIS LAB!!!

analysis.name: Judith Coffin
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Although she is an interesting professor and some of her classes were exciting, she is quite a tough grader, at least in my experience. I did not receive an A on any assignment other than one, despite following the given guidelines exactly and spending over a week on every essay. Nice lady, but I wish she had given clearer instructions.

I LOVE COFFIN! She can be blunt but if you show up, participate, and put in some effort she rewards you with great feedback and funny moments. First half of class was just discussion, so be prepared to talk. The second half was a research project but Coffin splits it into small parts and takes the time to provide individual help. Would do it again!

I love Dr. Coffin this my second semester with her now and she just gets better. She truly cares for her students (extra if u put in the work and participate in class) she helped me both in and out of class. She might be blunt sometimes but she knows what she's talking about knows you do too, truly such a great lady, I have so much respect for her.

Dr. Coffin was wonderful and probably one of the most interesting professors I've ever had. As long as you truly read the material, which is all intriguing, you will want to participate in the conversations had in class. The second half is focused on a research topic of your choosing, with a lot of guidance.

Coffin was my rudest teacher this semester. She belittled zoom students and openly stated that she cared less for them. This class is open for students as a culture credit class, DON'T take it. No electronics allowed in person, extremely book heavy, so few grades. There are three papers, each assignment is vague and she doesn't explain them well.

analysis.name: Shirley Cohen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is genuinely so sweet and caring, wants everyone to feel caught up and prepared. First half of semester is one project, second half is the second, and every week there is a quiz that is easy if you do the one chapter of reading. Totally manageable, especially for an upper divison CS
The course isn't too difficult, but be prepared to receive vague feedback and lose points—even if you repeatedly request basic feedback, success is unlikely.

One midterm. iClicker quizzes every class on readings (beware, your quiz grade will have a bigger affect on your grade than youd think). Building on same PARTNER project throughout whole semester, + final presentation. Pay attention to demos in class to make your weekly assignments go more smoothly. Nice woman, very understanding & willing to help

Ok professor. Lectures were kinda slow and unengaging, but the students didn't really help with participating either. Did fine, but midterm was harder than expected and didn't really reflect what we did on the project milestones. Project required a lot of self-learning. Overall, I felt like I didn't get much from the class, but it wasn't the worst.

I really do not like this teacher She made me miserable in life as soon as I started studying with her I will never study with her for sure again. Great class if you want a super vague understanding of Google Cloud Platform. Horrible class if you want to learn SQL. Prof talks SLOW slow- hard to concentrate. Mandatory lectures. Not too difficult.

analysis.name: Courtney Handman
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Would give a 0 if possible. Only one test which is the final and is worth 30% of your grade. Study guide is not helpful and only has the exact same information as the syllabus. Worthless. Seems like she changed the class starting this semester. So buyer beware. If you are thinking about unaIiving yourself then this is the PERFECT class for you!

I cannot hear her in her big lecture hall, so it was hard to stay engaged. Readings are unnecessarily long, and final is almost NOTHING like what was being done in the course. There are so many questions you may answer about the readings in the weekly quizzes that you will never see again. Just hope and pray you remember the readings in the final.

Prof. Handman was a very passionate and nice professor, but the class is super reading-heavy, and the assigned reading material was often very dense. The TAs were nice and good at explaining material, but the grading criteria were unclear and nearly abstract. I had to study and work quite hard in this class to get an A, so be aware.

This is a required course for stem majors, and the AMOUNT of work you have to do for AN ELECTIVE class is absurd. A reading every class that is AT THE MINIMUM 15 pages long and then a quiz EVERY week, with a max grade of a 95 is insane. Final test was also horrible, they give you over 15 readings and "only" test your knowledge on SEVEN of them.

Honestly some of the reviews for this class seem like an over exaggeration to me. It can be difficult but it's not that bad, even if you don't do all the readings just pay attention to lectures. Ended up being a lot easier than the reviews on here make it seem! Final is hard ish just attend review and study a little not that bad

analysis.name: Desmond Coles
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data
